body.text:
udayananirākaraṇam
prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text:
Refutation of <s>Udayana</s>
First Chapter

body.text: om namastārāyai |
body.translated_text: Oṃ. Salutation to <s>Tārā</s>.

body.text:
vijñāyante svavacanasaraṇiṃ ramaṇīyatamāṃ guṇigaṇāvaśiṣṭām
udayanavacanāt svavacana-[caraṇa]hatisaraṇiṃ bhaṇiṣyāmi |
body.translated_text: Having understood the most delightful path of one's own words, [a path] remaining beyond the multitudes of the meritorious, I shall declare, taking from the words of <s>Udayana</s>, the path [trodden by] the footsteps of my own words.

body.text: iha khalu viśālaśailamekhalāsthūlasthāṇusthānīye (2) parasya (jñāna prasūtapṛṣṭha) śrīmat jñānaśrīmitrapādīyamuktasāmarthyāsāmarthyātprasphuṭita upaśaṅkātaḥ sāmarthyāsāmarthyaviruddhadharmasaṃsargeṇa bhedasiddhau tatsiddhiriti sattvādiṣupareṇaśleṣitaṃ kliśyate |
body.translated_text: Now here, against the opponent [who is] like a firm post girded by vast mountain ranges, from the capacity and incapacity manifest in the venerable <s>Jñānaśrīmitra</s>'s [work], born from [his] knowledge — when the proof of difference [is attempted] through the conjunction of contradictory properties of capacity and incapacity, that proof [fails]; and [the opponent's argument], interlocked with [the properties of] <s>sattva</s> (existence) and the rest by the other [party], is tormented.

body.text: avikalena hi sakaladūṣyakeṇa (3) hi pālanā pratyakṣataḥ pṛthvīpavanapāśraḥ pratyarthivījāni parasparopasarpaṇasampūrṇapratyayapratyarjitasannidhānāni tadudbhūtasvādhīnavarddhiṣṇutādiguṇaramaṇīyapariṇatyā pravardhante (4) prarohaṃ pratipratyayabhāvajānya [bhāvajāni]prabhāvyante | yathoktaviśeṣaṇapratyayatvameṣāṃ pratyātmapratiṣṭhādhiṣṭhitasauṣṭhavapṛṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhasambhavānvayavyatirekapa (5) rikalpanā tasyā upalālitasakalitasahakārisākalyaviśeṣaṇasārupyamavasthāpanīyamaparathā pratyayāntarapratyāsattisāpekṣatve bījasyeva kramayau (6) gapadyaviśeṣasauṣṭhavasphuṭitamupādhāvagrimakṣaṇasyāpi sahakārisākalyāsākalyāvasthayoḥ sthitāsthitatayā prarohaṃ prati pratyetuṃ pāryeta | tathā ca kuśūlakukṣikuṇḍalitakṣaṇā (7) dhikatcāt sahakārikṣaṇakrameṇa kedārākrāntakalevaraṃ kadambakamekamanekambeti vistarata vicāracakramapakramante | kiṃ cet na tayo ka (8) thitamidamuttānīkrameṇa sahakārisahacaritapratyayapratyāsattibhrāntasvabhāvāntaramintyupakṣipya pakṣapratipakṣapa- rijighṛkṣākṣāntahṛdayā sādhakamidamiti jñāpakavirodhe vyāharanti |
body.translated_text: For by complete [cognition] of all the objects to be refuted, the protection [of one's thesis] is [secured] through perception. The seeds of the opponent, [like seeds] supported by earth, wind, etc., having their proximity mutually approached with fully matured cognition, grow through the delightful transformation of such qualities as self-dependent growth arising from them, and produce sprouts — [these] effects are to be produced [from] each cognition. The fact that they have the particular cognitions described is [established through] the contrivance of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), based on the perception possible through the excellence resting on each self-established [factor]; and the conformity of that [cognition] with the totality of the particular cooperative conditions (<s>sahakāri</s>) that have been gathered and nurtured must be established; otherwise, when there is dependence on the proximity of another cognition, then — just as for a seed — owing to the excellence of [its] beauty which manifests whether simultaneously or sequentially, even for the first moment of [germination], in the states of presence and absence of the totality of cooperative conditions, it could be accepted as a cause for the sprout by virtue of being established or not established. And so, the investigative wheel proceeds in detail: does the seed, with its body expanded across the field, [arise] from the sequence of moments of cooperative conditions — [starting] from the moment concealed, curled up in the belly of the granary — as one mass or many? But [they say:] if this were not stated by them in a straightforward manner, then, having introduced another nature confused by the proximity of the cognition accompanied by cooperative conditions, those whose hearts are impatient in their desire to grasp thesis and counter-thesis declare: 'This is the proof' — [thus they speak] in contradiction to the indicator.

body.text: jighṛkṣāsāmarthyasamarthanādau sākṣādvayavahatuṃ tattadā tatkarotyādi tatkarotyeva vā yathā (2) ca yasya nehaḥ sandohaniḥ sandehapariṇatau praṇatidehotkṛṣṭaḥ yathāprakāśitasādhanātattvaprasādhanaśca kevalopi kṣaṇatvapadārthaḥ na ca kevalastathābhū (3) to 'pi karotyapīti karotyeveti vā pratyākalitaḥ sa eṣa prasaṅgaprasaṅgato viparyayaḥ pūrvāparakālamilitakaraṇākaraṇayorādhārabhedañca saṃdīpayati | tathāhi (4) paryavasāne janakatvamabhimatakārye paryālocitaṃ pramāṇena pratyekamavasthitam |
body.translated_text: In establishing the capacity for the desire to grasp, one directly employs [terms like] 'that produces' or 'that alone produces.' And for one whose doubt has matured into the dissolution of doubt — the person of elevated prostration — and who is a prover of the true nature of the means of proof as illuminated, even a mere entity of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇatva</s>) — and a mere [entity] of such nature does not produce, or [is it that] it does indeed produce — [when] thus reflected upon, this reversal arising incidentally from incidental [arguments] illuminates the difference of basis between production and non-production conjoined in earlier and later times. For thus, at the conclusion, the producer-hood has been examined by the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), established individually.

body.text: anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ dharādhāmādisākalyaṃ ślathayitvā viśeṣaṇaṃ parāparabhāvabhaṅgayā svaviśeṣavyāptamālocyanimatyantāyogavyavacchedāyogavyavacchedacchadicchannamunnīyate -
body.translated_text: Having loosened the totality of the basis of earth and the rest through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), and having considered that the qualifier, pervaded by its own particular through the dissolution of the relation of prior and posterior, [reaches its] unwanted consequence of absolute disconnection — the conclusion of absolute non-connection — is unveiled, covered as it was:

children.translated_text: For a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) without particulars
would be like a hare's horn; agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) without qualification would be like a barren woman's son.

body.text: tasmādasmatpratibhāvarṇabhāvasthāpratibhāsaprabhāvāt bhāvānāṃ kintatraiva tathā (7) bhadantaiḥ paramaparāparasadṛśatā ca svabhāvāntarānubhavitaikapratisantānaṃ bandhyatvamakartṛtvaṃ keśakuntalakamalakāṇḍāt svaravatsaṃvedanīyam | tat(8) tapanādisahacarabhedasampāditatattadādibhedo darśyatāṃ pūrvāparāvasthā pāramārthikā bhedajñā pratyabhijñā paramaviśvāsasarvasvaṃ bibhrati bhramimūrṣaṇīyeti | pakṣa dva-(9) yānugrahanigrahe hetuḥ hetubhāva eva bhāvanāṃ saṃdūṣyate bhavyena | tathāhi, tatkartṛtvaṃ pareṣu madhyasthamiva vādiprativādisammatabilambakāritvāt sapakṣāditvaviśeṣasiddhiviśleṣe 'pi suśleṣakauśalabalābalambīvānumatamubhayabhūmibhāginorapi bhāvato bhūtoktipravṛttayostathābhūtañca bhāvyamānaṃ kartṛtvarūpaṃ kiṃ tattvato 'tyantāyogavyavacchinnanirvartmathābhūtañca bhāvyamānaṃ kartṛtvarūpaṃ kiṃ tattvato 'tyantāyogavyavacchinnanirvartmakartṛtvarūpamucchavibhramabhūmi - bhūtānubhavavyavasthānamanavasthitamapi anumanyate mānyena anyena vā prakāreṇa yadutāyogavyavacchinnakartṛ -(3) -tvarūpamutkīrtayitavyam, vyapetānubhavādivyavasthamapi svasthayaḥ sthaviravādivṛndavṛndārakānantarakathitapakṣayoranyatarāṅgokārakārāgāragraheṇa | arthagṛ(4)hītau-paryāyato dvāvapi dvāparadvārālaṅkṛtau kathaya ko 'tra nistrāṇamāpadyate avadyaprabheda iti ceducyate | ayameva prasaṅgaḥ yaduta yadyadā (5) yatsamarthavyavasthānasthānaṃ tattadā tatkarotyapi yathā sāmagryavasthāyāṃ vikalakālakalāyāmapi pūrvādikāyāmakathitasāmarthyavyavasthānaṃ sthānañca (6) kāñcanakāryamaryādāmādāya darśito bhāvabhedaḥ ityantāyogavyavacchedakartṛtvapakṣe lakṣayitavyaḥ prasaṅgaḥ | na ca kadācidapi vedyate niḥsahacarasa (7) hakāricakraḥ prakramamāṇaḥ kartu matyantāyogavyavacchedena abhimato bhāvaḥ svakāryamityāvarjanīyo viparyayaścātra | tathāpi syāt anekāntaśāntāvanamutthitāyāmabhitticitrakarmmapratimamidamābhāti | tathāhi sāmarthyavyavahārayogyatvepi prasaṅgasādhane kīddaśarktṛtvapravartitaśaktavyavasthānamākṣepamakṣe-(p. 5)-pakāritvavasya prasādhakapramāṇaprasthāpanārthatvāt | sahakārisākalye satyeva karotīti vilambakāritvalakṣaṇaśca kevalāvasthāyāṃ prasajjayitumaśakyatvāt | sahakā-(2) risākalye sati karotyevetyevaṃ svabhāvakartutvakīrtane 'kīrtiḥ karitalabilambitaiva sthiviravādānukulatvātkukṣitvādasya pakṣasya hantanitāntanirmalaiḥ subhāṣitabhānubhiranunnameva pareṣāṃ mohatamaḥ | yadevaṃ sākalyaṃ sahakārikalpaṃ bījakartṛtvaviśeṣaṇaṃ prakṣipya parapakṣaḥ kṣubhyate 'kṣepakāritvamapi tadviśe(4) ṣarūpaṃ pramāṇaprasiddhaṃ anurudhya bādhyate sādhuḥ yasmādakṣepakāritvānapekṣakāritvaṃ kartṛtvasāmānyasyāntyāvasthāyāṃ pratyakṣānupalambhasambhāvita (5) sya vyaktiprabhedatayā vyāpakaṃ sambhāvya prakārāntarāpratīteranakṣepakartṛtvarūpaṃ kartṛtvasāmānyasya pariṇāmamanumanyase prasaṅgasaṅgatau (6) nāṅgatā saṅgacchate doṣasya | tathāhi hetusāhitye 'pi bījasya kartṛtvaṃ dṛśyamānaṃ na sāhityena viśeṣaṇīyaṃ śilāśakalāderapi tathātvaprāpteḥ apitu kevalyai (7) va bījasya pratyekamavasthitaṃ anvayavyatirekayoravagamena pāṣāṇakulasya sāhityabahirbhāvabhajanāt | pratyekatvañca na ca viśiṣyamāṇaṃ kartṛtvaṃ bīja-(8)-sya pratyekatvābhāvasvabhāvo 'pratyekarūpaḥ sahakāricakrasaṃparkaḥ kathaṃ viśeṣaṃ śaknuyāt nahi cakṣurnāsti tena ca viśiṣṭamiti śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ pakṣaḥ | athāpi pra (9) tyekatvasya sāhitye pratyekamanvayādergṛhītau nāpratyekatvena viśiṣyata taduttarakālaṃ punarviśeṣaṇīyaṃ etāvanti sahakārīṇi sahitāni hi tā ni kāryāyeti pāṭhāntara aparahastena sāmagrīmīhamāno mānocitastāmevādatte sāmagrīpāṣāṇatalākīrṇāmapīti cet n akāraṇavikalpakatvādeva nopādīyate (2) kāryārthinā śilāśakalādiko bhāvaḥ | kintayā viśiṣya karaṇīyaṃ yadā tu viśeṣaṇametādṛśaṃ apasāritam | atha tadānīṃ avaśiṣyamāṇaṃ brīhikalevaraṃ kāraṇatvena niṣṭaṅkitena (3) atyantāyogavyacchedānumitau kevalamapi kadācitkarotu sāmagrīsamavagraha kāla iti prasaṅgasaṅkīrṇavataḥ prathano manorathonmatho 'yaṃ prārthitodoṣaḥ prārthitaḥ (4) tadayuktam -
body.translated_text: Therefore, from the power of the manifestation of states appearing as descriptive impressions of our own cognition — regarding entities, what [is the case] therein? The Venerable Ones [hold that] the supreme similarity between remote and proximate [states], and the barrenness and non-agency of a single continuum in which another nature has been experienced, are to be ascertained from hair, locks, lotus, and stalk by their own characteristics. Let [the opponent] demonstrate the differentiation produced by the distinction of attendant [conditions] such as heat etc.; the prior and posterior states as ultimately real; the recognitive cognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) that is the awareness of difference, bearing the full conviction of trust — for it appears that this should be shaken with the dizziness [of doubt]. The reason for supporting or refuting both positions — the very reason-nature — is vitiated by the discerning [opponent] among entities. For thus: the agency of that [entity] with respect to others, standing as if neutral — because of its delay-causing nature (<s>vilambakāritva</s>) agreed upon by both proponent and opponent — even when there is separation from the establishment of the particular distinction of being a <s>sapakṣa</s> (positive instance) etc., like one who relies on the strength of skillful connection, approved by both parties who share in both grounds, whose engagements proceed from true descriptions — and the form of agency being thus contemplated: is it, in its ultimate nature, of the form of agency delimited by absolute non-connection (<s>atyantāyogavyavacchinna</s>) [with the effect before conditions are met]? Or being contemplated as unreal, is that form of agency — which is the ground of the illusion of upsurge, the experiential basis of states that are not established — even if unstable, accepted by the honored one or by another in some other manner? That is to say: the form of agency delimited by non-connection is to be proclaimed, even though devoid of the arrangement of experience etc., by one well-established in his view, through grasping one of the two positions spoken of by the venerable Elders and their circle in immediate succession, as if confined in the prison of assent. When both [debaters], adorned at the gateway of the <s>dvāpara</s> [of debate], have grasped the meaning in turn — say, who here obtains freedom? If it is said that this is a classification of faults, then it is replied: This itself is the contingency (<s>prasaṅga</s>) — namely, whatever and whenever has its capacity-establishment standing in a certain locus, that and then produces its effect as well, just as in the state of the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>), even in a time deficient in parts, in the prior and other states, the previously unstated capacity-establishment and locus has been shown as the differentiation of entities, taking as its boundary the standard of effect-production — this contingency is to be noted in the position of agency delimited by absolute non-connection. And never at all is the entity intended to have agency delimited by absolute non-connection perceived proceeding to produce its own effect as a wheel of co-agents without companions — and the reversal too is unavoidable here. Even so, it may be [objected]: when non-one-sidedness (<s>anekānta</s>) has been pacified and arisen [again], this appears like a painting on a non-wall. For thus: even when fitness for conventional usage of causal capacity is admitted, in establishing the contingency — since it serves to dispatch the establishing evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for the challenged agency-initiated power-arrangement; and since the feature characterized as delay-causing agency — namely 'it produces only when the totality of auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakāri</s>) is present' — cannot be contingently applied in the state of the sole [unconditioned] cause; and since in proclaiming the own-nature agency — 'it produces indeed when the totality of auxiliary conditions is present' — the fame rests delayed upon the agent, and because of its agreeableness with the Elder tradition and because of the hollowness of this position — surely, by the thoroughly pure sun-rays of well-spoken words, the darkness of delusion of opponents remains ever unbowed. If thus the completeness of the auxiliary conditions is introduced as a qualification of the seed's particular agency, the opponent's position is disturbed; and even the non-delay-causing nature (<s>akṣepakāritva</s>), being that particular form well-established by evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>), is respected and [yet] refuted. The worthy [opponent argues]: since the non-delay-causing nature — causation without dependence on conditions — being a particular instance of agency in general, in the final state, which is possible through direct non-apprehension (<s>pratyakṣānupalambha</s>), by regarding it as pervading in the form of particular instances, and because of the non-perception of any other manner — you accept the non-delay-causing form of agency as the culmination of agency in general; yet in the alignment of the contingency argument, the defect does not fit in. For thus: even when the seed's agency is observed in conjunction with auxiliary conditions, it should not be qualified by that conjunction — since stones and the like too would attain the same status. Rather, the individual [capacity] alone of the seed, ascertained in each case through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), [is the cause] — since the stone family is excluded from that conjunction. And the individual [capacity being] such, the agency of the seed being qualified — its contact with the wheel of auxiliary conditions, which is by nature devoid of individual [causal capacity] and is of a non-individual form, how could it specify [the seed's agency]? For it is not an accepted position of the learned that 'the eye does not exist, yet through it something is qualified.' And even if the individual nature [of the seed] is grasped individually within the conjunction, it is not qualified by non-individuality; thereafter, [if one says] it should be further qualified as 'these many auxiliary conditions together produce that effect' — [this amounts to] a variant reading; striving for the aggregate by the other hand, one accustomed to pride takes up that very aggregate strewn upon the stone-surface [of false assumptions]. [Reply:] Precisely because [the stone etc.] does not have the nature of being a differentiating cause, it is not adopted by one seeking an effect — the entity such as a stone fragment etc. 'What then is to be done by qualifying it?' When such a qualifier has been removed, then the remaining rice-grain body, being stamped as a cause in the inference of [agency] delimited by absolute non-connection, [one might say] 'let it even singly sometimes produce, at the time of aggregate-comprehension' — this is the fancy of one infected by the contingency argument, this is the disturbance of fantasy, this sought-after fault has been sought. That is improper—

body.text: sāmarthya hi kṛtiḥ yogyatā vā? nādyaḥ sādhyāviśiṣṭatvaprasaṅgāt | nāpi dvitīyaḥ sā hi sahakārisākalyaṃ yā | pratisvikī vā, nādyaḥ siddhasādhanatvāt, parānabhyupagamena (5) hetvasiddhiśca yatsahakārisamavadhānavattaddhi karotyeveti ko nāma nābhyupaiti yamuddaśya | sādhyate, na cākaraṇakāle sahakārisamavadhānavanto 'smānabhyupeyate (6) yataḥ prasaṅga pravarteta | prātisvikī tu yogyatā anvayavyatirekaviṣayībhūtaṃ bījatvaṃ vā syāt tadavāntarajātibhedo vā | sahakārivaikalyaprayuktakāryābhāvavatvaṃ vā | nādyaḥ (7) akurvvatopi bījajātīyasya pratyakṣasiddhatvāt | tavāpi tatrāvipratipatteḥ | netaraḥ tasya kurvatyapi mayānabhyupagamena dṛṣṭāntasya sādhanavikalatvāt | ko hi nāma susthātmā (8) pramāṇaśūnyamabhyupagacchet | sa hi na pratyakṣeṇa anubhūyate tathānavasāyāt | nāpyanumānena liṅgābhāvāt | yadi na kaścidviśeṣa, kathaṃ tarhi karaṇākaraṇe cet (9) ka evamāha neti | kiṃ jāti bhedarūpaḥ sahakārilābhālābharūpo veti niyāmakaṃ pramāṇamanusaranto na paśyāmaḥ tathāpi yo 'yaṃ sahakārimadhyamadhyāsī no ḥkṣepakaraṇasvabhāvo bhāvaḥ sa yadi prāgapyāsīt tadā prasahya kārya kurvāṇo gīrvāṇaśāpaśatenāpyapahastayituṃ na śakyate, iti cetḥ | yuktametat yadyakṣepakaraṇasvabhāvatvaṃ bhāvasya pramāṇagocaraḥ syāt kutaḥ tatsiddhamiti cet na vidbhaḥ | prasaṃga tadviparyayāmyāṃ tatsiddhiriti ce na, parasparāśrayaprasaṅgāt | evaṃ svabhāvatvasiddhau hi tayo pravṛttistat pravṛttau ca caivaṃ svabhāvatvasiddhiriti |
body.translated_text: Is causal capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) action (<s>kṛti</s>) or fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>)? Not the first, because of the contingency of non-distinction from what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>). Nor the second; for that [fitness] is either the totality of auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakārisākalya</s>), or individual [fitness]. Not the first, because of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>); and there is the unestablishedness of the reason (<s>hetvāsiddhi</s>) due to the opponent's non-acceptance — for who indeed does not accept that 'whatever possesses the concurrence of auxiliary conditions indeed produces' — [the very thesis] with reference to which [the proof] is undertaken? It is to be proved; and it is not accepted by us that [entities] possessing the concurrence of auxiliary conditions exist at the time of non-production, from which the contingency would follow. But the individual fitness — is it seed-nature (<s>bījatva</s>) that has become the object of positive and negative concomitance? Or a subdivision of that kind (<s>jāti</s>)? Or the property of having absence of effect occasioned by the deficiency of auxiliary conditions? Not the first, because seed-type entities are established by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) even when not producing — and there is no dispute from your side either on this. Not the other [i.e., the sub-kind], because the example is deficient in proof, since I do not accept that [sub-kind] even when [the seed] produces; for who in their right mind would accept [something] devoid of evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>)? For that is not experienced through perception, since there is no such ascertainment; nor through inference (<s>anumāna</s>), because of the absence of a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>). 'If there is no distinction whatsoever, then how is there production and non-production?' If [asked], who says 'no'? Whether [the distinction] is in the form of a kind-difference or in the form of the gain and loss of auxiliary conditions — following the determining evidence, we do not see. Nevertheless, this entity which sits in the midst of auxiliary conditions and whose nature is non-delay-causing production — if it existed previously too, then, forcibly producing its effect, it cannot be pushed aside even by a hundred curses of the gods. If [you say] thus — this is reasonable if the non-delay-producing nature of the entity were within the range of evidence. If asked: from what is that established? — [the wise] do not know. If [one says] its establishment is through the contingency argument and its reverse — no, because of the contingency of mutual dependence (<s>parasparāśraya</s>). For the engagement of those two [arguments] depends on the establishment of such a nature, and the establishment of such a nature depends on their engagement.

body.text: ḥsyādetata kāryajanmaivāsminnarthai pramāṇaṃ vilambakārisvabhāvānuvṛttau kāryānutpatti sarvadeti cet |ḥ na, bilambakārisvabhāvasya sarvadaivākaraṇe (4) tattvavyāghātāt | tataśca bilambakārītyasya yāvatsahakāryasannidhānaṃ tāvanna karotītyarthaḥ | evaṃ ca kāryajanmasāmagryāṃ pramāṇayituṃ na śakyate na tu jātibhede | te tu kiṃ (5) yathānubhavaṃ parasparasāpekṣā vilambakāritvabhāvāḥ parasparaṃ pratyāsannāḥ kārya kṛtavantaḥ kiṃ vā yathātvaparikalpane kṣiprakārisvabhāvā inyatra (6)kāryopajananamajāgarūkameveti |
body.translated_text: It may be [objected]: the birth of the effect (<s>kāryajanma</s>) itself is the evidence for this meaning — when the delay-causing nature continues, the effect is never produced — if so, [the reply is:] no, because if the delay-causing nature were to never produce at all, that would contradict its very nature (<s>tattvavyāghāta</s>). And thus 'delay-causing' (<s>vilambakārin</s>) means: it does not produce so long as the auxiliary conditions are not present — this is the meaning. And thus the birth of the effect can serve as evidence for the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>), but not for a kind-difference (<s>jātibheda</s>). But are those [entities], as experienced, mutually dependent delay-causing beings that, having come near to each other, have produced the effect? Or, in attributing to them their true nature as quick-acting by nature (<s>kṣiprakārisvabhāva</s>), is the non-production of the effect elsewhere simply their being heedless?

body.text: nāpi tṛtīyaḥ, virodhāt sahakāryabhāvaprayuktakāryābhāvavāṃśca sahakārivirahe kāryāvāṃśceti vyāhatam | (7) tasmād yadyadabhāva eva yanna karoti tattadabhāva tatkarotyeti syāt | etacca sthairyasiddhereva paraṃ bījasarvasvamiti etena samarthavyavahāraocarattvaṃ heturiti nirastam | tādṛgvyavahāra(8) gocarasyāpi bījasyāṃkurākaraṇadarśanāt | nāsau mukhyastatravyavahāraḥ | tasya janananimittatvāt | ḥanyathātvaniyamaprasaṅgāditi ceti, na, kīdṛśaṃ punarjana (9) naṃ mukhyasamarthavyavahāranimittam | na tāvadākṣepakaraṇaṃ nimittaṃ tasyāsiddheḥ | niyamasya ca sahakārādisākalye satyeva karaṇaṃ karaṇameveti ye evaṃ svabhāvatvenāpyu-patteḥ | tataśca janananimitta evāyaṃ vyavahāro na ca vyāptisiddhiriti |ḥ
body.translated_text: Nor the third [alternative], because of contradiction: one who [says] the absence of the effect is caused by the absence of the cooperative condition, and [also says] the [seed] is capable of the effect in the absence of the cooperative condition — these are contradictory. Therefore, whatever does not produce when it alone is absent — that, when it alone is absent, [would] produce — this would follow. And this is the entire substance of the argument for the proof of permanence. By this, the [proposed] reason 'being within the range of the convention of capacity' is refuted — because even a seed that falls within the range of such a convention is seen not to produce a sprout. 'That convention is not primary [i.e., literal]' [they say]. [We reply:] because it is based on the occasion of generation. 'Otherwise there would be the unwanted consequence of non-restriction' — [they say], but no. What kind of generation, then, is the occasion for the primary convention of capacity? Not the [mere] fact of being a contributing cause (<s>ākṣepakāraṇa</s>) — because that is unestablished. And the restriction [of production] only when there is a totality of cooperative conditions — [if one says] 'production is just production' — this too is established through its own nature. Therefore, this convention is based precisely on the occasion of generation, and there is no proof of the [universal] concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>).

kaḥ svabhāvaḥ samarthito bhavati | nahi pakṣavipakṣābhyāmanyaḥ prakāro 'stīti cet na dūṣaṇābhidhānasamaye niścayābhāvenaiva sandigdhāsiddhinirvāhe kathāpūrvarūpaparya (8) vasānādityanena | ḥ prasaṅgasādhanaṃ parāmyupagamena vā saṃbhāvyamānatayā vā prakārāntarābhāvāt prastūyate | tatra sandigdhāsiddhatvamuktvā dūṣaṇameva mayaiva nābhyupagatamiti cet taccintyatāṃ kartṛtvamanumanyase tāvad tacca yāvat pūrvasthitameva pratyabhijñāśritya ityāśrayobījātmakaṃ yatkāryamavyapekṣakamanvayavyatirekāsāmarthyāvasthita(2) tathābhāvaṃ tāvadatyantāyogavyavacchedanakartṛtvarupaṃ sambhāvitaṃ tato 'dhiṣṭhitaṃ bhāge 'vinirbhāgabhāvinaṃ bhāvato bhāṣyate tadeva bījaṃ pūrvamapyāsīditi (4) tadākṣepakāritvakṣaṇajananajanitasamarthavyavahārayogyatvaṃ prasaṅgasādhanaṃ kathaṃ saṃdigdhāsiddhyā vidhūnanīyaṃ iti na prativādisamāśritottarapakṣapratānakathāpū (5) rvvabhāgaḥ svarūpabhaṅgamanaṅgīkṛtyāstīti vyastamakhiladoṣodbhāvananigrahādhikaraṇaprasaṅgavat | ubhayamapi akṣepakāritvānapekṣakāritvamanullikhyai (6) va bījaṃ kevalaṃ sahakārimadhye 'pyavasitakartṛbhāvaṃ prāgapi kurvan tathābhūtamiti bhāvato bhāṣasva susadhisādhibādhanam | [samādhimādhibādhanam ]
body.translated_text: He whose fame in proclaiming the glory of the dancer of the city-stage of the three worlds, where [feminine] persons dance, whose extreme sharpness in splitting open the mass of exceedingly harsh and prominent tortoise-shell-back ridges of the aged tortoise is enriched by the most formidable intellectual acuity — what more need be said in this connection? By this argument of absolute disconnection, having placed in the foreground the transformation of the universal of agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) itself, the acceptance by the clever speaker [of the opponent's position], begun without refuge, [goes] thus: 'Whatever, whenever, falls within the range of the convention of capacity to produce that, that indeed produces that at that time' — just as at the final stage, even at a prior separate stage, the seed was ascertained to be of such a nature, with the rapidity of being unconquered by non-seed. And the reflection on the reversal 'it does not [merely] produce' must be accomplished by the skilled one through inner production, [an argument] thundering within. Thus, the seed, having turned away from non-seed, being determined in its agency through the universal of agency (<s>kartṛtvasāmānya</s>) ascertained as the effect through positive and negative concomitance initiated by the perception of properties and non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), having the capacity of contributing and non-contributing generation produced by momentary generation — that fitness for the convention of capacity is both the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) and that which is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>). Here, the two types of agency — 'it produces' or 'it necessarily produces' — by alternation, just as admitted by the opponent, are themselves also possible, because of the possibility of the universal not being pervaded by the particular, since it is not characterized by the rejection of both theses. Even considering both theses, this must be characterized thus — the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its reversal, undeflected, [stand firm] because even by a moment's worth of the group of refutations that are adorned with being the cause of the convention of capacity to produce whatever whenever — what is perceived [to have capacity], that, like a non-producer at that time, just as at the final stage, even at the prior separate stage, the seed is accepted as not having produced senescence. Thus, with a smooth single reflective cognition, by the wise person. And what has been transmitted, even when closely examined, is never [refuted] merely by production; in the state of [the seed's] being cast into the immovable belly [of the granary], not even the entirety of the ten directions, traversed by the argument for living beings, has established the producer-hood of each of these individually. Therefore there is no satisfaction; with the resolution through each one's own understanding of the totality, in acknowledging the service-to-others of the wise individual — the self-nature and non-self-nature, the counter-positive of absence, 'at that very time,' combined with 'there itself,' combined with both, combined with 'in that very way' — attached [thus], the pomposity shattered by the stick of one's own stalk, even the concealment of one's own words amounts to counting one's flight — thus the root-and-branch dislodging of falsehood — how is it to be countered? Even by thousands of streams of tears flowing from eyes gazing into the far distance, trembling like rain-clouds, there is no protection until death for the wretched one who argues with the haste of distress — thus, though with compassion, one's inner [self] is alarmed. In the rules of debate, do not [waste time] with copious prattle of fabricated false poetry — but be devoted to logic (<s>nyāya</s>), be worthy also in the conduct of reasoning! For indeed, what is this reasoning of yours? Even with all this, what essential nature of an entity has been established? 'For there is no mode other than thesis and counter-thesis' — if so, [we reply:] no, because at the time of stating the refutation, by the very absence of certainty, the resolution of the doubtful and unestablished [brings] the conclusion to the earlier form of the debate. The proof by reductio (<s>prasaṅga</s>) is presented either through [the opponent's] own admission, or through what is being considered possible, because there is no other mode. There, having stated that it is doubtfully unestablished, [the opponent says:] 'This is indeed the refutation that I myself have not admitted.' Let that be considered: do you at least accept agency? And that [agency], insofar as it was previously established, resting on recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) — thus the effect whose basis is of the nature of a seed, independent, established in the state of being such through the incapacity of positive and negative concomitance — that [agency] whose form is the severance of absolute disconnection, conclusively established and unbroken — how can the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) be desiccated by the fault of being doubtfully unestablished? And the contributing-cause nature (<s>ākṣepakāritva</s>) too, [being] established therein from the established portion, [one should] contemplate the portion that has become manifest from the womb of the totality, having vivified it; from the established portion, that which abides in the portion without separation — from the [perspective of] existence, it is stated: that very seed existed before too. How then is the proof by reductio — [namely,] the fitness for the convention of capacity, generated by the generation through momentary contributing-cause-hood — to be shaken by [the charge of] doubtful unestablishment? Thus, the earlier portion of the debate consisting of the extension of the counter-thesis adopted by the respondent [cannot stand] without accepting the dissolution of its own form — [its refutation] is comprehensive, like an occasion for reductio in the suppression of all faults. Both [aspects] — contributing-cause-hood and non-dependent-cause-hood — without even mentioning [them], the seed alone, even in the midst of cooperative conditions, [maintains] its established agent-nature; even before [the final moment], being of such a nature — speak from [the perspective of] existence, [speak] with a refutation that is well-joined and well-established!

tadvirahepi karaṇayogamapyāśaṅkyeta āśaṅkyatāmiti cet-tarhi bījavirahe 'pi āśaṅkyeta | tathā ca sādhvī (9) pratyakṣānupalambhapariśuddhiḥ | syādetat na bījādīnāṃ parasparasamavadhānavatāmeva body.translated_text: Objection: the resolution has already been stated. For the meaning is as follows — (7) "without delay with respect to <s>kṛti</s> (productive activity)" — what is the sense? Does <s>kṛti</s> occur immediately after origination, or without delay after the <s>samavadhāna</s> (assemblage) of <s>sahakāri</s> (cooperative conditions)? Or does it mean that as long as there is no <s>samavadhāna</s> of those capable <s>sahakāri</s>s, there is non-production, or that there is non-production in every respect whatsoever? (8) Among these, regarding the first and fourth options, there is absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid evidence); and when there is uncertainty between the second and third, <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) itself is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. For it is established by <s>pratyakṣa</s> that something of the seed-class (9) produces or does not produce after the <s>samavadhāna</s> of <s>sahakāri</s>s. Likewise, that what is devoid of <s>sahakāri</s> <s>samavadhāna</s> does not produce — this too is perceptually established. And here you too cannot escape this, since it is established by <s>pramāṇa</s>, and because of the absurdity that would follow from the contrary. For if, in the absence of <s>sahakāri</s>s, something does not produce, then even upon their <s>samavadhāna</s> it would not produce — that class of thing would simply not be a cause at all, since there is non-production in both cases of <s>samavadhāna</s> and non-<s>samavadhāna</s>. (2) Similarly, if it were to produce even in the absence of their <s>samavadhāna</s>, then the <s>sahakāri</s>s would not be causes, since production occurs even without them. And thus, even for those possessing <s>anvaya-vyatireka</s> (positive and negative concomitance) not otherwise established, if they were denied causal status, (3) the absurd consequence would be that the effect is uncaused; likewise, occasional occurrence would be undermined. And so, if the second alternative is intended, the <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) of a <s>bhāva</s> (entity) is precisely to be productive-without-obstruction. If the third alternative is intended, the <s>svarūpa</s> (essential nature) of a <s>bhāva</s> is precisely to be productive-with-obstruction — thus there is no exclusion of either interpretation. (This very point!) — (5) Ah, what an unprecedented display of arrogance! He, standing upon a ground most abundant in confusion, like a lotus-fed mighty warrior, torments even the ornament of truthful speech accompanied by rivals. And so — O dear one! — with the abundance of affectionately charming speech, without abandoning the companionship of <s>sahakāri</s> and the caravan of meaning that bears your own measure, your demonstration is truly one of <s>sāhitya</s> (literary elegance) — and that was (6) done by him — he presents the account of selling the cow while guarding it. After that statement, in the unwavering commentary, <s>Kīrtimata</s> is celebrated: the fruit of <s>pramāṇa</s> is beneficial as a means of proof. (7) For when one is discerning and characterized by <s>kṣaṇa</s>-perishing, being <s>kṣaṇika</s> (momentary), it is difficult to refute even by writing at leisure the foremost of the non-obstruction positions — such is the demonstration endowed with <s>śakti</s> (power). Therefore, from the words of the <s>ācārya</s> (8), having extracted that very teaching with the cup of <s>śruti</s> (scripture/hearing), let one be pleased with delight — he is not the author even in <s>sāhitya</s> by another's form, and his <s>svarūpa</s> existed even before — therefore he would produce even before. And although (9) the disputant debating by this method is well-established, still — is the absence of <s>sahakāri</s> only for what is incapable, or is the <s>samavadhāna</s> of <s>sahakāri</s>s only for what is already a producer? Otherwise not? What is the determining factor (10) here? To this it is replied: is there or is there not some difference between a seed stored in a granary and a stone fragment with respect to being favorable to a sprout? If there is no difference, then there would necessarily be no activity toward one rather than the other, and there would be no cessation for one seeking that result. If you say: through a succession of moments, there exists a seed-moment capable of producing a sprout — then when, even through succession, will it produce something of that nature? If you say there is doubt about this — what form does that doubt take? Is the doubt whether, (2) even when <s>sahakāri</s>s are assembled, it will produce or not? Or whether even when they are not assembled, it will produce or not? Or rather, that precisely when there is <s>samavadhāna</s> of <s>sahakāri</s>s, it will certainly produce — the doubt being only about when their <s>samavadhāna</s> will occur? (3) The first doubt has no scope, because causality in general has not been left undetermined — or if there were scope, then causality would already be determined. The second likewise has no scope, because the nature of the <s>sahakāri</s>s has been (4) determined — or if there were scope, their nature would not have been determined. But on the third option, all seed-moments falling within that causal continuum are of equal disposition, since wherever there is (5) <s>samavadhāna</s> of <s>sahakāri</s>s, production is invariable, and <s>sahakāri</s> <s>samavadhāna</s> is possible everywhere. If you say: <s>samavadhāna</s> of earth and such occurs only at a capable <s>kṣaṇa</s> — then what? Is it that (6) there is simply no <s>samavadhāna</s> of <s>sahakāri</s>s at an incapable moment? Or that even when there is <s>samavadhāna</s>, the effect is not born from it? Not the first, because the conjunction of earth, water, fire, and wind is observed (7) even in stone fragments and the like. Not the second, because it would absurdly follow that even from a seed possessing the full complement of <s>sahakāri</s>s, a sprout would sometimes not arise — just as from a stone fragment. If you say: let it be so — what is the fault? (8) This has not been observed in the first place. If you say it is merely suspected — then just as one might suspect non-production even when those conditions are present, one might equally suspect production even in their absence — let it be suspected! But then, even in the absence of a seed, it could be suspected. And thus, the purification through (9) <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension) would be sound. One might say: the suspicion is raised only on the basis that seeds and such produce effects precisely when in mutual <s>samavadhāna</s> — so that from the indeterminacy of <s>samavadhāna</s>, one might conclude that all things of that class are of uniform nature. Nor is the suspicion raised by accepting that capacity arises anywhere whatsoever — for that would conflict with <s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anupalambha</s> in allowing the possibility of effect-production even from incomplete causes. Rather, when seeds and such (2) are assembled, the possibility of effect-production is entertained in dependence on a specific sub-class distinction. Reply: when the explanation is already achieved by the mere observed <s>samavadhāna</s> alone, (3) there is absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> for such a supposition, the absurd consequence of excessive hypothesizing, and because the supposition is refuted, the absurd consequence of the disappearance of supersensory faculties and the like, and because the supposition is untenable, and because a <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular) is what is effective with respect to another <s>viśeṣa</s>. That too is without substance — the seed's birth, that is, its arising, whose established (4) cause is the sprout, stalk, spike, and so forth — even when concealed in wool-stores, barley-fields, forest granaries, and ground-level containers, through implements such as sickles, winnowing fans, mortars, and mirrors, and thereafter through the occasion suitable for sowing, (6) through observation of the season in the granary, through the drawing forth and excellence of the field, and through the <s>samavadhāna</s> of the ground, foundation, and such — being dependent on the condition of approaching — this has been ascertained in its entirety. And through however much succession of <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation) it is honored in proper (6) coherence, the effect called 'sprout' of earth and such elements is imperceptibly discerned. In this succession of transformed causes, does one's own <s>svabhāva</s>, or the <s>svabhāva</s> of the seed, or its unchanging prior form, (7) truly exist? — with such deliberation, one of stunted pride puts forth the question. Therein, the admission of a distinction that is not a separate matter does not stand before reason; nor is the well-known <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) of the Buddhists — the continuation of the subject under discussion — (8) of this kind — one that gladly benefits all three ears.

body.text: tadyathā samarthaḥ kutaḥ utpanna iti cet svakāraṇebhyaḥ | tānyenamaparapratyayasannidhāna eva kiṃ janayanti? kadācidanyathā syāt tataścaikopi kvacijjanayediti cet "aparāparapratyayayogena pratyabhikṣaṇaṃ bhinnaśaktayaḥ santanvantaḥ saṃskārāḥ yadyapi kutaścetsāmyātsarupāḥ pratiyante tathāpi bhinnaevai ṣāṃ svabhāvastena kiśñcideva kasyacitkāraṇamiti "kasmādḥ dṛśyāvāntarajātibhedopālambhaḥ sṛgallapallavitaḥ prabalajanavaduttānenāntaḥkaraṇaṃ prīṇāti prā (2) māṇikasya sthūlaparāmarśena hi vijātīyavyāvṛttavījāvarjitaṃ svakāryakāritvamavasthāpitamapi sūkṣmāvāntaraprasaṅgatadviparyayaparyālocanākhya vimarśāntaravṛtyā (3) bījatvādhiṣṭhitasvabhāvaviśeṣapratiṣṭhitaṃ prasādhyate kiṃ tatrānupapannaṃ nāma yathā davīyasi deśe viniveśitātmabhāvaṃ bhāvaṃ vibhāvya vṛkṣa ityavṛkṣavyāvṛttamavadhārayatyavadhā (4) raṇādhvarīṇodbhava janaḥ putraḥ sannidhānādhīnadhīviśeṣeṇa śiṃśapeti tatrāpyete nirūpaṇāt vakrakoṭarapaṭalaghaṭitasskandhasandhiriti svabhāvāntaramavagamya (5) mānamapi na vṛkṣatvaśiśapātva śūnyamavasīyate | na vā sarvovṛkṣaḥ śiṃśapā na vā sarve ca śiṃśapā vakrakoṭarapaṭalaghaṭitaskandhasandhiriti tathābhūtaṃ prastutama (7) pyastu vastuvyathāvyūhasyāpahateḥ anupahasita eva sādhyāsādhanabhāvaḥ bījatvameva hi sāmānyambidhirūpe 'vasthitaṃ akhilāsu vyaktiṣu nāsmākamaṅgīkārago (7) caraḥ punaśca tatrāvāntarādṛśyajātibhedābhyupagamavādo vāvadūkakalpita evamucyate [muhyate] na puñjapuñjena pratyarthitaḥ, etaccāmbaravartmavartikamalaparimalālolarolambamānā (8) virāvakulāvagāhi, yaduta- sa khalu jātiviśeṣaḥ saṃgrāhako vā syāt pratikṣepako vā syāt - evaṃ śālitvamapi saṃgrāhakaṃ carapratikṣepakaṃ vā | ḥ na ca nobhayamapītyādi (9) yathā vikalpakalpitapratidūṣaṇaprasaraḥ yasmātsmerāsyasarasīruhahārihasitenāpi nārpitasatyaṅkāraḥ kaścidapi vipaścidevaṃ vidhāvāntarajātibhede yādṛśastupa rāparapratyayaprabandhānubandhabodhitaḥ sāmānyasambhave 'pi svabhāvabhedastathā prakhyāpitamanantaraṃ sahetu hetuvittasaṃspandanena yatpunaruktirucyate viśeṣasya viśeṣaṃ prati prayo (2) jakavirodhācce ' ti tatsiddhameva sādhayitumārabdham | tathāpi yadyapi kutaścit sā syāt sarūpāḥ pratīyante tathāpi bhinna evaiṣāṃ svabhāva iti bhāṣayā śālibījatvādhiṣṭhitāntyavyaktilakṣaṇañca (3) vilakṣaṇasvabhāvaviśeṣavibhrānta eva kartṛvādo 'ṅkuraṃ pratisthūlaparāmarśavyavasthāpi tatkartṛbhāvabhājaṃ bījadharmmiṇaṃ adhyavasāyasāhityetarayoravasthayoḥ adhikaraṇakara (4) ṇe kalayā kalayitumaśakye virodhākarṣiprasaṅgaṃ tadviparyayapramāṇamaikyaparipanthipaśyatā dṛśyate hi prāmāṇikacakramaulilālitacaraṇayugalānā (5) mapyevaṃvidho kṣaṇavyāhāraḥ yathā pramāṇetataratāsādhāraṇavedavākyamākalayyādhikaraṇapramāṇāntareṇa prāmāṇyalakṣaṇasvabhāvāntarasādhanam | yathā vā (6) mahīmahīdharādiśaśadharakṛtetarādinā rūpeṇa saṃdigdhamapi dharmapurodhāya sādhanāntareṇa tanute jano jānāti cācaraṇīyacakrabahuviratitattvaṃ yaścāyamu(7) -pasaṃhāraḥ saṃddabdhaḥ | tasmādyo yathābhūto yathābhūtamātmano 'nvayavyatirekāvanukārayati tasya tathābhūtasyaiva tathābhūte sāmarthyam, tadviśeṣāstu kāryaviśeṣaṃ prayojayanti śālyādivaditi yuktamutpaśyāma iti mayokto yasmātsthūlāskhalitapratyākalanena aṅkenādāya tasminnaṃśe niḥśaṅkaḥśaṅkaśukopilokaḥ | kathaṃkathi(9) -kastu tadavāntaravicāracakracaurapravyāvitasthūladṛṣṭiniviṣṭabuddhiḥ prameyaḥ pradāpyate | nāmunā nyāyeneti punarbhaṇāmaḥ | anyabījajātīyamapi ca kusūlamī lanānuktabījaṃ bījatvena nirūpaṇāt | anayoravasthayoḥ sthitaikasvabhāvatvaṃ viruddhatā prasaṅgādināpramāṇenāha prayojakamātreṇābījatvamāyātīti kena bhāvena bhāṣya-(1)-te | kintayoravasthayo sthitasya sthairya pratyakṣeṇa siddhamasti | atha tadvā syāttāddak cāsyānukaścidviśeṣamityabhisandhinā |
body.translated_text: For example, if [asked] 'whence did the capable one arise?' — [the answer is:] from its own causes. Do those [causes] produce it only in the proximity of other cooperative conditions? If [it be said that] sometimes it would be otherwise, and thus even one [cause] could produce [an effect] somewhere — [we reply:] 'The latent impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>), continuously extending with differentiated capacities through conjunction with successive cooperative conditions, although from some [perspective] they are cognized as having the same form due to similarity, their nature is nevertheless indeed different; therefore, only a particular [thing] is the cause of a particular [effect].' Why? Because the apprehension of a visible sub-universal distinction, having branched out like a jackal, pleases the inner faculty of the epistemologist like a powerful person's [argument] by its forthrightness. For although causal efficacy toward its own effect — exclusive of the seed excluded from dissimilar [kinds] — has been established through gross apprehension, through the operation of another reflection, called the examination of the subtle sub-[distinction] and its contrary, it is demonstrated to be grounded in the particular nature governed by seed-hood. What is untenable about this? Just as a person — a son born of the sacrificial priest of ascertainment — having perceived an entity whose self-nature is situated in a distant place, ascertains 'tree' as excluded from non-tree; through a particular cognition dependent on proximity, [he ascertains] '<s>śiṃśapā</s>' (Indian rosewood) — since examination [occurs] there too with respect to these; and although another nature is being cognized [as] 'having a trunk-joint composed of crooked hollows and layers,' it is not determined as devoid of tree-hood and <s>śiṃśapā</s>-hood. Nor is every tree a <s>śiṃśapā</s>, nor is every <s>śiṃśapā</s> [one] with a trunk-joint composed of crooked hollows and layers. Let the matter at hand be of such a nature, since the array of distortions of the real object is not destroyed; the relation of <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and <s>sādhana</s> (probans) remains unimpaired. For seed-hood, which is a universal established in the form of a rule across all particulars, is not within the scope of our acceptance. And furthermore, the doctrine accepting invisible sub-universal distinctions therein is said [to be confused] — devised by a verbose [disputant] — it is not countered mass by mass. And this [argument] enters into [a space] swarming with the confused buzzing of bees hovering eagerly around the fragrance of lotuses growing along the sky-path — namely: 'That particular universal (<s>jātiviśeṣa</s>) would be either inclusive (<s>saṃgrāhaka</s>) or exclusive (<s>pratikṣepaka</s>).' 'Thus, rice-hood (<s>śālitva</s>) too would be either inclusive or exclusive.' 'And it cannot be both' — and so forth — as the proliferation of refutations devised by conceptual construction [proceeds]. Since no wise person has placed a seal of truth, even [one adorned] with the charming smile of a lotus-like face, upon such sub-universal distinctions. But a difference of nature, of such kind as is made known through the continuum of the succession of cooperative conditions, even when the universal is possible — as has been declared immediately [above] — together with the vibration of the cognition of cause and effect, the further statement that is made — 'because of the contradiction of the particular being the efficient [cause] of a particular' — that has begun to prove what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). Nevertheless, even though from some [perspective] they are cognized as having the same form, their nature is indeed different — by this statement, the doctrine of agency with respect to the sprout, characterized by the last particular governed by rice-seed-hood, is itself confused by the particular nature of a different character. Even the determination through gross apprehension, [which takes] the seed as the property-possessor partaking of that agency — in making the substratum and instrument in the two other states along with ascertainment — the unwanted consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>) of drawing a contradiction [arises] in what cannot be calculated by a fraction. For one who sees the proof of the contrary of that as obstructing unity — indeed, such a momentary utterance is observed even among those whose pair of feet is gracefully placed upon the crown-jewels of the circle of epistemologists — just as, having considered the <s>Vedic</s> statement [which is] specific to the validity of such and such a means of cognition, [one establishes] through another means of cognition pertaining to the substratum the establishment of another nature characterized by validity. Or just as, having placed in the forefront a property (<s>dharma</s>) that is doubtful with respect to the form of earth, mountains, moon-made, and other [things], one extends [the proof] through another means of proof; and the person knows the truth of the many cessations in the wheel of conduct. And this conclusion has been zealously undertaken. Therefore, that which, being of such a nature, causes its own positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) to follow in accordance with how things truly are — of that very thing, being of such a nature, [there is] capacity toward that which is of such a nature. But the particulars of that impel a particular effect, like rice etc. — this we see as reasonable — thus I have said, because by the comprehensive review without gross error, having taken [it] by a mark in that respect, the world, including even the parrot of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, is without doubt. But the doubter, whose intellect is fixed in gross vision — agitated by the thief of the wheel of sub-inquiry therein — is amenable to [being shown] the object of knowledge. 'Not by this method' — we state again. And since even a seed belonging to another seed-class — a seed unmentioned in the closing of the granary — is examined as possessing seed-hood, [the opponent] says by the non-proof (<s>apramāṇa</s>) [consisting of] the unwanted consequence of contradiction [with] the oneness of nature established in these two states: 'By merely being an efficient [cause], seed-hood accrues.' In what sense is this stated? Is the permanence of what is established in those two states proven by perception? Or perhaps it might be so — with the intention that 'such and such a specific [nature] of it [may hold].'

atha prasaṅgatadviparyayameva na kiñciditi kṛtvā | kiṃvā bījatvameva (3) sāmānyamātmasakalavyaktipratyekaparisamāptamūrtisahajaśaktisaśabditamāgantu śakti vyapadeśyaṃ sahakārisāhityasametamupalabdhamaṅkurajananayojyamanyathātve (4) bījatve iti manasi niveśya sthairyasya pratyakṣasiddhiparyālocanātśūnyatvānnādyaḥ | tādṛk tvamapi paryantavatināmeva bījānāmiti dvitīyopi na | prasaṅgatadvi (5) paryayapramāṇaṃ punarnirastasamastadūṣaṇam | abījaparāvṛtyā bījatvaṃ bahutamavyaktisammate 'pi pūrvāparakālayorbīje niścāyayiṣyate tena nijāgantukaśaktipakṣo (6) pakṣeṇa vailakṣaṇyāviṣkaraṇamātramatrāṇaṃ aṃkurasya jātiniyamākarmmakatvaprasaṅgastuviparyayavādhakamabādhakameva yatī'bījaparāvṛttiviśeṣeṇa bījatva (7) vāṅkuratvaniyamasyopapatteḥ | etena viparyayopyanaikāntikaḥ kathitaḥ | bījaviśeṣa eva hi prayojako na tanmātraṃ bījasya pramāṇavṛtterbalavatvāt | sthūladṛṣṭyā tvevamavasthāpya tāṃ na vyavahārahāniḥ pratibandhasādhanopāyaḥ punaḥ sāpāyaḥ aṅkurasya hi jātiniyamo na tāvannirmittaḥ, sārvatrikaprasaṅgāt | nāpyanyanimittaḥ tathābhūtasyābhāvāt seyaṃ (2) nimittavatā vipakṣānnivartamānā svavyāpyamādāya bījaprayojakatāmeva viśrāmyatīti pratibandhasiddhirityevaṃ varṇitā bījatvādhiṣṭhitasvabhāvabhedasyānyāvasthārūpatayā tūpalakṣaṇa (3) stha aṅkuratvaniyamaṃ pratiprayojakatvāt | vyabhicāryeva bījatvamātramaṅkurasyaprayojakatāyāṃ bījasvabhāvatvamātraṃ nāṅkure prayojakam, prayojakaṃ punaḥ tatsvabhāvādhiṣṭhita-(4) śeṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ prayatamāne bījatvamupalabdhamiti sthūlakalanam, na rūḍhakaphalaṃ tat anālokitastattvasthaloti etadeva tvamiti nāsau vyavahāraḥ pāramārthika(5) ityetattadā evamavatārito vicāraḥ kathaṃ prastāvamavavisphūryate tena bījasvabhāvatvaṃ kvacitkārye prayojakatvaṃ na vā? na cettatsvabhāvaṃ bījam, tena rūpeṇa (6) kaścidapyanupayogāt | evaṃ ca pratyakṣasiddhaṃ bīṃjasvabhāvatvannāsti sarvapramāṇāgocarastu viśeṣo 'stīti viśuddhā buddhirityupahāsabhāvāpyupahasitabhāva(7) meva tiraskaroti | kvacidapyupayoge tvekasya tena rūpeṇa sarveṣāmaviśeṣa tādrūpyāditi | yadyapi kutaścitsāmyātsarūpā pratīyante tathāpi bhinna eva eṣāṃ (8) svabhāvastena kiñcideva kasyacitkāraṇamityanena tathātvaṃ yacca bhāva syāditi kathitaṃ tadapi aprāptasahakārisāhityābhyāṃ viśeṣādipariṇāmalakṣaṇasāmarthyakāraṇa-(9)tvāt | antyabījarūpatvābhāvāt prasiddharoṣastiṣṭhati | tadeva hi tanna pūrva na paratvāditi kiṃ mukhasyete tasmāṃtpratikṣaṇamaparāparayat kāryānukūlapratyaya sākalyamadhi śayya bījatvamavāntaraṃ svabhāvālambanaṃ samvedyate tadeka kāryaprati tathābhūtaṃ samvedyate tadekakāryaṃ prati tathābhūtaṃ tadeva prayojakamasadvādagrahaḥ yaduktamanena tathā ca (2) bījaṃ kiṃcideva svakārya kuryānnāparāṇi | na ca vastumātraṃ tatkāryaṃ abījādanutpattiprasaṅgāt | nāpi bījamātraṃ aṃkurakāriṇo 'pi tadutpattiprasaṅgāt | nāpyaṅkurānyatamamātraṃ prāgapi tadutpattiprasaṅgāt | yadāyadutpannaṃ (3) sat yatkāryānukūlasahakārimadhyamadhiśete tadā tadeva kāyaṃ prati tasya prayojakamiti cet tatkimavāntarajātibhedamupādāya bījasvabhāvenaiveti vā ādye (4) sa eva jātibhedaḥ tatra prayojakaḥ kimāyātaṃ bījatvasya dvitīye tu samānaśīlānāmapi sahakārivikalpādakaraṇamityāyātaṃ tattatsahakāri sā (5)- hitye tattat kāryaṃ prati prayojakasya bījasvabhāvasya sarvasādhāraṇatvāditi | atrāpi prayogaḥ yat yena rūpeṇa arthakriyāsu nopamucyate na tattadrū paṃ yathā bī (6) jaṃ aṅkuratvena na kiṃcidpyakurvan na aṅkurasvarūpaṃ tathā ca śālyādayaḥ sāmagrīṃ praviṣṭādhibījatvenārthakriyāsu upayujyanta iti vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ (7) prasaṅgahetuḥ tadrūpatāyāṃ arthakriyāṃ pratiyogyatayā vyāptatvāt, anyathātiprasaṅgāt | tadrūpatvameva tasya pratyakṣasiddhatvādaśakyāpahravamiti cet - astu tarhi vi-(8)-paryayaḥ | yat yadrūpaṃ tattenārthakriyāsūpayujyate | yathā svabhāvena sāmagrī niveśino bhāvā bījajātīyārścaite kuśūlasthāsādayaḥ iti svabhāvahetuḥ tadrūpamātrā (9) nubandhitvāt yogyatāyāḥ tataścāsti kiñcitkāryaṃ yatra bījamupajyate | ityādirārambhe gambhīraḥ kaṇeravat tatsūramargalaḥ prasphuṭitaśaṃkha-(śṛṃga)-vat prabandho baddho vā bāla kathaya kutaḥ kutarke tvayā kalitaḥ | yataḥ pradarśādyānavadyavidyācāryaprakāṇḍaparipiṇḍinvīkṣikīkīrtitadharmakīrtikamatamaparāparapratyayogenetyādikaṃ prasaṅgo nāṅgasaṃgataḥ |
(2) tadrūpatāmātrasya vastuvat prasūtaprarohādikāryārjanayogyatayā vyāptyayogāt | kāraṇābhāvāt samarthasvabhāvānupapatteḥ | tathāhi tatra yo 'vyavadhānādi deśabīja-(3)- viśvambharādikalāpaḥ sa sabhāgāṅkurakaraṇe samartho hetuḥ yasteṣāṃ parasparopasarpaṇāśraya pratyayaviśeṣaḥ (4) sa taddhetujanane samarthaḥ teṣāñca na pūrvaṃ na paścāt na pṛthak bhāva iti samarthānāmapi pūrvāparapṛthagbhāvabhāvino doṣā nopalīyante | tenaiṣāṃ parasparopasarpaṇādiheturyaḥ samarthaheturiti tasya na kadācidanyathābhāvaḥ | anena (5) nyāyena sarvatra hetuphalabhāvapratiniyamaḥ draṣṭavyaḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ anyānyasvabhāvabhedānvayinīṣu bhāvaśaktiṣu na tu sthiraikabhāveṣu bhāveṣu svabhāvasyānyathātvāsaṃbhavāt (6) samarthāsamarthasvabhāvayoḥ kriyākriyāyogāt | anyasahitaḥ karoti cet kiṃ na kevala iti cet kiṃ kevalasya kāryakaraṇe 'samarthaḥ svabhāvaḥ | samarthaḥ kiṃ na karoti? (7) akurvan kathaṃ samartha iti? hetuvindāvācāryavacanamakalaṅkahariṇāṅkanirmalamapi svapakṣanirvāhavāhādhirohādiva pratyūhavyūhavyastamupanyastavān abhyasitamanīṣaḥ pā-(8) rśvakarāni utprekṣyate sāhityamupādhimadhiropya sāmarthyāsāmarthyāpekṣayā prasaṅgatadviparya yapratyāśāṃ śāti bhavān tatrāpyācāryavacanaṃ na sāhityepi para-(9) rūpeṇa kartā svarūpañcāsya prāgapīti prāgapi kuryāt | iti sāhityepi na sāhityaviśeṣaṇaṃ karaṇasāmarthya miti prasaṅgāt | proktaṃ vākyantu tataḥ svabhāvaniṣṭha-(10) mapratiṣṭhāpya prasaṅgo nāṅgasaṅgatimaṅgīkarotyuktameva |
body.translated_text: Now, having concluded that the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its reversal amount to nothing — or rather, having fixed in the mind that seed-hood (<s>bījatva</s>) itself is the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), complete in form in each and every instance of its own [class], designated by innate capacity (<s>sahaja-śakti</s>) and adventitious capacity (<s>āgantu-śakti</s>), endowed with the totality of cooperative conditions (<s>sahakāri-sāhitya</s>), perceived as fit for sprout-generation — whether in [its] being otherwise or in [its] being a seed: the first [alternative is rejected], because of the emptiness [resulting] from the consideration that permanence is established by perception; the second too [is rejected], because such nature belongs only to seeds that have a terminus. The proof by <s>prasaṅga</s> and its reversal, however, has all objections removed. Seed-hood, through the exclusion from non-seed (<s>abīja-parāvṛtti</s>), will be ascertained in the seed at both earlier and later times, even when accepted in a great number of instances. Therefore, the thesis of innate and adventitious capacity — merely revealing difference through the [opposing] thesis — provides no protection. The <s>prasaṅga</s> concerning the unrestricted class-determination of the sprout through seed-hood alone is [refuted by] the reversal-defeater, which is indeed not a defeater, since the restriction of seed-hood and sprout-hood is established through the particular exclusion from non-seed. By this, the reversal too is shown to be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). For only a particular seed is the productive cause, not mere seed-hood — because the operation of the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) regarding the seed is stronger. But having provisionally established [the matter] thus from a coarse perspective, this does not impair conventional practice. The method for establishing the invariable concomitance (<s>pratibandha</s>) is as follows, and it is feasible: the class-restriction of the sprout is indeed not uncaused, because of the unwanted consequence of universality; nor is it caused by something else, because of the absence of such [a cause]. This [restriction], turning away from the counter-positive while carrying its own pervaded [property], comes to rest precisely in the productive causality of the seed — thus the establishment of invariable concomitance has been described in this manner. The differentiation of essential nature presided over by seed-hood, in the form of another state, is merely an indicator, because of its being a counter-productive-cause for the restriction of sprout-hood. Mere seed-hood alone is a deviating [reason] with regard to the non-productive-causality of the sprout; mere seed-essential-nature is not productive of the sprout. Rather, what is productive is [the nature] presided over by the remainder presided over by that essential nature — [when] endeavoring, seed-hood is perceived — this is the coarse calculation, not [yielding] a firmly established result. Without examining the true state of affairs — 'that is just this' — that convention is not ultimate. When the investigation has thus been introduced, how does it come to be expounded on this occasion? Therefore, does the seed-essential-nature have productive capacity for some effect, or not? If the seed is not of that essential nature, then in that form it is of no use whatsoever. And thus, seed-essential-nature established by perception does not exist; but a distinction beyond the reach of all means of valid cognition does exist — [if this is proposed as] a 'purified cognition,' [then] even this mockery mocks the mocked. But if there is [some] use of one [seed] in that form, then there is no distinction among all [seeds] because of their having that same form. Even though they may appear similar due to some commonality, their essential natures are indeed different; therefore, only some particular [thing] is the cause of some particular [effect]. And what was stated — 'that which would be the [nature of] existence' — that too, because of the capacity that has the character of transformation in respect of distinction etc. [arising] from the cooperative conditions whose proximity has and has not been attained — because of the absence of the form of the final seed — the established [counter-argument] stands. For that [final stage] alone is that [productive cause], not the prior nor the subsequent etc. — so what is [gained] by face alone? Therefore, at every moment, presiding over the totality of conditions favorable to the effect in its successive [states], seed-hood is experienced as an intermediate self-nature-basis. With respect to one effect, that which is of such a nature — that alone is productive. The grasp of the non-existence doctrine [is refuted]. As was stated by this [argument]: thus the seed would produce only its own effect, not others. And a mere entity is not its effect, because of the unwanted consequence of non-production from a non-seed. Nor is mere seed-hood [the cause] of the sprout, because of the unwanted consequence that even sprout-producing [conditions] would produce it. Nor is it mere [identity with] any particular sprout, because of the unwanted consequence of its production even before [the appropriate conditions]. When, having arisen, [the seed] presides over the cooperative conditions favorable to a particular effect, then that alone is productive of that effect — if [one argues] thus, then [we ask:] is this by taking recourse to a sub-classification of class-distinction, or by seed-essential-nature alone? In the first case, that very class-distinction is the productive [cause] therein — what role has seed-hood? In the second case, it follows that even among those of the same character, there would be non-production due to variation in cooperative conditions — because the seed-essential-nature, being common to all, is productive of each particular effect [only] in the totality of each particular cooperative condition. Here too is the formal argument: whatever is not employed in causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) in a particular form — that is not of that form; just as the seed, not producing anything whatsoever qua sprout-hood, is not of the nature of a sprout. And thus, rice and the like, having entered the totality [of conditions] qua seed-hood, are employed in causal efficacy — this is the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). The <s>prasaṅga</s> reason [is valid] because of the pervasion — that the form in question is pervaded by fitness for causal efficacy — otherwise there would be over-extension. 'But that very form-hood is impossible to deny, being established by perception' — if so, then let the reversal [stand]: whatever is of a particular form, that is employed in causal efficacy in that form; just as entities that have the character of entering into the totality [of conditions] by their own essential nature, being of the seed-class — these, such as those stored in the granary — this is a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential-nature reason), because fitness is connected with mere form-hood. And so, there is some effect for which the seed is employed. And so forth — at the beginning, [the argument is] profound like a <s>kaṇera</s> (oleander tree); like the bolt of its champion, like a conch-shell horn burst open, a composition is bound — tell me, O child, whence has this sophistry been contrived by you? Because the <s>prasaṅga</s> of 'and so forth' does not connect with the [main] argument — [these are] the doctrines famed as <s>Dharmakīrti</s>'s, embodied in the immense logical science (<s>vīkṣikī</s>) of the eminent teachers of faultless learning beginning with exposition, [established] through successive cognitions. [Now regarding] the [claim that] mere form-hood alone, like an entity, has fitness for accomplishing effects such as germination and growth — [this] lacks pervasion. Because of the absence of the cause, the essential nature of capacity is untenable. For thus: that collection of location, seed, supporting-earth and the like that is without obstruction — that is the capable cause (<s>samartha-hetu</s>) for producing a homogeneous sprout. That particular condition which is the basis for their mutual approach — that is capable of generating its effect. And these [conditions] are neither prior, nor subsequent, nor separate — therefore the faults pertaining to prior, subsequent, and separate existence do not attach to the capable [causes]. Therefore, whatever capable cause is the reason for their mutual approach etc. — that never becomes otherwise. By this principle, the restriction of cause-effect relationship is to be observed everywhere — in the powers of entities that follow different essential natures at each moment, not in entities of a permanent single nature, because it is impossible for the essential nature [of a permanent entity] to be otherwise; because of the [respective] fitness and unfitness for action and non-action of capable and incapable essential natures. 'If [something] acts together with another, why not alone?' — if [asked] thus: 'Is the essential nature incapable of producing the effect by itself alone? If capable, why does it not produce? If not producing, how is it capable?' — [these are] the words of the teacher in the <s>Hetubindu</s>, immaculate as the mark of the deer [on the moon] of <s>Akalanka</s>, and yet one who has practiced [such] thought has propounded [them] as if mounted on the chariot of maintaining one's own thesis, interspersed with the array of obstacles. One imagines side-by-side [arguments], and, attributing the totality as a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), with regard to capacity and incapacity, [the opponent] extinguishes the expectation of <s>prasaṅga</s> and its reversal. But there too is the teacher's statement: 'Even in the totality, it does not produce in another's form; and its own form existed before too' — therefore it would produce even before. Thus, even in the totality, the capacity for production is not qualified by the totality — this follows as a <s>prasaṅga</s>. The statement that has been made, however — that which rests on the essential nature — having left the <s>prasaṅga</s> without a foothold, does not accept the connection with the [main] argument. This has already been stated.

body.text: nanu sati kṣaṇabhaṃga bhaṃgireṣāgurugariṣṭhopi śāstrakṛtaḥ tatprasādhakapramāṇaprasaṅgasaṅgatau durgatāṅganādohadalīlāṃ samudvahati picchilatattvatucchānacchārthā sa ya samūrcchalitā pakṣālakalaṅgaṇabharṅginaḥ sādhīyebhyo 'pi samyebhyo bībhatsanta iti (2) naitadāścaryaṃ sahasreṇāpi hi niṣpīḍāmavadhānataḥ surapatirakṣāṃ vīkṣyamāṇo na prekṣate 'sau sthitasthitasthityādisaṃvidhānādaparadaśāyāṃ bījasya janakatvamiti (3) sthirapakṣe kathamayaṃ niyamo mahanīyatāṃ nīyatāṃ kiṃ svahetudattamaryādatayā sāmagrayepi vā pratyekasāmarthyāsamarthamasahatayā vā paryantapratipannaparyantapratipannasaṃmūrcchanatādi sva-(4)-bhāvahīnatayā vā paripakṣādṛṣṭasadasatkarmanirmāṇanirmūlatayā vā dṛśyate tāvadevamevaṃ te kathamityanarthakaprathamakathā prathanādvā kaścarat purato gacchet svabhraṃ (5) vā svargameveti pakṣāḥ pañcendriyakalpanāt pañca vā upaskṛtasañcitānyaviṣayaniścayanānnādyā manasi vipaścitaḥ praviśati śakyamevamatathyamapi (6) sthāpayituṃ svakāraṇakalāpaparikalpitaṃ cakṣuṣo rūpaṃ yadidaṃ madīyo rūpaṃ ca samavaiti |
body.translated_text: Now, given <s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s> (momentary destruction), even the author of the treatise, who is most weighty among those devoted to the doctrine of destruction, carries on the sport of a pregnant woman's cravings in the application of the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) that establishes it — those whose arguments are slippery in essence and trifling in substance, who have taken up the buzzing-bee manner of besmirching the opponent's thesis, are disgusted even by those who are better and more balanced. (2) This is no wonder, for even with a thousand efforts, when examined without care, <s>Indra</s> (lord of the gods) looking at his own protection does not truly see it. That one does not perceive that the seed has generative capacity in another state due to the arrangement of persistence upon persistence and so forth. (3) In the thesis of permanence, how is this restriction to be established? Let it be honored — is it by the limitation bestowed by its own cause, or by the incapacity of each individual factor even when the aggregate of conditions is present due to lack of cooperative power, or by the absence of the intrinsic nature of the mutual coalescence of that which has reached its final stage, (4) or by the uprooting of the construction of existent and non-existent <s>karma</s> (action) unseen from the opposing thesis? It is seen thus indeed — how then is this for you? From the spreading forth of the first pointless discourse, or someone might go forward falling into his own pit, (5) or to heaven itself — these are the five theses, from the construction of the five sense-faculties, or five; because the accumulated and refined determinations regarding objects not within their scope do not enter the mind of the wise in the first instance. It is possible to establish even what is untrue (6) — the form attributed to the eye constructed by its own causal aggregate — that which is 'my form' also comes together with it.

body.text: śabdamatha pratyāsīdantaṃ tadātmanā tulayati aparatrānyevaṃ viṣaye-(7)-'nuśāsanīyamiti tṛpañcatayī kalpanā pāramārthikī syāt grāhyārthaviṣayā upadravyaṃ bhāvayituṃ pāryante | svahetudattamaryādatayā yadekameva hi svahetuvihitaviśeṣa (8) pañca vā dhiyaṃ dhatte pañcaprapañcacakṣurādīndriyaprasādāditi tadanantaramaghātapariśīlinamapi (śīlanīyaṃ) ekaikaśaḥ kalitānvayavyatirekatvāt anyapariṇāmapraṇāśamā-(9)-śaṃsatāṃ pūrvāśivatātiḥ prativādasya prārabdhāpriyeṇa priyamanuṣṭhitam | karmmanirmāṇanaipuṇyaṃ na pramāṇayatā praṇetavyo vyomāntarjātoyo vījādi bhāva (grāmaḥ) tasya dṛṣṭābhiniviṣṭatve vā kāmaṃ anya pratīkṣo 'stu, niyamastu virudhyata iti guruprabādhakapramāṇaprahāraḥ prakṛṣṭa āste | vādādikathā navyasya kathane ca vikṣepanigrahaprasaṅgaḥ (2) syāt pakṣapūjāviṣkaraṇamātramantimasapakṣe lakṣyate na punaradhikaṃ kiñcit |
body.translated_text: Then, approaching the word as identical with that, one weighs it thus: 'In another domain, one should instruct in this manner regarding the object' — (7) this fivefold or threefold construction would be ultimate, having as its object the graspable meaning; subsidiary substances can be cultivated. By the limitation bestowed by its own cause, that which is one alone, endowed with the distinction fashioned by its own cause, (8) sustains five or more cognitions through the clarity of the five-fold elaboration of eye and other sense-faculties — and then, even for one practiced in non-destruction, through the <s>anvaya-vyatireka</s> (positive-negative concomitance) ascertained one by one, for those who proclaim the destruction through transformation by another, (9) the prior inauspiciousness of the counter-thesis is accomplished — the disagreeable begun achieves what is agreeable. The skill in the construction of <s>karma</s> (action) is not to be established by one who validates <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) — the collection of entities such as seeds born within the space of the sky; or if one is fixated on what is observed regarding that, let another expectation stand, but the restriction is contradicted — thus the blow of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that refutes the teacher's position stands supreme. (2) In the discourse of debate and so forth, in the exposition of the new, there would be the contingency of distraction and restraint; in the final thesis, only the display of honor to the position is observed, and nothing more.

body.text: tasmāt tathā tatkāraṇaṃ vastu tathaiva tadakāraṇam

children.translated_text: By whom is it accepted that what is a cause of that is not also accepted as a non-cause? (3)
Without a difference in intrinsic nature, even activity (<s>vyāpāra</s>) is not logically possible;
Since a permanent entity is without surplus capacity, its efficacy (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is also difficult to trace through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance).

body.translated_text: Therefore, just as a thing is that cause in that manner, so too it is equally a non-cause of that;

body.text: iti prasaṅgatadviparyaya preriṇāprasaraḥ sthiratve sati janakatvena nirṇītasyānti-(4)-ma pariṇāme brīhiviśeṣasyāvicala iti sthitamācāryavacanaṃ tasmāttatsvabhāvasya anyathātvāsambhavāt | taddharmaṇastu tathābhāvo 'ntyāvasthāvadanivāryaḥ | antyāvasthāyāṃ-(5)-prāga samarthasya sāmarthyotpattau sāmarthyasya tatsvabhāvatve 'pūrvotpattireva sā | atatsvabhāvatve sa prāgiva paścādapi akāraka eva | sāmarthyākhyātapadārthānta (6) rātkāryonpatteriti tasmātpratiṣṭhitasvabhāvabhāgī bhāvaḥ | ahetubhirjanyate na punaryayathānupratiṣṭhaḥ bījantu sati sahakārisākalye saṃdigdhe ni-(7)-ghananibandhanādhīnatvaṃ saśaṃsitasaṃbhāvanaṃ svahetunā janyata iti janyametat samastanyāyanīte |
body.translated_text: Thus the advance of the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its converse is set in motion — when permanence is established, the final transformation of the particular rice-grain, which has been determined to have generative capacity, remains unmoved — thus stands the word of the <s>Ācārya</s> (master). Therefore, since the intrinsic nature of that cannot become otherwise, the property of that being so is as inevitable as up to the final state. (5) When capacity arises in what was previously incapable at the final state — if that capacity is of the same intrinsic nature as that entity, then that is nothing but a new arising not previously existent. If it is not of that intrinsic nature, then, just as before, it remains a non-agent even afterwards. Since the effect arises from a different category of thing called 'capacity,' (6) therefore an entity that partakes of a firmly established intrinsic nature is not produced by non-causes; rather, a seed, when the full complement of <s>sahakārin</s> (cooperative conditions) is present but doubtful, (7) with the possibility of dependence on a dense foundation being suspected, is produced by its own cause — thus this entire matter is settled by the principles of reasoning.

children.text: pāratantryaṃ hi sambandhaḥ siddhe kā paratantratā |
children.translated_text: For dependence is relation; when something is already established, what further dependence is there?
Therefore, for any entity whatsoever, there is no relation in the ultimate sense;

children.text: rūpe śleṣo hi sambandho dvitve sati kathaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: For relation is contact with form; when there is duality, how can it obtain?
Therefore, for things different by nature, there is no relation in the ultimate sense.
Even mutual dependence is a relation — if that is non-existent, (9) how does it depend?
And how does an entity that is self-sufficient and without expectation of another depend?

body.text: siddhāsiddhayorapekṣābhābādatyantasambhavī sambandhaḥ na siddhasyāsiddhaṃ kiñcidasti yadarthamapekṣyate yathā sāmānyātmanāsiddhaṃ viśeṣātmanārthamapekṣate aṅkurādiko bhāvaḥ niṣpattyaniṣpattivirudddharyādhyāsena bhinnatvāt siddhāsiddhavikalpānatikramāt tato na sahakārisāpekṣa-(2) balakṣapakṣādipadārthasārthasya sambhavaḥ svahetoḥ sambhāvanāspada nahi bhavati nijajanananigaḍaniyamita evāyaṃ naropasannamaunaniyama eva vācā vācaspati-(3) mapi picchayati | tasmātpramāṇaviruddha evārtho jñāpakena jñāpyate kāraka hetunā ca karaṇīya iti eṣa eva paramapramāṇikaḥ pracāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Since there is no dependence between the established and the unestablished, relation is absolutely impossible — for what is established has nothing unestablished for the sake of which it would depend; just as what is established in its universal nature depends on something for the sake of what is unestablished in its particular nature, entities such as sprouts, being different through the superimposition of contradictory properties of coming-into-being and not-coming-into-being, do not transcend the alternatives of established and unestablished — therefore the existence of an entity that is a companion to the category of <s>sahakārin</s> (cooperative condition), capacity, thesis and so forth, (2) does not become a ground for the possibility of its own cause. For this one is constrained by the fetters of its own production — just as one who has taken a vow of silence near a person silences even <s>Vācaspati</s> (lord of speech) by his speech. Therefore, the very object that contradicts <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) is made known by the indicator, and what is to be done is done by the efficient cause — this alone is the supreme procedure of valid cognition.
