body.text: yaccoktam ḥathavā vyatirekeṇa prayogaḥ (4) vivādādhyāsitaṃ bījaṃ sahakārivikalpaprayuktāṅkurādikāryavaikalyaṃ tadutpattiniścayaviṣayībhūtabījajātīyatvāt, tatpunaḥ sahakārivikalpaprayuktāṅkurādikārya (5) na bhavati tadevaṃbhūtajātīyam, yathā śilāśakalamiti etadapi na sasāhityepi pararūpeṇa kartā ityetena gatārthaḥ | aṃkurajanasvabhāvabhraṣṭabhāvādeva anā-(6)-virbhūtābhinavodbhidvījaṃ prāgavasthāyāmiti sthāpitameva | sthūlaparāmarśāśraye samāveśyābījavyāvṛttavījaviṣayamanvayavyatirekakalpanaṃ sūkṣmāvā-(7)-ntaranirūpaṇaparāhanyamānamānasenāpi mantavyaṃ ko 'tra mantrayate | tasmātsthūlaparāmarśāpekṣayā yadi svabhāvaviśeṣabhraṃśena nāsyāṅkurakāryavika(8) latvaṃ sādhyamevamanokāntaḥ | sūkṣmaprekṣāpakṣāpekṣatā yajjātīyatvamasiddham | sa eva hi tasya nāsti yastajjanakaḥ | niḥsvabhāva iti bhāvaḥ | tadatra paramārthaḥ satvaṃ (9) tu hetuḥ kṣaṇikatve kutaḥ sapakṣo jaladharaḥ sa ca sāśvadharmādhyāsito bodhanīyaḥ pramāṇena pramāṇañca prasaṅgaviparyaya tacca kiṃ vyāpāraṃ upapādyate | pūrvāparāvasthayoḥ karaṇākaraṇamadhyakṣaprekṣitaṃ lakṣyīkṛtya pramāṇāntarabādhādvā kādācitkānapekṣavat iti tarkopaniṣadācāryavacanādviruddhamekatve pūrvāparāvasthayorbījasya prānte prekṣitapratyekakartṛtvasya sādhayati karaṇākaraṇam | yasmādvirodhasya sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ ca vicakṣaṇaḥ samācakṣāṇaḥ parabhāga-(3)-bhāgī tatra sāmānlayakṣaṇamekadharmaṇyanavasthitiniyatatvaṃ tacca sāmānyaṃ vyaktidvayātmanā viśeṣī syāt | sahānavasthānalakṣaṇaṃ parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇa-(4)-tākhyaṃ ca | tatra prācyasya (ādyasya) pratyakṣānupalambhapratyakṣāṇi sattā sādhyasiddhāni dvitīyasya punaranyonyabhedasiddhervā dhruvabhāvavināśavat pramāṇāntarabādhādvā | kādācit(5) kānapekṣavaditi vacanādupāyadvayamupanyastamāste | tatra tatkālaṃ kāritvamatatkālakāritvabhedena sidhyati viruddhaṃ na kālāntarākāritvena tadavacchede-(6)-nāsya vidhervidhuratvāt | yathā kādācitkamakādācitkatvena viruddhaṃ anapekṣatvamapi sāpekṣatvena |
body.translated_text: And as for what was said: 'Or alternatively, the application through <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) — (4) the seed that is the subject of dispute, the deficiency of effects such as sprouts occasioned by the alternative construal of <s>sahakārin</s> (cooperative conditions), being of the same type as the seed that is the object of certainty regarding its production — that again does not produce effects such as sprouts (5) occasioned by the alternative construal of cooperative conditions, being of such a type, like a piece of stone' — this too is already settled by the statement that even in conjunction it is an agent only in its own form. The seed in which the novel sprout has not yet appeared, having fallen from its sprout-generating nature, (6) is established as being in its prior state. When this <s>anvaya-vyatireka</s> (positive-negative concomitance) reasoning concerning the seed, distinguished from the non-seed, is accommodated within a framework of gross apprehension, (7) it should be understood as being struck down by the examination of subtle distinctions, even by one whose pride is being humbled — who deliberates here? Therefore, if through gross apprehension, by the lapse of its specific intrinsic nature, (8) its deficiency in producing the sprout-effect is to be proved — this is inconclusive in just this way. From the standpoint of subtle examination, the type-identity is unestablished. For that very nature which would make it a generator of that does not exist in it — the meaning is: it is devoid of intrinsic nature. Here the ultimate truth is this: (9) existence (<s>sattva</s>) is the reason for <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness) — whence comes the positive instance? A cloud — and that is to be understood as superimposed with the properties of the permanent. By what <s>pramāṇa</s>? And the <s>pramāṇa</s> is <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s> (reductio and its converse) — and what activity does it establish? The doing and not-doing in prior and subsequent states, as observed by direct perception, and through the obstruction by another <s>pramāṇa</s>, or like the occasional and the independent — from the statements of the masters of reasoning and <s>Upaniṣad</s>, contradicting unity, it establishes the doing and not-doing of the seed in its prior and subsequent states, the individual agency observed at its final point. (3) And a discerning one declaring the general characteristic of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), partaking of the other's portion — therein the general characteristic is the necessary non-co-existence in a single property-bearer, and that <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) would be particularized through the nature of two instances. (4) The characteristic is non-co-existence, and it is also called the characteristic of standing in mutual exclusion. Of the first, direct perception and non-apprehension serve as <s>pramāṇas</s>, establishing existence as what is to be proved; of the second, either through the establishment of mutual difference, like permanent existence and destruction, or through obstruction by another <s>pramāṇa</s>, (5) or like the occasional and the independent — by this statement, two means are presented. Therein, the contradiction is established through the distinction between being an agent at that time and not being an agent at another time — not by mere non-agency at another time, (6) since this rule would be ineffective in delimiting that. Just as the occasional is contradicted by the non-occasional, so too non-dependence is contradicted by dependence.

body.text: atha cayenaiva pramāṇena kādācitkānapekṣa-(7)-yoḥ eka dharmiṇyanavasthitiniyatatvaṃ nirūpyate, tenaivānayorvirodho bodhasaudhādhirohī tadvatkālabhedena anāśritādimavirodhabodhopāyayora-(8)-pi karaṇākaraṇayoḥ prasaṅgaviparyayākhya makṣatapramāṇalakṣaṇamākhyāti, parasparapratyanīkatvamekadharmaṇyanavasthitiniyamaṃ nirūpayaditi palāyitaṃ pra(9) tyāśayā parasya ato yadaparamevamavādīt vādī tadapi dalitadardhamapasarpati sacivān |
body.translated_text: Now, by the very <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) by which the necessary non-co-existence of the occasional and the independent (7) in a single property-bearer is ascertained, by that very same means the contradiction between these two ascends to the palace of understanding. Likewise, with respect to doing and not-doing, which are means of understanding contradiction not based on temporal division (8) and not dependent on a beginningless foundation, the <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s> (reductio and its converse), which is the characteristic of an unimpaired <s>pramāṇa</s>, declares their mutual opposition, ascertaining the necessary non-co-existence in a single property-bearer — thus the opponent (9) flees in expectation of return. Therefore, whatever else the proponent said in this manner also crumbles and slips away along with its allies.

body.text: astu bījatvameva prayojakam, bhavatu sahakārisannidhāne sati kartṛsvabhāvatvaṃ bhāvasya, tathā ca tadasannidhāne 'karaṇamapyupapadyatām, tathāpi tajjātīyamātra eveyaṃ vyavasthā na tvekasyāṃ vyaktau karaṇākaraṇalakṣaṇaviruddha dharmādhyāsasya (2) tathā ca tadasaṃnidhāne pratyakṣasiddhatayā tatra durvāratvāditi cet-na virodhasvarūpānavavodhāt | sa khalu dharmayoḥ parasparābhāvarūpatvaṃ vā syāt nityānityavat(3) dharmiṇi tadāpādakatvaṃ vā śītoṣṇatvavat tadvatā vā daṇḍitva kuṇḍalitvavat |
body.translated_text: Let seed-nature (<s>bījatva</s>) alone be the motivating [cause]; let it be that the entity has the nature of being an agent when the auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakāri</s>) are present, and likewise let non-production be accounted for in their absence. Nevertheless, this arrangement pertains only to the kind (<s>jātīya</s>) [in general], not to the superimposition of contradictory properties — characterized as production and non-production — upon a single individual (<s>vyakti</s>). And since [the seed] is established by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) as existing in the absence of those [conditions], the [objection] is irresistible there — if so, [the reply is:] no, because of the failure to understand the true nature of contradiction (<s>virodha</s>). That [contradiction] is indeed either: the mutual absence of properties, like permanence and impermanence; or the production of such [opposite] attributes in a substrate, like cold and heat; or [the presence of contradictory attributes] in what possesses them, like being a staff-bearer and being coiled [like a snake].

body.text: nādyaḥ nirviśeṣaṇasyāsiddheḥ yāvatsatvaṃ kiñcittkaraṇāt | saviśeṣaṇasya tu virodhasiddhāva-(4)-pyadhyāsānupapatteḥ | yadāyadakaraṇaṃ hi tatkaraṇasyābhāvo na tvanyadā tatkaraṇasya na caitayorekadharmisamāveśamātiṣṭhāmahe | netaraḥ bhāvābhā(5) vavyatiriktayoḥ karaṇākaraṇāsiddheḥ vyāpārāparavyapadeśasahakāribhāvābhāvau hi karaṇākaraṇe kāryabhāvābhāvau vā | ati-(6)-rekasiddhāvapi svakāla evaṃ svābhāvapratikṣepavadakaraṇābhāvamākṣipet karaṇaṃ na tvanyadā | nahi yo yadā nāsti sa tadā svabhāvaṃ pratikṣeptumarha-(7)-ti, virodhyabhāvaṃ vākṣeptuṃ tathā sati na kadācidapi tatra syānna kadāpi tadvirodhī bhavediti | 'nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sata' iti āyātaṃ na vā viro -(8)-dha ityādikamatarkya tārkikatvaṃ arkakarasaṃparkakarkaśagāminopo mano na sāntvayati asarpāyopetatvādamīṣāmasadvikalpānām | yat punaḥ prasaṅgavipa-(9)-rya yamadhikṛtyai vā (e) kābhidhānam ḥstāṃ vā tathāpi na tābhyāṃ śakyāśakyayoravivakṣita kāla bheda eva virodhaḥ, sādhyate tathopasaṃhartuṃ aśakyatvāt | ḥ yadā tadetyupekṣya(10) yatsamartha tat karotyevetyupasaṃhartuṃ śakyamiti cet na kāla niyamāvivakṣāyāṃ yat samartha tat karotyeva kadācidit syāt | tathā ca sambhava vidheratyantā yogo viruddhaḥ, na tvayogaḥ nīlaṃ sarojaṃ bhavatyeveti vat iti | tadapi ayogo 'tyantāyīgavyavacchedenāpi sarvadā bījasya satve sambhavantu katṛtvamityabhimatatvāt malinanalina-(2)- nibhaṃ nibhālanīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Not the first, because that which is without qualification is not established — for as long as [the entity] exists, it produces something. But for the qualified [entity], even when contradiction is established, superimposition is untenable — for when at one time there is non-production, that is the absence of production at that [time], not at another time; and we do not maintain the inclusion of both these in a single substrate. Not the other [option], because production and non-production are not established as distinct from existence and non-existence [of the entity]. For production and non-production are [merely] the presence and absence of the auxiliary conditions designated as activity etc., or [alternatively] the presence and absence of the effect. Even if a distinction were established, production, just as in its own time it precludes its own non-existence, would preclude the absence of non-production — but not at another time. For one who does not exist at a certain time cannot at that time preclude its own nature, nor invoke the absence of its contrary; otherwise, there would never be [production] in that [locus], and its contrary would never arise there. [The principle] 'There is no coming into being of the non-existent, nor is there ceasing to be of the existent' [Bhagavadgītā 2.16] has been arrived at — or [the claim that] there is no contradiction — such inconceivable logicality [of the opponent], whose mind proceeds harshly like the touch of the sun's rays, does not console [us], because these false conceptions are devoid of any real basis. As for the further single statement made with reference to the contingency argument and its reverse — let that be; nevertheless, by those two [arguments], the contradiction is nothing but the unintended temporal distinction between what is capable and what is incapable, because it is impossible to conclude otherwise. If [one says:] setting aside 'when, then' [temporal qualifications], it is possible to conclude 'whatever is capable, that indeed produces' — [the reply is:] no, for when there is no intention of temporal restriction, 'whatever is capable, that indeed produces' would apply only sometimes. And thus the absolute connection (<s>atyantāyoga</s>) would contradict the rule of possibility (<s>sambhavavidhi</s>), but not the non-connection — [this is] like [the statement] 'a blue lotus indeed exists.' That too — the non-connection through the delimitation by absolute non-connection — is to be considered as resembling a tainted lotus, since it is accepted that agency accrues to the seed at all times when it exists.

body.text: yaccoktam - "nanu yadasamatha (tvaṃ) prathamamāsīt, tasya paścādapi sāmarthya kuta āgatam | prathamaṃ samarthasya nā paścāt tatra gataṃ naitadevaṃ tattatsahakārimataḥ (3) tatkārakatvaṃ hi sāmarthya, atadvatastadanyavato vā tadakartṛ tvamasāmarthyamidañcautpattikamasya rūpamiti | ḥ tadapi sahakārisāpekṣajananabījavimarśena gatam te ca (4) sahakāriṇaḥ svopasarppaṇa pratyayavaśādbhinnakālā ityarthāt kāryāṇāmapi bhinnakālateti tathāpyekakālastha eva bhāvo jāto naṣṭastadā kāryaṃ karotu utpannamā (5) trasya tatsvabhāvatvāt | ekadeśasthavaditi cet -seyamekakālatā svarūpakālāpekṣayā sahakārisāṃnidhyāpekṣayā vā ādye na kiñcidanupapannaṃ (6) nityānāmapi evaṃ rūpatvāt, vartamānaikarūpatvādbhavānāṃ tadeva tu kvacitsāvadhi kvacinniravadhīti viśeṣaḥ | sāvadhitvepi vyāpāraphalapravāhaprakarṣāpraka-(7)-rṣābhyāṃ viśeṣaḥ | dvitīyastu syādapi yadi teṣāṃ yaugapadyaṃ bhavet | kramiṇastu sahakāriṇa ityuktam | sahakārisahitaḥ svabhāvena karotīti vaktari jā-(8)-ta naṣṭa eva karotu ityuttaraprasaṅgo nirargalaśaiśavasyetyalamanena | tasmātkāryasya sa eva kālaḥ kāraṇasya sacānyaśceti sambandhikālāpekṣayā pūrvakālatā vyavahā-(9)-raḥ | etadapi sahakārisākalyaviśeṣaṇakaraṇanirākaraṇādalīkaṃ parikalpanamanalpaṃ śalyacakrasātabhājanam deśabhedena tu kartṛtvākartṛtvamupalabdhaṃ ānyākṣepaṃ upayanātmahasitasahacarañca na virodhatvādi (2) sanamāpannaḥ | tenaiva sahakāreṇa tasyaiva tadaiva tathaiva sambaddhatvamasambaddhatvaṃ ca pūrvāparavelāyāmaniścita ḥastu tarhi tasyaiva tenaiva sahakāriṇa sahasambandho 'sambandhaśceti (3) virodhaḥ na vikalpānupapatteḥ | tathāhi sambandhinaḥ sambandhyantare svābhāvasvābhāvyaṃ vā virudhyeta, abhāva pratiyogitvaṃ vā, tadaiveti sahitaṃ vā, tatrai vati (4) sahitaṃ vā, ubhayasahitaṃ vā, tathaiveti sahitaṃ vā? vikalpakrameṇa (1) taduddharaṇavaktavyañcācakṣitamālocanīyam | (5) tathāhiśaśaśṛṃgasya |
body.translated_text: As to what was said: 'But if that which was incapable at first — whence did its capacity come later? [And] if it was capable at first, where did that [capacity] go subsequently?' [The reply is:] it is not so. From the standpoint of the respective auxiliary conditions, the capacity to produce that [effect] is the causal capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>); the non-agency of what does not possess that [capacity], or of what possesses something other than that — [that] is incapacity; and this is the innate form of the entity. That too is resolved by the consideration of the seed's production dependent on auxiliary conditions. And those auxiliary conditions have different times due to the conditions of their own approach — hence the effects too have different times; nevertheless, the entity that exists at one time alone — born and destroyed — let it then produce its effect, because of the identity of nature with [the entity] as it has arisen. If [one says:] as one who exists in one place [does not act in another] — [the reply is:] this same-temporality (<s>ekakālatā</s>) is either with reference to the entity's own time or with reference to the presence of auxiliary conditions. In the first case, nothing is untenable, since even permanent entities have such a form; for entities have the same form in the present, but the distinction is that in some cases [existence] has a limit and in others it is limitless. Even when limited, there is a distinction due to the greater and lesser extent of the stream of activity and result. The second [option] might be [viable] if there were simultaneity of those [conditions]; but the auxiliary conditions are successive, as stated. When one says 'the entity produces by its own nature together with auxiliary conditions,' the further contingency that 'let it produce even when born and destroyed' [follows] — [this is] the unrestrained childishness — enough of this. Therefore, the same time of the effect is the time of the cause, and [if] that [time is considered] different, then the prior temporality is merely conventional with reference to relational time. This too, from the refutation of qualifying production with the totality of auxiliary conditions, is an extensive false imagination, a receptacle for the circle of thorns. But as for the [attempt to establish] agency and non-agency through spatial distinction — the perceived [difference] involves the objection from another [quarter], accompanied by the self-ridicule of the approach, and does not arrive at being a contradiction etc. The connection and non-connection of that very [entity] with that very auxiliary condition, at that very time, in that very manner, in the prior and subsequent moments — [this remains] undetermined. Let there then be connection and non-connection of that very [entity] with that very auxiliary condition — [if] this is a contradiction, [the reply is:] no, because of the untenability of the conceptual alternatives. For [would the contradiction] be with respect to the related [entity's] own nature in relation to another relatum? Or the counter-positive of absence? Or conjoined with 'at that very time'? Or conjoined with 'in that very place'? Or conjoined with both? Or conjoined with 'in that very manner'? [Each alternative] is to be resolved in the order of the conceptual alternatives — what has been indicated is to be examined. For thus: of a hare's horn [there is no contradiction].

body.text: ñca ye yogyamayogyaścāpi jāyate ||
body.translated_text: And that which is both fit and unfit is also born.

children.translated_text: For one whose nature is eternally fit, because of the contradiction with that very conceptual alternative,
the nature that is to be designated as 'fitness' (<s>yogyatā</s>) — let that be determined.
What need is there of others such as separation, conjunction, and kind (<s>jāti</s>) — of going and the rest?
Even when those [categories] exist, [the question] 'of that' [remains] — because of the non-establishment of the relation.

body.text: yuktaḥ svabhāvabhedo 'yaṃ tatpratikṣaṇajanminām |
body.translated_text: This difference of nature is justified for those that are born at each moment (<s>pratikṣaṇajanman</s>).

body.text: iti nyāyāt yadi saṃsargayo-(7)-gyaḥ svabhāvo bījasya nijo nāpaiti kadācana tadā svābhāvasvabhāvavatvamatṛṇahetuṃ kathamuktaṃ nānyat karmma iti | śeṣaṃ tu phalguvarjitaṃ anargalabālatvasyetyādi (1) tamālokasya | atha kādācitkaṃ tadrūpaṃ tadeva nirūpyatāṃ nibandhanaṃ ............... dipi yaḥ kimadhikeneti dhūrtatvena |
body.translated_text: By this reasoning: if the nature of the seed that is fit for conjunction is innate and never departs, then how can the nature of possessing one's own essential nature be said [not to be] the cause of grass — 'there is no other action'? But the remainder is devoid of substance — [it belongs to] the unrestrained childishness etc. of that dark [opponent]. Now, if that form is occasional (<s>kādācitka</s>), let that very ground be determined [...] what more need be said? — [this is dismissed] as roguery.

body.text: 'iti anvayamukhena kṣaṇikatvānumānanirākṛtasya nirākaraṇam |'
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the refutation of the refutation of the inference of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) through the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) aspect.

body.text:
vyatirekabhāvādinirṇayaḥ
dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: The determination of the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) aspect etc. — Second Chapter.

body.text: prasaṃgaviparyayarahasyaṃ.....pūrvaparyavasthi (ta).....vipakṣādakṣaṇikā vyāyāvṛttaṃ prāptaṃ varṇanam | adhikaśca tatrāśrayahetudṛṣṭāntasi (1) ddhau-pramāṇābhāvaḥ, avastuni pramāṇābhāvavṛtteḥ, pramāṇa pravṛttāvalīkatvānupapatteḥ | evaṃ tarhi avyavahāre svavacanavirodha iti cet-tat kiṃ svavacanavirodhenateṣupramāṇamupadarśi-(2)-taṃ bhavet vyavahāraniṣedhavyavahāropi khaṇḍitaḥ syāt | aprāmāṇiko vyavahāro 'vaśyaṃ svīkarttavya iti vā bhavet |
body.translated_text: The secret of contingency and its reverse (<s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s>)...... previously established...... the description obtained of non-momentary [entities] being excluded from the counter-thesis (<s>vipakṣa</s>). Additionally, there is the absence of evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for the establishment of the basis (<s>āśraya</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), and example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) — because the absence of evidence pertains to [what is] unreal (<s>avastu</s>), and because it is untenable for the chain of evidence-engagement to be false. If then [one argues] there is self-contradiction (<s>svavacanavirodha</s>) in [asserting] non-conventional-usage — [the reply is:] what [follows] from the self-contradiction? Would it show evidence for those [permanent entities], or would the conventional usage of denying conventional usage also be refuted? Or would it mean that non-evidential conventional usage must necessarily be accepted?

body.text: nādyaḥ-nahi virodhasahasreṇāpi sthire tasyakramādivira-(3)-he vā śaśaśṛṅge vā pratyakṣaṃ anumānaṃ vā upadarśayituṃ śakyaṃ tathātve vā kṛtaṃ bhautakalahena | dvitīyastu iṣyata eva pramāṇikaiḥ | avacanameva tarhi prāptaṃ kiṃ kurmo yatra vaca-(4)-naṃ sarvathaivānupannaṃ tatrāvacanameva śreyaḥ, tvamapi paribhāvaya tāvat | niṣprāmāṇike 'rthe mūkavāvadūkayoḥ kataraḥ śreyān pramāṇika iti |
body.translated_text: Not the first — for not even by a thousand contradictions can perception or inference be shown for a permanent [entity], or for one devoid of sequence etc., or for a hare's horn; and if such were [its] nature, what use is the quarrel about elements? The second, however, is accepted by those who [rely on] evidence. Then silence alone is arrived at. What can we do? Where speech is entirely untenable, there silence alone is preferable — you too, consider this for the time being. Regarding an object devoid of evidence, which is better — the mute or the loquacious — [who is more] authoritative?

body.text: evaṃ viduṣāpi bhavatā na mūkībhūya (5) sthitaṃ apitu vyavahāraḥ pratiṣiddha evāsatīti cet satyaṃ-yathā aprāmāṇikaḥ svavacanaviruddho 'rtho mā prasāṅkṣīditi manyamānena tvayi yo 'prāmāṇika-(6)-evāsati vyavahāraḥ svīkṛtastathāsmābhirapi pramāṇacintāyāṃ aprāmāṇiko vyavahāro mā prasāṅkṣīditi manyamānairaprāmāṇika eva svavacanavi-(7)-rodhaḥ svīkriyate | yadi tūbhayatrāpi bhavānsamānadṛṣṭiḥ syādasmābhirapi tadā na kiñciducyata iti | ḥ tṛtīye tvapramāṇikaścāpyavaśyasvīkartavyaśceti kasyeyamājñā iti bhavāneva (8) praṣṭavyaḥ | vyavahārasya sudṛḍhanirūḍhatvāditi cet-aprāmāṇikaśca dṛḍhanirūḍhaśceti vyāghātaḥ | kathañcidapi vyavasthitatvāditi cet-aprāmāṇika(9) ścennakathañcidapi vyavatiṣṭhate-prāmāṇikādivattadevocyatāmitivāde vyavasthā | ekameva jalpavitaṇḍayostu pramāṇapraśnamātravyavasyate svavacanavyāghātaḥ | tatra (10) pramāṇenottaramaśakyam ca, apramāṇena tūttare svavacanenaiva bhaṅgaḥ, madukteṣu praśnādiṣu pramāṇaṃ nāstīti svayameva svīkārāt anuttare tu aprati bhaiveti | yadi ca vyavahārasvīkāre virodhaparihāraḥ syāt asau svīkriyetāpi na tvevaṃ-na khalu sakalavyavahārābhājanañca tanniṣedhabhājanaṃ veti parasparamavirodhi(tam(2)cet) iti pareṇoktaṃ tadetatsakalamasaṅgatam-svavāgvādhābodhanayā hi vyāpakānupalambhāśrayādyasiddhimudbhāvayato 'doṣodbhāvanaṃ nāma nigrahasthānaṃ utthāpyate | (3) kathamiti cet-ucyate |
body.translated_text: Even by you who know thus, [the position] has not been maintained by remaining silent; rather, [you say:] 'Conventional practice (<s>vyavahāra</s>) is indeed prohibited regarding the non-existent.' If so, [we reply:] True — just as you, thinking 'Let not an invalid (<s>aprāmāṇika</s>) meaning contradicted by one's own words be spread,' have yourself accepted a conventional practice regarding the non-existent that is itself invalid; so too by us, thinking 'Let not invalid conventional practice spread in the investigation of means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>),' the self-contradiction of one's own words is accepted as itself invalid. But if you were of the same view in both cases, then we too would have nothing to say. As for the third [alternative] — 'that which is invalid must nevertheless be necessarily accepted' — whose command is this? You yourself are to be asked. If [you say] 'because conventional practice is firmly established' — [then there is] a contradiction: invalid and yet firmly established. If [you say] 'because it is somehow established' — if invalid, it is not established in any way whatsoever; let it be stated just as [the case of something that is] valid, etc. — [that is the] resolution in debate. In <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (destructive criticism), the one thing [that] is determined by the mere question of <s>pramāṇa</s> is self-contradiction of one's own words. Therein, a reply by means of <s>pramāṇa</s> is impossible; but with a reply by non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, there is defeat by one's own words, since one has oneself accepted that there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for the questions etc. stated by me; and without a reply, there is non-response [which is also defeat]. And if the removal of contradiction could [be achieved] by accepting conventional practice, let it be accepted — but it is not so. For 'one who is unfit for all conventional practice is not [thereby] a fit vessel for the prohibition of that [practice]' — [this assertion of] mutual non-contradiction stated by the opponent — all this is incoherent. For by [the opponent who], through the method of demonstrating the invalidity of his own words, raises the unestablishment of the substrate etc. of the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) — what is raised is [precisely] the point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) called 'raising a non-fault as a fault.' How? It is stated:

body.text: āśrayadṛṣṭāntādau pramāṇābhāva iti sādhyamadhyavasitam | avastuni pramāṇāpravṛtteriti heturāveditaḥ | pramāṇapravṛttāvalīkatvānupa(4)patteriti svābhiprāyeṇa upapattiḥ pratipāditā tathā cāśraye 'vaṣṭambhakapratipanne pramāṇena pramāṇāpravṛttilakṣaṇadharmasya dharmidharmmatvāvarodhe ca niṣpa-(5)-nne kathaṃ nāśrayādyasiddhibodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'There is an absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding the substrate, example, etc.' — thus the <s>sādhya</s> (thesis to be proved) has been determined. 'Because <s>pramāṇa</s> does not operate regarding a non-entity' — thus the reason (<s>hetu</s>) has been announced. 'Because the falsehood of the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> is untenable' — thus the justification has been presented according to one's own intention. And when the substrate has been acknowledged as established by the supporting <s>pramāṇa</s>, and when the inclusion of the property characterized by the non-operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> in the property-bearer has been accomplished — how can there not be an understanding of the unestablishment of the substrate etc.?

body.text: atha nāstyeva asiddhyādidoṣa parapramāṇasyāpyasiddhayā sādhanādau na sannidhānaṃ labdhavyamityāpātam | tathā ca tatpramā(6) ṇamevāpavādadaridratvāt | tataśca yattvayādūṣaṇamuktaṃ tatra dūṣaṇamiti adoṣodbhāvanaṃ nāma nigrahasthānamatastayorekataravādinirākaraṇāntā paryavasāna (7) mānītaivakatheti kiṃ paraṃ nirarthakavikalpatrayeṇa bhavitavyam | tathā hi kiṃ pramāṇamupadarśitaṃ bhavediti pramāṇamevāpadarśitaṃ nirdoṣatā visphuraṇāt svasādhanasya paroktāva-(8)-dyasya svavacanavicalanā bhrāntatvāt | avyavahārapratiṣedhavyavahārakhaṇḍanāpi svavāgbādhitavyavahārapratiṣedhasannidhānāyakā vastudharmmidharmasya ca pramāṇatvāt prativādinaḥ na (9) ca vyavahāraniṣedhavyavahāraheturapahastito haste 'nyastaśca vyavahārapratiṣedhavyavahāra iti hṛdayaṅgamaṃ janaṅgamasyāpi vyāpakānupalambhena vyāpyābhāvavyavahāraṃ vyavahārataḥ sudūramapakṛṣṭaprāmāṇikavyavahārāvaśyamaṅgīkaraṇam |
body.translated_text: Now, if there is absolutely no fault of unestablishment etc., [then] by the unestablishment of the opponent's <s>pramāṇa</s> too, presence in the proof etc. should not be obtained — this is the [unwanted] consequence. And thus, that <s>pramāṇa</s> itself, being devoid of counter-exception — and therefore, whatever refutation was stated by you therein, that very [refutation] is a refutation — [constituting] the point of defeat called 'raising a non-fault as a fault.' Therefore, the conclusion is that the debate is brought to an end by the refutation of one of the two disputants. What more — one must [inevitably] arrive at one of three meaningless alternatives. For thus: would a <s>pramāṇa</s> be shown? [Answer:] the very <s>pramāṇa</s> has been shown to be faultless, by the manifestation of the faultlessness of one's own proof and the wavering of one's own words regarding the faults stated by the opponent, because of [the opponent's] confusion. The refutation of the convention of prohibiting convention regarding non-conventional-practice too — because of the presence of the prohibition of convention invalidated by one's own words, and because the property of the property-bearer is a <s>pramāṇa</s> for the opponent — and the reason for the convention of prohibiting convention has not been set aside in the hand, while the convention of prohibiting convention has been placed in the hand — this [argument], penetrating the heart even of one who moves [restlessly], through the non-apprehension of the pervader, necessarily requires the acceptance of the convention of the absence of the pervaded, [a convention] far removed from valid conventional practice.

body.text: yatpunaruktaṃ nahi virodhasahastreṇāpītyādi tadapi svavacanavirodhānuruddhamavadhāryam | nitye 'vastuni pramāṇamupadarśayitu-(2) maśakyaṃ pratyakṣamanumānamiti kiṃ tvayā pratipannaṃ apratipannaṃ vā | pratipattirapi kiṃ pramāṇena apramāṇena vā | pramāṇena pratipatrau svavacanavyāghātaḥ | apramāṇena tu pratipattiraprāmā(3)ṇikasyaiveti mahatī vikṛtiḥ | na cāyaṃ bhautakalaha pramāṇasyavyāpakānupalambhasyaṃ darśitatvāt | dvitīyastviṣyata iti cāntarbhūtvā bhāsate janaḥ prāmāṇikaśceti avastuni vyavahāra-(4)-pratiṣedhavyavahārakhaṇḍanā kutaścetibruvantaḥ eva viśiṣṭa viṣayavyavahārapratiṣedhavyavahārakhaṇḍenāśabdenaiva tadviṣayapramāṇāpravṛtyā tadviṣayatvamuktasādhyasya duḥsamādhānam | avastuni (5) vyavahārapratiṣedhavyavahārakhaṇḍanāśabdavācyavyavahārapratiṣedhavyavahārapratiṣedhasamādhāne vā svavāgbādhā sannidhānaṃ āpadyante | prakṛtavādanidhanāvadyakaramiti kṛtārtho 'nu-(6)-palambhavādī niyatavyastatvāt prativādinaḥ | 'kiṃ kumo yatra vacanaṃ sarvathaivetyādi' yaduktaṃ tadapi svavacanaviruddhamanuruddhamanubaddhaṃ anupravartate | etadbhayādabhagatau vā kiñcidapratibhā-(7)-vānubhāskaraprabhāvānābhibhavabhūmirmavyasthāpīti nitarāṃ nistīrṇavyasanāntarovādī | tathāhi vyāpakānupalambhe punaḥ samutthāpyante prativādinī dūṣaṇā duṣkare 'bhāṣaṇabhāvabhājibhūte parāja-(8)-yabhūmirapratibhābhāvataḥ prabhevabhāsvataḥsādhujananiveśitaṃ sādhanaṃ prasādhanamevodyotayatīti labdha eva kathāvadhiḥ |
body.translated_text: As for what was further stated — 'Not even by a thousand contradictions' etc. — that too should be understood as constrained by the self-contradiction of one's own words. 'It is impossible to show a <s>pramāṇa</s>, whether perception or inference, for a permanent non-entity' — is this accepted by you or not accepted? Is that acceptance too [based] on a <s>pramāṇa</s> or on a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>? If accepted by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is self-contradiction of one's own words. If accepted by a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, then the acceptance belongs precisely to the invalid [domain] — a great distortion. And this is not a vulgar quarrel, because the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) has been shown as a <s>pramāṇa</s>. But if the second [alternative] is favored — then [the opponent] appears as one who, having entered within, [claims] 'People are authoritative' — from whence then [comes] the refutation of the convention of prohibiting convention regarding non-entities? [Those who] speak thus are [themselves refuted] precisely by the refutation, through the unspoken [implication], of the convention of prohibiting convention regarding a distinguished object — by the very non-operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding that object, the [nature of] that object of the stated <s>sādhya</s> is difficult to resolve. Or, in resolving the prohibition-of-convention-that-prohibits-convention-regarding-non-entities, [a prohibition] expressible through the word 'refutation,' they incur the invalidity of their own words. Because it constitutes a fault that terminates the debate at hand — the proponent of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) has achieved his purpose, because the opponent is necessarily defeated. 'What is the use where speech is in every way...' etc. — what was stated, that too follows, constrained by the self-contradiction of one's own words. From fear of this, or in the face of defeat, some [display of] non-response — the ground of being that is not overpowered by the radiance of the sun of non-response — 'let this be firmly established,' thus the disputant is thoroughly freed from the distress within. For thus, when the non-apprehension of the pervader is raised again, the opponent's refutations — when speech has become impossible, [entering] the ground of defeat through the state of non-response — from the very radiance of brilliance, the proof established among the good people illuminates [all], like an ornament. Thus the limit of the debate has been reached.

children.translated_text: Through the invalidity of his own words, perplexed, and fearing the loss of [his] brilliance,

children.text: abruvan avibruvan (9) vāpi vādī bhavati bhartsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether not speaking or speaking improperly, the disputant becomes rebuked.

body.text: yatpunaḥ svabhāṣābhaṅgibhirasaṅgatābhiraṅgīkaroti vyavahāraṃ na coktāvadyaṃ śrutisabhyaḥ praspandaṃ girāmityudbhaṇati | satyaṃ yathāprāmāṇikaḥ svavacanavi(10)ruddho 'rtha' ityādi tadapi śūnyasaṃśanaṃ praṃsanāpātram | svavacanaviraudhaviruddhatayaiva nātiprasakto vyavahārapratiṣedhavyavahāraḥ na punaḥ sa tathābhūto mā bhūdityayaṃ vyavahāro 'smākamanumataḥ kintarhi tadvyāpakavirahāt vyāpyaviraho vibhāgataḥ pramāṇānugataśca vyāpyavyāpakabhāvasvapramāṇasiddhatvāt tadvirahitasya cāvastusato dharmmiṇaḥ pratipannatvāt(2) asato 'tyadhikaraṇādivivakṣārūḍhakārakakalāsaṃkrāntakalevaratvātkathamaparathā sthūlaskhalitasvavacanabādhāvāruddhā vṛthānyāyavinmānino naiyāyikāḥ svavacanabādhehi svavacanaṃpramāṇaṃ bādhakaṃ ḍhaukitam | ataḥ kathamayamaprāmāṇikaḥ kathita iti ślathaya śūnyagranthigranthanārthitvam | tathā ca aprāmāṇikaḥ svavacanabādho 'bhyupagamyayamānopi tvayā svavāgbādhatvaṃ na jahāti nānumānaṃ pramāṇamiti-(4)-vit yadi tvabhyupagamādevādoṣatvamevamanyatrāpi astu avastuviṣaye 'siddhatvamabhyu pagacchāma iti vayamapi vadiṣyāmaḥ utpattyāpi jalpavitaṇḍe 'pi kathyata iti tatpakṣāpekṣayā (5) vivakṣitodoṣaḥ kṣipyate |
body.translated_text: As for what he further [states] — that he accepts conventional practice through the turns of his own language, [turns that are] incoherent, and 'the stated fault is not [real]; the cultured ear [would recognize] the movement of speech' — thus he proclaims. [But the statement] 'True — just as an invalid meaning contradicted by one's own words' etc. — that too is fit [only] for being cast into the void [of emptiness]. The convention of prohibiting convention is not excessively attached, precisely because it is contradicted by the self-contradiction of one's own words. But it is not [the case that] 'let not [such convention] exist in that form' — this convention is not approved by us. Rather, [we hold:] because of the absence of the pervader, [there is] the absence of the pervaded — this is established distributively, in accordance with <s>pramāṇa</s>, because the pervaded-pervader relationship is established by its own <s>pramāṇa</s>; and because the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) — a non-existent entity devoid of that [pervader] — has been acknowledged, being like [something predicated] of an extraneous locus (<s>atyadhikaraṇa</s>), with the [grammatical] body having passed into the artistic portion of the intended expression — how then, tripped up in their own gross stumbling, constrained by the invalidity of their own words, do the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, who pride themselves on knowing logic, [fare]? 'Invalidate by your own words! Your own words [as] the <s>pramāṇa</s> of invalidation have been brought forward.' Therefore, how is this called invalid? Loosen [your] eagerness for tying the knot of the void! And thus, even though the invalidity of one's own words is conceded — even as it is being conceded by you — it does not abandon the nature of being self-invalidating. 'Inference is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>' — [this is your] knowledge. But if from concession alone comes faultlessness, then let it be so elsewhere too — 'we accept the unestablishment regarding the object that is a non-entity' — we too shall say this. In <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> too it is stated — therefore, with regard to that thesis, the intended fault is cast.

children.translated_text: 'Of one who has engaged merely in asking about <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding the thesis etc.' — and so forth:
By that disputant (<s>jalpaka</s>), victory-minded, asking about <s>pramāṇa</s>,
[a debate] commenced from the conduct of [establishing] non-entities — that [questioning] does not succeed.
But when, through conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), that [questioning] is accomplished and the question has been put forward,
the original reason, having been given opportunity, would be the good [one] that manifests itself.

body.text: avastudharmī kutaḥ pramāṇāt prasiddhamiti bruvanneva avastudharminiṣṭhapramāṇapraśnaḥ tadasiddhau pramāṇataḥ (7) prāptānavakāśaḥ kāśatalalavaladhīyāniti kathaṃ na svavacanapratihataḥ | tathāhi viśeṣaviṣayapramāṇapraśnāt viśeṣaḥ siddhaḥ tadasiddhau tadviṣayavimarśāyogāt | siddhyabhyupagamevā ye-(8)-naiva vacasā paramacarodhvamadhurastenaiva svapakṣaṃ kṣiṇotīti kṣīṇaḥ kathaṃjalpavitaṇḍayorapi svavacanavyādhātaḥ | tadevaṃ bauddhena vyāpakānupalamme vyāpyābhāvārthamupanyaste kasyā-(9)mapi svavāgjarjarit jayo jāyate | na bhāṣate cet apratibhāṃ bhūribhūmimābhajatīti kṛtaṃ kāyavratena sabinaiva nyāyena avastvapi dharmisvānurūpadha-(10)-rmāpekṣayā svānurūpanirūpaṇaniṣṭhitaniḥ śeṣanijadharmaviṣaya iti abhyupagamyatām | ayaṃ sabhyāḥ tathāhi jīvati śarīre kṣetrajña saṃjñā upameyameyajñāpanāṅga prāmāṇadimatvaṃ nyastam | kevalavyatirekakīrtitavikramaḥ śrāvaṇatvasamaṃ mābhūditi sapakṣe tara syādeva vyāvṛttamiti varṇanīyatāsapakṣe(2)-satvamasyāpadyateti mṛṣodyaṃ vidyoteta | kevalavyatirekatvamasyeti pramuṣitamanḥparitoṣatayā sapakṣasyāvidyamānatvāt | tasminnasya sattvamaśastamupanyastamapahastanīyamitice-(3)-tayamānaḥ |
body.translated_text: The one who says 'from what <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) is the <s>avastu-dharmin</s> (unreal subject) established?' — by merely asking this question about the <s>pramāṇa</s> residing in the unreal subject, when that [subject] is unestablished, the one who claims that 'there is no scope [for proof] obtained from <s>pramāṇa</s>' — how is he not struck down by his own words? For indeed, from the question about a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose object is a particular, the particular is established, since without its establishment there can be no deliberation regarding its object. Or, if [the opponent] concedes the establishment, then by this very statement with which he attacks the other side, he destroys his own position — thus he is defeated. How then, even in <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (destructive debate), is there not self-contradiction of one's own words? Thus, when the Buddhist presents the absence of the pervaded through the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>), victory arises over any [opponent] whose own speech is already shattered. If he does not speak, he falls into the vast realm of loss of response (<s>apratibhā</s>) — so enough with this bodily vow! By this very reasoning, let it be conceded that even an unreal entity (<s>avastu</s>), with respect to properties appropriate to its nature as a subject (<s>dharmin</s>), is the object of all its own properties established through investigation appropriate to itself. O assembly! For thus: while the body lives, the designation '<s>kṣetrajña</s>' (knower of the field) is applied, and the property of being endowed with <s>pramāṇa</s> and such is posited as an instrument for making known the comparable and the measurable. [The opponent] whose prowess is proclaimed only through the method of <s>kevala-vyatireka</s> (pure negative concomitance) — lest it be equal to the [fallacious example of] '<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>' (audibility) — should be demonstrated as: 'in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (positive instance) it would indeed be excluded,' thus the presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> of what needs to be demonstrated would follow — let this false objection be illuminated! That this [inference] is purely negative (<s>kevala-vyatireka</s>) — [the opponent says this] with a mind robbed of satisfaction, because the <s>sapakṣa</s> does not exist. [The opponent] who thinks: 'its presence in that [non-existent sapakṣa] has been improperly presented and should be rejected' —

body.text: kiṃ sadbhāva bhaṃgenāsadbhūte prāṇādimattvasya sapakṣe sadbhāvavipakṣaṃ lakṣayati na cettarhi sadbhāvāsadbhāvaniṣedhavyavahāropi niṣedhavyavahāra eveti nivṛttiḥ kiṃ niṣidhyate | prā-(4)-ṇādimattvaṃ sapakṣasya vidyamānattvāt | na nivṛttamapādānatvasyābhāvāditi | sa eṣa vyavahāro naiyāyikasya vyatirekihetupratihatipratyūhananidāno dīpyate | na bauddhaprārabdhavirodhānurodhā-(5)-danubaddha iti bhaṇa guṇamayamanoharanītiṃ pramāṇapraharaṇasya kāñcit | yayā sapakṣo vikṣobhitavipakṣaprasaraḥ prekṣyairūpalakṣyate siddhadharmitayā tadāśritaścāyamavidyamā-(6) nattvaṃ nāma pakṣadharmatādhyastaṃ syāt | syāccāsyāpyanvayādyanuśaraṇamaṇīyasāpyaṃśitvaramaṇīyaṃ yadavidyamānaṃ na tacchaktisamākhyātakāranibandhanasuvarṇādipadaprāsāda-(7) dhavaladakṣam, tadyathāntarikṣabalakṣajalajajālam | akālajaladharadhīradhvānaṃ nedānīṃ vyāyanītinipuṇaprasādhyamārabdhaprameyabodhopāyamanapāyamāpadeṣābhāvaprameyadarśamu-(8)-tkarṣitaroṣā parāpatati | asmādavismayaveśmāpraviśya praguṇopāyaṃ mānapratipīpadaḥ prasādhakaṃ pramāṇamabhāvaprameyasya vikalpamanalpābhāvavyavahāraparibhāvitasāma-(9) rthyamanarthakakadarthanaṃ kathākathācchādanena kiṃ tarayati prastutavyatirekakramam |
body.translated_text: Does he, by the destruction of real existence (<s>sadbhāva</s>), designate the <s>vipakṣa</s> (negative instance) as the real existence of the property of possessing life-force and such in the <s>sapakṣa</s> that has become unreal? If not, then even the conventional usage of negating the negation of real existence and non-existence is itself merely negation — what is being negated? [Nothing], because of the existence of the <s>sapakṣa</s> possessing life-force and such. It is not excluded, because there is no absence of being a ground of exclusion. This convention shines forth as the cause of obstruction to the <s>Naiyāyika</s>'s (logician's) attack on the negative-only reason (<s>vyatireki-hetu</s>). It is not bound by conformity or opposition to what the Buddhist has undertaken — so declare some meritorious and captivating principle of the weapon of <s>pramāṇa</s>, by which the <s>sapakṣa</s>, having disturbed the spread of the <s>vipakṣa</s>, is recognized by the discerning as having an established subject (<s>siddha-dharmin</s>), and this [property] called non-existence (<s>avidyamānatva</s>), resting upon that, would be superimposed as the thesis-property (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>). And there could also be a charming pursuit of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and other [relations] for this, delightful in its partial character — that which is non-existent is not capable of producing the splendid abode of words like 'gold' whose basis is the cause designated by power (<s>śakti</s>), just as a web of sky-flowers (<s>antarikṣa-jalaja-jāla</s>). The bold thunder of untimely clouds does not now fall upon [us], for the means of ascertaining the object of proof, being accomplished by those skilled in proper method, is unfailing and free from false attribution, and [the opponent], whose anger is surpassed by the demonstration of the object of proof as absence, comes falling down. Without entering this house of wonder, does the one who would honor [his own] measure (<s>māna</s>) with a well-prepared method — the <s>pramāṇa</s> that validates the object of proof as absence — the conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) whose capacity is pervaded by the usage of manifold absence, whose tormenting of the meaningless — does he cross the sequence of <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) under discussion by concealing the dialogue?

children.translated_text: This path has been traversed and not traversed in many ways by the logicians (<s>hetukāna</s>),
By those who examine here with the body, through the removal of the delusion of nectar,
In the thesis of the discourse of envy and anger, [this path is] capable of washing away examination,
In the thesis that momentariness (<s>kṣaṇakṣapyatva</s>) is real, let this <s>vipakṣa</s> (counter-instance) be observed.

body.text: evaṃ prameyatvamapi sakalakālakalāpavyāpisvabhāvaṃ śāśvatatvamanusaṃdhāya (sādhya sā) dhanau dharmiṇi kevalānvayamanumanyamānaṃ amunā (nyāyena) nā (na) yena nirvvahati |
body.translated_text: Thus, even the property of being an object of proof (<s>prameyatva</s>), contemplating permanence (<s>śāśvatatva</s>) — whose nature pervades the entire collection of time (<s>sakala-kāla-kalāpa</s>) — accepting purely positive concomitance (<s>kevalānvaya</s>) in the subject to be proved (<s>sādhya-dharmin</s>), does not succeed by this method (<s>nyāya</s>).

body.text: nanu cādhunā pi na dhunāti vākyaṃ svaparaparāmarśasāmyamasapakṣanyāyasya nyāse viśeṣaṇaṃ manasi ha prāptakālamavā(2)lasya pramāṇavyāpārasparśanena tatra kama bhāṇīt guṇīguṇaḥ bahubādhāvidhopi tarkopaniṣadanavadyavidyācāryakīrti(dharmakīrti) kīrtipramāṇavyāpāraparipālanamiha nidānaṃ mudaḥ prāmāṇikam (3) asti ca abhāvavibhāvanāvibhuḥ prabhutapramāṇavyāpāraḥ pīrasphuṭā pi paṭubhirapi nāraṭitaḥ pratyarthijanābhyarthanayā niḥpramathanaṃ kathyate |
body.translated_text: But even now, one does not shake the statement — when the equal applicability of self-referential and other-referential deliberation is posited as the rule of the absence of <s>sapakṣa</s>, the qualification [that comes] to mind has arrived at the proper time for one who is not lazy, and by the touch of the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s>, whatever may be said there — the virtuous one endowed with qualities, even though obstructed by many objections — the fame of <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Dharmakīrti</s>, the teacher of blameless knowledge, the secret doctrine of reasoning (<s>tarkopaniṣad</s>), the protection of the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the authentic cause of joy here. And the one who is mighty in the manifestation of absence (<s>abhāva-vibhāvanā</s>), whose operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> is extensive — even though not entirely clear, even by the sharp-witted is not refuted — by the entreaty of the opposing party, the complete refutation is declared:

body.text: rūpābhāvādabhāvasya śabdorūpābhidhāyinaḥ | (4)
body.translated_text: Because of the absence of form (<s>rūpa</s>), the words that denote the formless [nature] of absence,

body.text: na śakyā eva siddhāste vyavacchedasya vācakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Cannot possibly be established as those [words] that express exclusion (<s>vyavaccheda</s>).

body.text: abhāvapramāṇavedyo 'bhāva iti bhaṭṭabhāvamabhibhūya viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvabhāvasannikṛṣṭābhāvamakṣajapratyaya-(5)-pratyājyaṃ taccāsyākṣapā damatam | tatparicchinatti tato 'nyadvyavacchinatti tṛtīyaprakārābhāvañca sūcayatītyekapramāṇavyāpāra eṣa iti narasiṃha siṃhāsanārūḍha prau-(6)-ḍhaprāmāṇikacakracūḍāmaṇivacanaratnaṃ yatsataḥ śrūyatām |
body.translated_text: <s>Abhāva</s> (absence) is cognized by the <s>pramāṇa</s> of absence — thus, having overcome the view of <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> [<s>Kumārila</s>], the absence closely connected with the existence and non-existence of the qualifier and the qualified (<s>viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣya</s>) — that which is to be rejected by sense-perception (<s>akṣaja-pratyaya</s>) — and that is its intolerant nature. That [<s>pramāṇa</s>] delimits that [absence], excludes what is other than that, and indicates the third type of absence — this is a single operation of <s>pramāṇa</s>. Thus, O <s>Narasiṃha</s> seated upon the lion-throne, let this jewel of speech be heard, which is the crest-jewel of the proud circle of authoritative logicians (<s>prāmāṇika</s>)!

body.text: atra hi prasaṅgaviparyayanirvāheṇa pūrvāparāvasthayorvyavasthāpito vastubhedaḥ sa evānityatā śabdavācyatā (7) tathā ca svabhāvādavasthyamanityatāṃ vrūma iti vacanam | sa cāntaraṃ prāgabhāvaṃ pradhvaṃsaṃ ca sāmākhyāto vastubhedaḥ prasiddhyati yena pramāṇena kṣaṇaparyavasānabhajanabhāvena kṣaṇa-(8)-bhaṅgabhāṣayā bhaṇitaḥ tenaiva tadviparītamapi nityatvamakṣaṇikatvaṃ ca siddhipaddhatimadhyārūḍhaṃ jāyate | tasya paricchidyamānādanarthāntaratve tattvena vilokane syādata-(9)-tve tataḥ pṛthagavasthānavyavasthānamamunaiva pramāṇena paricchindatā tṛtīyaprakārāpakāraśca kalitaḥ | tatpunaḥ pramāṇamācāryapādairdarśitam | antyakṣaṇadarśināṃ niścayāditi pratyakṣam | tathā-
body.translated_text: For here, the difference between entities (<s>vastu-bheda</s>) has been established between the prior and posterior states through the method of <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s> (reductio and its converse) — that itself is impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>), expressible by words. And thus the statement: 'we declare impermanence from [the thing's own] nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) as [its] non-persistence.' And that difference of entities, identified as the interval — prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) and destruction (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>) — is established by whichever <s>pramāṇa</s> expressed it in the language of momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇa-bhaṅga</s>), taking the form of belonging to the conclusion of a moment (<s>kṣaṇa-paryavasāna</s>); by that very [<s>pramāṇa</s>], the opposite too — permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) and non-momentariness (<s>akṣaṇikatva</s>) — comes to ascend the path of establishment. When, upon examining in truth its non-difference from what is being delimited, there would be identity, then the determination of separate states distinct from that — delimited by this very <s>pramāṇa</s> — also calculates the removal of the third type [of absence]. Furthermore, that <s>pramāṇa</s> has been shown by the revered <s>Ācārya</s> [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>]: 'From the certainty of those who perceive the final moment' — this is direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Likewise —

children.translated_text: In some cases, the non-recognition of that [destruction] is due to the possibility of [another] similar [thing arising],
Due to the error of one who does not see the difference, like the difference in magical balls (<s>māyā-golaka</s>).
For thus, seeing [a thing that is] without a mark (<s>aliṅga</s>), immature (<s>ābāla</s>), with no subsequent arising connected [to it],
A person indeed determines [it as] perishing, like a lamp (<s>dīpa</s>) and so forth.

body.text: tathā sarva hi pradeśamarthāntaraṃ adhvānaviviktamupalabdhavataḥ sa yena yena asāreṇa tadasāraṇatāṃ tato bhedamabhilapantī smṛtirūtpannā pratyakṣabalenetyā-(3)-dinā tatra tatra saśūnyaṃ vacaḥ tadihāpi nityatvamanityatāgrāhipramāṇena svapremayādvahirbhāvabhāgismaraṇajanadvāreṇa ātmavyāpāraṃ vyavahāratathatāvatāritaniścayaṃ vipaścitaḥ pa-(4)ritaḥ paritoṣayato yathā salilaṃ salilajasya nidānamadīnamānasena pramāṇasanāthena sthāpayitvā salilasarojabījasvabhāvamabibhrato 'bhūto na bhrājate bhāvato bhāvo bārijanye (5)-ti kāraṇābhāvena kāryamasaditi pratipipādayiṣā paravaśasyākāśadeśe pi ya śabdaprayogo rogamiva bhāvamaspṛśan abhāvābhidhāyī nāśaṅakya eva sadbhāvavibhāvakṛt-(6)-na cāpramāṇapūrvakaḥ svayamapramāṇamapi smaraṇasamarthitapadārthasārthavadayamapipramāṇapraṇīta evāṅgīkaraṇīyaḥ | tathā suprasūtaḥ svannarūnna-(7)-tanītinimnenāmnoto yenaiva mānena manasvinā satā tenaiva bandhyāsūnuśabdo viniveśitaḥ nāśaṃkā taṅkena tarkate bhāvacanopamiti balābalambīvyavahā-(8)-ro 'mbudasaṃvṛtadigantare vā pi pramāṇayitavyo nāmānyathā prasthānaṃ paripanthividhirūpeṇa tu pramāṇapraṇayānusaraṇakāraṇako 'yamakāṇḍacaṇḍaḥ kolāhalo (9) lokālokamākramatīti kimatra kurmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Likewise, for one who has perceived every location as something different, distinct from [other] times — from whatever is inessential, the memory arises declaring its inessentiality and hence difference from that, by the force of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and so on. In the same way here too, impermanence — through the door of recollection belonging to the external aspect, born from the <s>pramāṇa</s> that grasps both permanence and impermanence, arising from one's own object of proof — its own operation, the certainty brought down to the level of conventional reality (<s>vyavahāra</s>), fully satisfying the wise on all sides, just as water is the cause of what is born from water — having established [this] with a mind that is not feeble, supported by <s>pramāṇa</s>, [this certainty], bearing the nature of the seed of the water-lotus, does not shine forth as an unreal entity; from existence, existence arises in what is born from water — thus by the absence of the cause, the effect is non-existent: this is what is desired to be demonstrated. Even the usage of words applied in the realm of space (<s>ākāśa</s>), which is under the control of another, not touching existence like a disease, denoting absence — this should not at all be suspected as producing the manifestation of real existence, nor is it without a prior <s>pramāṇa</s>; even though not itself a <s>pramāṇa</s>, like a group of objects whose meaning is supported by memory, this too must be accepted as guided by <s>pramāṇa</s>. Likewise, well-produced, by the channel of policy not lowered from its own standard — by whatever measure (<s>māna</s>) an intelligent and virtuous person [has established things], by that very [measure] the word '<s>bandhyāsūnu</s>' (son of a barren woman) is applied. There is no doubt that reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) thinks the expression of existence [is problematic] — thus the convention of strength and weakness, even in a region where the horizon is covered by clouds, must be validated by <s>pramāṇa</s>; otherwise, the course [of argument] takes the form of an obstacle, but this one, whose cause is the pursuit of devotion to <s>pramāṇa</s>, this fierce and untimely uproar pervades the world of light and darkness — what can we do about it?

body.text: tadeva,
body.translated_text: That very [point] —

children.text: nityaṃ nāsti na vā pratītiviṣayaṃ tenāśrayāsiddhatā,
children.translated_text: The permanent does not exist, nor is it an object of cognition; hence there is the unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddhatā</s>) [fallacy],

children.text: hetoḥ svānubhavasya cākṣatirataḥ kṣiptaḥ svapakṣo 'pi ca |
children.translated_text: And the impairment of one's own experience as a reason (<s>hetu</s>); therefore one's own thesis (<s>svapakṣa</s>) too is cast aside.

children.text: śūnyaṃ ca dvitayena sidhyati na vā (10) sattāpi sattā yathā,
children.translated_text: Emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>) is established by both [arguments], or else even existence itself, just as existence [is established],
The establishment of contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) with the permanent is not possible through non-existence, nor through sequence and the like.

body.text: iti doṣa saṃgrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the collection of faults (<s>doṣa-saṃgraha</s>).

body.text: atrāmī evaṃ paryananujyante,

children.translated_text: When the establishment by <s>pramāṇa</s> of some property in an unreal entity [is questioned],
Is there or is there not here a [valid] obstruction (<s>bādhā</s>) or a positive conventional usage (<s>vidhi-vyavahṛti</s>)?
If it exists somewhere, how do these refutations (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>) not apply?
And if it does not exist at all, then the establishment of self-contradiction (<s>svavacana-pratirodha-siddhi</s>) [follows].

body.translated_text: Here these [faults] are examined in this manner:

children.translated_text: Therefore, in the dissimilar example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>), the necessary substratum is not desired here;
and from the statement 'in the absence of that, that does not [exist]' too, the same conclusion [follows].
But that [property-bearer], established through conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>) arisen from beginningless latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>),
the property-bearer (<s>dharmī</s>), threefold as word and meaning, resting on existence, non-existence, and both —
when existence is not taken up in that [property-bearer], the non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) of this is the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>).

body.text: tathā heturna tasyaivābhāvaḥ śabdaprayogataḥ
body.translated_text: Likewise, the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is not the mere absence of that, [but is established] from the employment of the word.

body.text: asaṃkhyāto hi viṣayaḥ sarvabhāvadharmmanivṛttīnāṃ vyavahārāyābhāvānurūpadharmavi-(4)-dhīnāṃ sarvopāravyāvirahalakṣaṇābhāvo bhāvayitavyo yathoktaprakramaprasādhitasamastapramāṇavyāpāratayā pramāṇikajanasamāśvāsaviśvambharābhūtaḥ tathā (5) na sapakṣo 'sapakṣaḥ tato 'nyastadviruddhastadabhāvaścetyapi paramasutarāmanayā rītyāgatamānuṣaṅgikam | prastute punarupadiśāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the domain is uncountable — of the cessation of all properties of all entities, for the sake of conventional practice, of rules of properties conforming to absence — absence characterized by the lack of all subsidiary [obstructions] is to be contemplated, through the operation of all means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) established in the manner stated, having become the ground of confidence for the community of epistemologists. Likewise, [what is] neither a positive instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) nor a negative instance (<s>asapakṣa</s>), nor something other than those, nor the contrary of that, nor the absence of that — even this has been most easily reached incidentally by this method. In the matter at hand, we shall now instruct.

body.text: yadi ca vyāvahārasvīkāre virodho parihāraḥ syāt (asau svīkriyetāpi, na tvevam), na khalu sakalavyavahārābhājanañca tanniṣedhavyavahārabhājanañceti vacanaṃ parasparamavirodhīti,-yaduktaṃ tadvālenāpi durabhila(7)pam | abhāvo hi dharmī svānurūpapramāṇavyāpārānusārī syātte pratyayapratiṣṭhāpitaḥ svasminnasaṃbhāvinā ca bhāvadharmeṇa vimuhyamāno vyāpakānupalambhena sambhā-(8) vitaḥ | tatkimucyate na khalu sakalavyavahārābhājanañcetyādi avastuno 'vastusamucitadharmavidhivyavahāragocaratayāpīṣyata eveti nābhyupagaṇa eva do-(9)-ṣāyeti śeṣa prabandho 'pi niḥsāratayādambhārambhāstambhasambhāvanāṃ bibharti | bandhyāsutaśabdena ca svabhāva evocyate ityuktam | tatastadanubandhane prabandho bandhya(10)tvaṃ pratisaṃvidhātavyam | yatpunaruktam kiṃ vaktṛttvavivaktasyāvastuno niyameno pālambhāt | āhosvidvastu tadviviktasyā-(vaktṛtvasya)-nupalambhāditi tadapi pātayitvā vasuṃtata vadanātītamitivat bhautavacanasvarucigocaraḥ | carācaravipaścitāmiti ciraṃ cintanīyaṃ cetanena | tathāhi niyatarūpāt bhavabhāvitabhāvābhāvavidhipratiṣedhavikalpapramāṇavyā (2)pāraparicayādyathā paryanvasitaṃ tathā sthāpitameva prāgiti susthatā bhāvataiva stheyā | tasmāt pramāṇameva sīmā viṃdhipratiṣedhāvyavasāyaniyamasyetyupasaṃhāro bhāva-(3)-tkaḥ sarvasmai svadate nirvyūḍhaśca yaḥ punarvikalpamātramādāya asatkhyātiranyathākhyāti ritivā vicāraprakrama vaso 'pi na prakṛtānurūpaḥ niyatānubhavo hi vika-(4)lpānāṃ pravartayitā |
body.translated_text: And if contradiction were the remedy through the acceptance of conventional usage (even if that were accepted, it is not so) — the statement 'it is not a vessel of any conventional usage whatsoever, yet it is a vessel of the conventional usage of its negation' is not mutually non-contradictory — what was said [to this effect] is difficult to articulate even by a child. For the property-bearer 'absence' (<s>abhāva</s>) follows the operation of the means of valid cognition conforming to itself and is established by [its own] conditions; and being confounded by an entity-property that is impossible in itself, it is countenanced through the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>). Why then is it said 'it is not a vessel of any conventional usage whatsoever' and so forth? Since the non-entity (<s>avastu</s>) is accepted precisely as being within the scope of the conventional practice of rules of properties appropriate to a non-entity — it is not the case that the [mere] acceptance itself is the fault. The remainder of the treatise too, being without substance, sustains the expectation of the pillar of ostentatious display. And it has been said that by the word 'barren woman's son' (<s>bandhyāsuta</s>), essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) itself is denoted. Therefore, in the continuation thereof, the treatise should attend to the barrenness [of the argument]. And what was further said — 'Is it from the non-apprehension of a non-entity that is restricted to having speaker-hood? Or from the non-apprehension of speaker-hood isolated from the entity?' — having cast that aside too, like [a statement] transcending the face of <s>Vasundharā</s>, it falls within the scope of one's own taste for material speech. 'Of the wise among the moving and the unmoving' — this is to be long contemplated by the conscious [thinker]. For thus: from the determinate form, from the familiarity with the operation of the means of valid cognition [concerning] conceptual constructions of positive and negative rules regarding the presence and absence of states cultivated through existence — as it was investigated, so it has been established previously — well-being (<s>susthatā</s>) should be maintained through the very nature [of things]. Therefore, the means of valid cognition itself is the boundary of the restriction of the determination of positive and negative rules — this conclusion, [arising] from the nature [of things], is agreeable to all and has been thoroughly demonstrated. And whoever, merely taking up conceptual construction, [proclaims] the cognition of the unreal (<s>asatkhyāti</s>) or the cognition of the otherwise (<s>anyathākhyāti</s>) — though subject to the method of investigation, [this person] does not conform to the matter at hand. For the determined experience is the impeller of conceptual constructions.

children.translated_text: And the distinctions of pleasure, pain, and so forth
are specifically of those [conceptual constructions] alone, dependent on the dullness and sharpness of that very cognition.

body.text: iti nyayādavidyānubhavavāsanāsanāthavikalpajālama (5) nāhatamūlamiti | na ca tāvataiva vāsanāta eva nikhilalīlādijananamastviti svasthaṃ manaso vacanamucitam, jñānajo jñānahetuśca vāsaneti, arthajo (6)'rthahetuścetyupalakṣaṇāt kinnākhyāyate | atha prasādhakapramāṇasambhavādityuttaramatrāpi samānam | pramāṇastu na pañjaritabhāvāvikalpajāla-(7)-manalasāḥ paśyantaḥ śabdayoniḥ vikalpo vikalpayoniśca śabda iti saṃketavyavahārakālamilitānāvilavikalpajāladurjaṭitavidhipratiṣedhavaddhacakṣubandhutvā(8)sta (tta) tvānusāriṇaḥ sarve parinirvṛtāḥ kimaparaṃ parāmarśaprasaraste taniṣyati |
body.translated_text: Thus, by this logic, the net of conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpajāla</s>) — sustained by latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) [arising from] the experience of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — has an unuprooted root. Nor is it appropriate for a calm mind to say 'by latent impressions alone, the production of all play-like [appearances] takes place' — since the latent impression is born from cognition and is a cause of cognition, and is born from objects and is a cause of objects — this being an indication [of their mutual dependence], why is this not stated? If [it is said] 'because of the possibility of establishing means of valid cognition' — the same reply [applies] here too. But the means of valid cognition — those who, seeing the net of conceptual constructions as not caged in the nature of entities, [understand that] 'conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) is the source of words, and words are the source of conceptual construction' — [these persons,] following the truth of the eye-binding [spell] of positive and negative rules tightly knotted by the impure net of conceptual constructions, closed at the time of conventional agreement (<s>saṃketa</s>) — all are completely at rest. What further extension of reflection will come to pass for them?

body.text: eka pratyavamarśākhye jñāne ekatra hi sthitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the cognition called reflective awareness (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>), [which is] one, situated in a single [object],

body.text:
prapattā tadataddhetūrthān vibhajate svayam(9)
tadbuddhivartino bhāvān bhāto hetutayā dhiyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: having reached that, it discriminates by itself the meanings [that are] causes of 'that' and 'not-that'; entities abiding in that cognition, being manifest as causes of cognition,

children.translated_text: deficient in the form of non-cause, appearing as if having multiple forms by themselves,
are cognized through differentiation — this statement is employed [to establish] difference.

body.text: iti sakala puroktāvadya pra-(10)-cchādanapūrvaikasaṅketakaraṇanyāyaḥ | ekapratyavamūlajanananidānamapi darśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus the method of making a single conventional agreement (<s>saṃketa</s>) by first concealing all that was previously stated [has been shown]. The root-cause of the generation of single reflective [cognition] has also been demonstrated.

children.translated_text: In establishing a single object from the cognition of the meaning of a single reflective awareness,
even in [the case of] difference, some [entities] are restricted by their essential nature, like the sense organs and the like.

body.text: ityetena pratisandhānamapi sabāhyābhyantarabhāvayoratadvyāvṛttaikārthakriyākāritvalakṣaṇaikatvaviṣayaṃ tadevaṃ bandhyāsutaśabdenātyantābhāva ucyate | (2) tatproktanyāyasamānatvāt |
body.translated_text: By this, the reconnection (<s>pratisandhāna</s>) too, having as its object the unity characterized by a single causal efficacy (<s>ekaarthakriyākāritva</s>) that is exclusion from non-that (<s>atadvyāvṛtti</s>), pertaining to both external and internal entities — thus by the word 'barren woman's son,' absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>) is denoted, because of the similarity with the reasoning previously stated.

children.translated_text: The parts of the head are concave, devoid of growth and hardness;
in the form of a hare's horn (<s>śaśaśṛṅga</s>) and the like, that is accepted as absolute absence.
Likewise, this too is to be stated:
The belly of the barren woman is concave, devoid of growth and hardness;
in the form of a barren woman's son (<s>vandhyāsuta</s>) and the like, that is called absolute absence.
Through the doctrine of such-and-such absence, by the force of corresponding latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>),
cognition arises in that [case] — its non-cognition is not [the cognition] of another.

body.text: yādṛśī śemuṣī paramā (4)rthastadabhāvavāde tādṛśī cedākāraviśeṣaśālinī, avidyānubhavavāsanāvāde tadā svasvabhāvamadhyamagnatayā parasparaparicayacyuticarcāṃ cārūccāryate | pratiniyatatvārū-(5)-patvādeva cābhāvākāra niścayasya vyavahārāṅgatā | yathā saṃsāraḥ tathā na tadabhāvalakṣaṇo mokṣaḥ praṇidhātā sātānubhavanabhavanamiti bhavyavyavahāriṇāṃ pa-(6)-ddhatiranurudhyatām |
body.translated_text: Whatever supreme cognition (<s>śemuṣī</s>) [there is] — in the doctrine of the absence of the ultimate, if [the cognition] is such, possessing a distinctive form — in the doctrine of latent impressions from the experience of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), then, because of being submerged in its own essential nature, the discussion of the loss of mutual familiarity is beautifully articulated. And precisely because of the determinate form, the certainty of the aspect of absence has its role in conventional practice. Just as <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), so too <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is characterized by the absence of that, is not to be meditated upon as the experience of that [saṃsāra] — let the method of those who engage in worthy conventional practice be followed.

body.text: yaccoktam-ghaṭastāvatsvābhāvavirahasvabhāvaḥ pramāṇasiddhatādrūpyeṇa kadācidapyanupalambhāt | etāvataiva tadabhāvo 'pi ghātaviraharūpaḥ siddha iti (7) ceta na ghaṭābhāvasya tadabhāvavirahasvabhāvatvānabhyupagamāt | na cānyasvabhāvepramāṇagocare tadanyopi siddhaḥ syādatiprasaṅgāt | evaṃ bhūtāveva ghaṭatadabhāvau (8) yadekasya paricchittirevāparasya vyavacchittiriticeta | na cānyasya svabhāve ghaṭavat ghaṭābhāvasyāpi prāmāṇikatvānabhyupagame svabhāvādanavakāśāt pramāṇasiddhevahi (9) svābhāvāvalambanaṃ na tu svabhāvavādāvalambane naiva vastusthitiriti bhavatāmevāyaṃ tatra tatra jayadundubhiriti tadapi bhagnagrahavādimukhasukhavādanaṃ bhavato na te svabhāvālambanamavalambanavāsināpyetatkṛtam ghaṭaḥ paricchetavyo na vā ādye sāvadharaṇo 'nyathā vā, ghaṭa evāyaṃ nānyathā sthāpanīya iti cetparicchedaḥ tarhi karṣita eva pramāṇadvayāvegaḥ (2) atha na tathā tathāpi ghaṭaḥ paricchinno paṭa iti tadarthī nopasarpyedantikamasya na kim | taduktaṃ na hyayamanalaṃ paśyan analameva paśyati | iti kathaṃ yena salilārthī tatra na pravartete tyādi | tasmātprati-(3)-niyatapadārthānubhava evānvayavyatirekakalpanasya bījamityucyate | na tu svabhāvālambanavyavadhibodhānurodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: And what was said — 'A pot, to begin with, has as its essential nature the absence of its own [existence], because it is never apprehended in the identity-form established by the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). By this alone, the absence of the pot too, having the form of absence-of-pot, is established' — if [this is argued], no, because the absence of a pot is not accepted as having the essential nature of absence-of-that [pot]. And if [something has] an essential nature not within the scope of the means of valid cognition, then something else too would be established — because of the unwanted consequence of over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>). Thus the pot and its absence are precisely of such a nature [that] the determination of one is indeed the exclusion of the other — if [this is argued], [we reply]: in the non-acceptance of the absence of a pot — like the pot — as being within the scope of the means of valid cognition, because there is no room for the essential nature [of absence], [we say:] it is in the essential nature established by the means of valid cognition that the grounding on the essential nature [takes place], not in the grounding on the essential nature doctrine alone is the state of things [established] — this is indeed your own victory-drum here and there. But that too is the discourse of [one who utters] the pleasure-producing speech of a proponent with a broken grasp. You have not taken recourse to the essential-nature grounding — even one dwelling in the abode of grounding has not produced this [result]. [If asked:] should the pot be determined or not? In the first [case], with a determination; or otherwise. [If] 'this is indeed a pot and not otherwise' — if [that is the claim], then the determination draws the force of two means of valid cognition. If not so, even then, the pot having been determined, someone seeking that object would not approach [the pot thinking] 'this is a cloth' — is that nothing? As it was said: 'For one who sees this as fire does not see it merely as fire' — then how [is it that] one desiring water does not proceed there? And so forth. Therefore, the experience of a restricted object alone is said to be the seed of the construction of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), not the conformity to the awareness of the boundary of essential-nature grounding.

children.translated_text: From the experience of a single apprehension, [the thought] 'I do not apprehend this';
or 'I do apprehend' — of this constructed [cognition] is the arising.
This alone is the aggregate of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>) therein — namely, from the single apprehension,
through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), a pair of conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpayugala</s>) arises.
Those whose doubts are resolved [think] 'it is precisely thus, because it has been seen' —
they cannot be dislodged by the false utterances of opponents.

body.text: ghaṭavadabhāve 'pi svena rūpeṇa vidhirnāstīti bhaṇito nābhāvaḥ syādapi tu parasparābhāvavān | bhāva eveti | bhāva parasparābhāvabhaṅgaṃ vā bhavati vi-(6)śvambharāsambhāvye veti | bhavata eva dṛṣṭyā niṣṭaṅikatamidamanumatamasmākam | yādṛśastu parasparapratiṣedhasvabhāvastādṛśo bhāvagrāhiṇaiṣa bhāvaṃ niyamavantaṃ bhāvayatā (7) pratīta eveti kimatra chadmaneti bhaṇāmaḥ kalpanānirṇītameva trairūpyamityapi pāpīyaḥ vyāptyādau tṛtīyaprakārābhāvavirodhasādhakaprasaṅgādeḥ pramāṇasya praṇītatvāt | (8) na kevalakalpanopālambhatrayamabhyastasabhyanīterjanasya tasmātpramāṇamūlākalpanāpi smaraṇavatsamyagliṅgarūpāṇāṃ paryāptā | alamaphalamūlākalpanābhistasmātpra-(8)-māṇopapannarūpacayatvāt sthitametat |
body.translated_text: Even in the case of <s>abhāva</s> (absence) like the pot, it has been stated that there is no positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>) by its own form — it would not be <s>abhāva</s>, but rather a <s>bhāva</s> (positive entity) possessing <s>parasparābhāva</s> (mutual exclusion). [The opponent says:] 'A <s>bhāva</s> either undergoes the dissolution of <s>parasparābhāva</s>, or it does not — [both options are problematic] since the universal ground (<s>viśvambharā</s>) cannot accommodate [this].' This is precisely what is accepted by us, as established from your own perspective. But such is the nature of mutual negation (<s>parasparapratiṣedhasvabhāva</s>) — one who grasps <s>bhāva</s> has indeed cognized this very <s>bhāva</s> as possessing a fixed determination; so what deception is there in this? We say: the claim that <s>trairūpya</s> (triple characterization of the inferential mark) is established by mere conceptual construction alone is even worse, because the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) has been rigorously established to demonstrate the absence of the third type in cases of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) and so forth, leading to the consequence of proving a contradiction. The triple support of mere conceptual construction alone is not [sufficient] for a person trained in proper reasoning. Therefore, even conceptual construction grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s>, like memory, is capable [of establishing] the proper forms of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Enough with fruitless conceptual constructions — since the accumulation of forms is supported by <s>pramāṇa</s>, this stands established.

body.text:
'asanto 'kṣaṇikāḥ sarvekramākramavirodhataḥ' |
arthakriyāsamarthantu yat tadeva paramārtha sat |
'artha kriyāsamarthaṃ yat tadatra paramā (10) rthasat |'
body.translated_text: 'All non-momentary things are non-existent, due to the contradiction between sequential and simultaneous [causal action].' That which is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) — that alone is ultimately real. 'That which is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> — that here is the ultimately real.'

body.text: yataścārthakriyāsamarthaṃ yat tasmādakṣaṇiko amantaḥ (asammataḥ) | arthakriyāyāṃ kramayaugapadyavirodhāt | tadevaṃ kramayaugapadyābhāva eva bādhakaṃ pramāṇamupadarśitam vināśasya svaparahetutvaṃ parikarabandha eva aitenaitadapinirākṛtam |
body.translated_text: And since that which is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> [must be momentary], therefore the non-momentary is unaccepted [as real], due to the contradiction between sequential and simultaneous [modes] in <s>arthakriyā</s>. Thus, the refuting <s>pramāṇa</s> has been demonstrated precisely as the absence of both sequential and simultaneous [causal action]. The [question of] whether <s>vināśa</s> (destruction) is caused by itself or by another is merely a preliminary preparation — by this very [argument about <s>arthakriyā</s>], that too has been refuted.

body.text: yaduktamanena astu, tarhi dhruvabhāgitvena vināśasyāhetu katvasiddhekṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ na vikalpānupapatreḥ | taddhi tādātmyaṃ vā (2) nirupākhyatvaṃ vā tatkāryatvaṃ vā abhāvatvameveti vā sthitā vikalpā niṣedhyaniṣedhakayorekatvānupapatteḥ | nādyaḥ-upapattau vā viśvasya vaiśvarūpyānupapatteḥ |
body.translated_text: What was stated by the [opponent]: 'Granted, then if <s>vināśa</s> is established as causeless by virtue of belonging to the permanent category, <s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s> (momentary destruction) does not follow, because the conceptual alternatives are untenable.' For those alternatives are fixed as follows: [destruction is] either identity [with the entity], or characterlessness, or an effect of it, or simply <s>abhāvatva</s> (the nature of absence) — since the identity of what is negated and the negator is untenable. Not the first — even if it were tenable, because the diversity of the universe would be untenable.

body.text: nanu kālāntare (3)'rthakriyāṃ pratyaśaktirevāsya, nāstitā sā ca kālāntare samarthetaratvabhāvatvameveti cet-nanvayameva kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ tathā cāsiddhamevāsiddhena sādhayataḥ kaste pratimallaḥ | api ca deśā-(4)-ntarakālāntarānuṣaṅgiṇyasya nāstitā yadyayameva nūnamanakṣaramidamuktam, 'yadayameva deśāntarakālantarānuṣaṅgīti | yadi vā svadeśakālavat kālāntaradeśāntarayorapi nāstitāna-(5) nuṣaṃge 'stitvaprasaṃgaḥ | aśakteḥ kathamastu śakteḥ sattālakṣaṇatvāditi cet-atha ki kālāntarakāryaṃ prati svakāle 'śaktirasattvam | kiṃvā svakāryamapi pratikālāntare 'śaktirasatva-(6)-mādye svakāle 'pyasatvaprasaṃgaḥ tadānīmapi tasya tādrūpyāt | kālāntarakāryapratyevametaditi cet kimayaṃ mantrapāṭhaḥ, nahi yo yatrāśakta sa tadape (7) kṣayā nāstīti vyavahriyate | na hi rāsabhāpekṣayā dhūmo jagati nāstīti tatkasya hetoḥ | nahyaśaktasya svarūpaṃ nivartate iti | dvitīye tu kālāntarādhārā śaktiḥ vā nāśaktiḥ (8) kathaṃ tadātmikā | tadādhārā cet tadaivāsatvaprasaṃgaḥ ityādi phalavikalakalahalakalākaṭhorakolāhalavilasitam, hālikasyāpi hāsyaheturūpahāsitaṃ svamahimamaha(9)-nīyanītinikhilaniṣṭheva akṣikṣaṇakaṇakulinamamandaravispandasundaragirāṃ gīrvāṇagurugarimnāmārcāryāṇāmākarṇya vartanam | vināśakāraṇavicāraṇāyāṃ tathā(10) hi-
body.translated_text: If [the opponent says]: 'Its very incapacity for <s>arthakriyā</s> at another time is its non-existence, and that [non-existence] at another time is simply the state of being other than what is capable' — well, this is precisely <s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>! And thus, for one who proves the unproven by the unproven, who is your worthy opponent? Moreover, if this entity's non-existence is connected with another place and another time, then surely this has been said without a syllable's difference: 'that this very [entity] is connected with another place and another time.' Or alternatively, if there is no non-existence connected with other times and places as there is in its own place and time, then there would be the consequence of existence [everywhere]. If [you say]: 'How can there be [existence] for what lacks capacity, since capacity is the defining mark of existence?' — well then, is the incapacity at its own time with respect to an effect at another time what constitutes non-existence? Or is the incapacity at another time even with respect to its own effect what constitutes non-existence? In the first case, there would be the consequence of non-existence even at its own time, since it has the same character then too.
