If [you say] 'this applies only with respect to effects at another time' — is this a mere mantra recitation? For it is not the case that one who is incapable with respect to something is thereby said to be non-existent even apart from that [particular capacity]. For smoke is not said to be non-existent in the world merely from the standpoint of a donkey [which cannot produce it]. For the intrinsic nature of what is [merely] incapable [in one respect] does not cease to exist. In the second alternative, is the capacity based on another time a capacity or an incapacity? How can it be identical with that [entity]? If it is based on that [other time], then there would be the consequence of non-existence even then — and so on, this is a fruitless, harsh, tumultuous clamor of barren quarrel, a laughable spectacle that would make even a ploughman laugh, which we hear as the conduct of the venerable <s>Ācāryas</s> whose words are beautiful like the gentle trembling of Mount <s>Mandara</s>, weighty as the divine preceptors, in whom all established doctrine culminates. Now, in the investigation of the cause of <s>vināśa</s> —

body.text: sadasatpakṣabhedena śabdārthānapavādibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Through the division of existent and non-existent positions, by those who do not contradict the meaning of words —

body.text:
vastveva cintyate hyatra pratibaddhaḥ phalodayaḥ
arthakriyāsamarthasya vicāraiḥ, kiṃ tadarthinām ||
body.translated_text: It is the real thing itself that is examined here, where the arising of the result is invariably connected; of what use are [mere] analyses to those who seek <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy)?

body.text: ṣaṇḍhasya rūpavairūpye kāminyā kiṃ parīkṣayā ||
body.translated_text: What use is a beautiful woman's examination of the beauty or ugliness of a eunuch?

body.text: sa hi bhāvo 'bhāvovā śabdārthaḥ puruṣārthaṃ yadi kiñciduparuṇaddhi samādadhāti vā yathābhini-(2)-veśaṃ tattvāt | tadā tadātvasamīhitasampādanāhetutāsabhyūhe samīhamānaḥ samānaḥ tadvastvadhiṣṭhānīkaroti vitānacakracalanapariśramasya | atrāyaṃ naḥ padārthaḥ (3) pratibaddha iti tataḥ prastute 'pi vastunisvahastasthāpitaṃ nyāyī vihasto vahistokagopālāditaḥ | ko nāma nyāyanyāsamīdṛśamanalasaḥ samāśrayate | svahetuta eva te nimīlitavinaśvarasvabhāvo bhāvaḥ pratiniyatakālāyogaphalitaḥ prathamavaṃśaprabhavaprabhāvavanmudgaraguruprahārānehasi ghaṭakoṭiśakapālapatalamapahāya vilocanavicayenāpi (5) nirūpayatā vināśanāmno 'rthasyāvalokanāt tathā ca |
body.translated_text: For whether the meaning of the word is <s>bhāva</s> (positive entity) or <s>abhāva</s> (absence), if it in any way obstructs or accomplishes a human purpose according to one's conviction, then one who desires to ascertain the causal relation for accomplishing what is desired at that time makes that real thing the basis [of inquiry], [rather than enduring] the labor of moving the canopy-wheel. Here, this is our meaning: 'invariably connected' — therefore, even when the real thing is under discussion, the <s>Naiyāyika</s>, having placed [the matter] in his own hand, [stands] empty-handed, [no better than] a cowherd boy outside. What logician, worthy of the name, would resort to such a lax [method of reasoning]? The <s>bhāva</s> (entity), whose perishable nature is revealed through its own cause alone, yielding the result of connection with a determinate time, like [a pot manifesting] the power of the first bamboo-born [hammer] — you do not desire [to see that] even by searching with your eyes, setting aside the surface of pot-rim sherds, because of the non-perception of any entity called '<s>vināśa</s>' (destruction). And thus —

children.translated_text: First, this pot is seen falling; likewise the hammer is seen;
The collection of sherds is seen; but beyond that, no separate <s>abhāva</s> (absence) is seen.

children.text: tenābhāva iti śrutiḥ kva nihitā kiṃ vātra tatkāraṇam,
children.translated_text: So where is the received teaching (<s>śruti</s>) that [speaks of] '<s>abhāva</s>' placed? And what is its cause here?
Merely this row of sherds is seen, subject only to the hammer's own force.

body.text: adṛṣṭameva ca niṣeghakaṃ manamaśanasvabhāvama-(7)-paraṃ parāmṛśya niṣedhyamapi avyavasāya ghaṭapaṭaparṇavākhyamaparatvena vyavatiṣṭhamānamāha niṣedhyaniṣedhakayorekatvānupapatteriti | nahi vināśe koṭiśakalaśaka-(8)pālavalayavyatirekiṇi vināśakahetuprahatajanmani niṣedhakatvasupathaṃ tena vā vighaṭanaṃ ghaṭa-paṭa parṇavāde.........pratyakṣīkāritaṃ yena tanniṣedhyaṃ tataśca bhedopa-(9)-labdherlabdhavyo na cānayoraikyaṃ vicārakrurakrakacakartittaṃ yattarhi yuktitulābhalatādikaṃ sakalalokalocanālocitasvasvabhāvavyavasthitayātiparasparasminnānupra-(10)-viṣṭamiti bheda upapattau viśvasya vaiśvarūpyāpalāpaprasavaprasaṅgaḥ, pramāṇasaṃsargamaṅgīkṛtavataḥḥ tadviparyaye kathaṃ bādhakaḥ
body.translated_text: And having grasped a separate negating cognition whose nature is imperceptible as non-existent, [the opponent] states that the object of negation too — designated as pot, cloth, or leaf — exists as something separate, saying 'because the identity of what is negated and the negator is untenable.' But when <s>vināśa</s> consists of the array of pot-rim sherds and is not different from them, and when it arises from the cause struck by the instrument of destruction, the assertion that [this destruction] follows the proper path of being a negator, or that the pot-cloth-leaf thesis is dismantled by it — [all this] has been directly perceived [to be otherwise]. Therefore, from the apprehension of difference, [identity] is not to be obtained; nor is there unity between these two, which has been cut apart by the cruel saw of analysis. For whatever [there is] — the scale-beam of reasoning and so forth — each thing is established in its own nature as observed by the eyes of the entire world, not entering into one another, and thus difference is established. [Given this,] there would be the absurd consequence of denying the diversity of the universe. For one who has accepted the connection with <s>pramāṇa</s>, how can there be a refuter when the opposite [is proposed]?

children.translated_text: All <s>bhāvas</s> (entities), by their <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), are established each in their own nature;
Since they partake of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) through both their own nature and the nature of others;
Therefore, the distinctions of <s>jāti</s> (universals) are conceived as grounded in that
from which the exclusion of things arises, by one who apprehends those particular differences.

body.text: iti nyāyena svahetoḥ svarūpameva hi parasmāḥ danyarūpamutpattimāsannaṃ ātmānurūpapratibhāsamutpāditasvaparaviṣayaviṣayavidhipratiṣedhasmārtavikalpadvayadarśitavaśaṃ dala-(3)-pati dṛḍhadarppamapi samapyaita prasaṅgam | ....yathā śarkarānayāgnivalayarmmanarmmadādikaṃ hi nihitajanananibaṃdhanādhīnaniveśaveśamaśeṣasya śleṣayati hṛdaye parasparā-(4)-saṃkīrṇamarṇavāntamātmānamabhāvanāmānamapahastyāpi svarūpapratibhāsaprabhāvāt tadvadidamapi yadi pratipādayati | pratikālakalama vāptā niḥsaṃ(5)-saṃsargasaṃsargaḥ svargārgalagovargādikavastusvanidānadattadaśāvadhivibhratāvadhibhāvasvabhāvasambandhaṃ viparītāsamvandhabhārabhuvaṃbhavantaṃ hanta tadā kā te hāniḥ (6) śubhaśriyaḥ tadidamāyātamḥ-
body.translated_text: By this reasoning, the intrinsic form of a thing, arising from its own cause, being different in nature from another, approaching origination, having manifested a reflection conforming to itself, and having shown [itself] subject to the pair of conceptual constructions — positive and negative — regarding its own and other domains, generated by the <s>smārta</s> (memory-based) [cognition], subdues even a proud army commander, bringing this consequence to completion. ... Just as [the nature of things like] sugar, fire, the garland [of flames], or the <s>Narmadā</s> river and so on — established in a disposition whose foundation depends on the fixed arrangement of their origination — binds everything to the heart, [each maintaining] its own form unmixed with others within the ocean [of existence], [each] not bearing the name <s>abhāva</s>, yet by the power of manifesting its own form even while removing [others] — so too, if this [principle] is demonstrated [here]: at each moment, the connection with what is utterly free from connection is obtained, [each entity] bearing the relationship of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) with a limit of condition given by its own cause regarding things like heaven-bolt-cow-herd and the rest, sustaining the burden of the opposite non-relationship — alas, then what loss is there to your auspicious glory? This has arrived —

body.text:
bhāvaiḥ svabhāvasaṃsiddhā pṛthagātmavthavasthitiḥ |
svīkṛtairaparaṃ pīḍā vādināṃ mahatī hṛdi |
body.translated_text: The separate self-established existence of entities, each with their own nature, is accomplished by <s>svabhāva</s>; having accepted this, the great anguish in the hearts of [opposing] debaters is something else entirely.

body.text: vinaśyatīti vināśaḥ kartari bahulaṃ (7) vacanāt ghañ kṛtvāha tat hetvantarau jananahetusamutpattitaḥ vinaśvaratvaḥ padārthaḥ prajñapyate | vinaśanaṃ vināśa ityabhisandhāya punarasamarthasamāsaṃ samāveśaya-(8)-ti | na bhāvo bhavatītyuktamabhāvo bhavatītyapītyādinā kriyāpratiṣedhamātraṃ kriyā iti tathaiva pramāṇa pravṛtteḥ | astvayaṃ āyuṣmān | bhāvaḥ | dhvaṃsena vidhvastasamastārtha-(9)-kriyā ityavocadvācaspati sa evānarthanyāyasya nyāyasya vyākhyātā ākhyātavyaḥ kimīdṛśamākhyā tava āsīt |
body.translated_text: 'That which perishes' — thus <s>vināśa</s> (destruction) [is formed with] the <s>ghañ</s> suffix in the agent sense, as per the rule 'bahulaṃ' (frequently [used]). He says: the entity is designated as having a perishable nature arising from the origination through a generative cause other [than a destruction-cause]. Then, intending [the meaning] '<s>vināśa</s> means the act of perishing,' he introduces an improper compound. [The statement] 'It is not that <s>bhāva</s> exists, nor is it said that <s>abhāva</s> exists' — by such [expressions], what is merely the negation of an action is [understood as] the action [itself], since <s>pramāṇa</s> operates in just that way. Let this venerable <s>bhāva</s> be [as you say]. <s>Vācaspati</s> has declared: 'destroyed by <s>dhvaṃsa</s> (annihilation), with all <s>arthakriyā</s> demolished' — he, the very expounder of the doctrine of fruitless reasoning, should be called [to account]: was such a proclamation truly yours?

body.text:
dhvaṃso vastuvidherbalāt parighavat yadvā yathā śarkarā,
bhāvo 'sau tadavastha eva tu na yatkiñcitkarāstasya te ||
body.translated_text: <s>Dhvaṃsa</s> (annihilation), by the force of the real positive entity, acts like a bolt, or alternatively like sugar — that <s>bhāva</s> remains in just that state, for your [supposed destructions] accomplish nothing whatsoever.

body.text:
vyāpārāviratistataḥ kṣaṇinaye tattvādavarndhya katham,
deśākāravadasya hetuniyataḥ (2) kālo 'pi yatmānmataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Activity does not cease from that [entity]; in the momentarist view (<s>kṣaṇinaya</s>), how can [activity] be truly obstructed? Just as its spatial extent and form are determined by the cause, so too its time is held to be determined by [its own] nature.

children.translated_text: For those who hold that destruction (<s>vināśa</s>) is the birth of posterior annihilation (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>), by that [annihilation] too, since another destruction would arise—

children.text: tpāde nāśa parampareti vibhavedbhāvaḥ kadācinna saḥ |
children.translated_text: there would be an infinite regress of destruction — [hence] the entity would never exist.
If [one says] there is no cessation other than destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) — then how can the destruction of one [thing] by another [occur]?
Because in that [case] there is the perception of the [persisting] entity — [the reply is:] it is not so, because [the destruction] is declared to be unlike [complete] annihilation.

body.text:
'yadi ca tasminsamati vastvadarśanāt dhvaṃsākhya vastunibṛttirucyate, tadā-
nāśo mudgara (4) eva vastu śakalānyevāthaveti mitrapādairuktaṃ prasaṅgataḥ vyavahartavyarupāyāstu nivṛtterdeśakālākārādhārā ca vāriṇānurodho vyavahāraka pratiniya-(5) tapratibhāsatadviviktārthāntaradarśanākhyānupalambhanaprabhava vikalpātalpaśāyitayā tena tucchasya kīdṛśaṃ janmetyādi galapallavaprayāsaḥ phale phala (6) ruhetaḥ |
body.translated_text: And if it is said that when in that [same locus] the entity is not seen, the cessation of the entity called 'destruction' (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) is asserted — then destruction is the hammer itself, or else [only] the fragments are the entity — as stated by the venerable <s>Mitrapāda</s>. As a contingent [consequence], the means of convention [must be stated]; but the [conventional] cessation has its basis in spatial location, time, and form; and the accommodation of the conventional [designation] is dependent on non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) — arising from the definite appearance of what is excluded, the perception of a distinct object, and [their] absence — [all] reposing on the bed of conceptual construction. Therefore, the effort of 'what kind of birth can the utterly void have?' and such [objections] is as fruitless as [seeking] fruit from the cause of [another] fruit.

body.text:
tasmātpracyutimātrakaṃ vyavahṛteḥ pātraṃ prasajyāhvaya
bhūyo 'rthasya virudhyate na tu janistasyeti ki hetunā |
rodhādeva sakṛnna tadvyavahṛtirhetu kṣayānnodayo |
rodhastātvika eva tāttvikamithaḥ svābhāvyabhaṅgasthiteḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, mere falling away (<s>pracyuti</s>) is the object of convention, called '<s>prasajya</s>' [absolute negation]; the [further] birth of the entity is contradicted, but not by what reason? Only from obstruction [does convention arise] — once [established], there is no convention for that [entity]; the cause is not the arising from the cessation of the cause. The obstruction is ultimately real, for the mutual collapse of essential natures is itself ultimate.

body.text: tasmādyo ho samagrātmā hetuḥ sa svakāryamupārjayan naśvarabhāvālaṅkṛtamupārjayati niyatānehaskamasya punarapara(4) smānnivṛttidharmā svabhāvo na janmahetoriti |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the cause whose nature is the aggregate (<s>samagra</s>), in generating its own effect, generates [it as] adorned with a perishable nature — [this is] invariable and effortless. Moreover, the nature whose property is cessation from another [state] is not the cause of birth.

children.translated_text: Having generated a perishable [effect], that cause is the destroyer of the other [prior entity];

children.text: tameva naśvaraṃ bhāvaṃ janayedyadi kiṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if it were to generate that very perishable entity [again], what would happen?

body.text:
kṣaṇamapyanapekṣatve bhāvo bhāvasya neti cet
bhāvo hi sa tathābhūto 'bhāve bhāvastathā katham ||
body.translated_text: If [one says] there is no dependence of entity upon entity even for a moment — [the reply is:] for that entity exists as such; if in [its] non-existence, how can the entity be such?

body.text: tena 'yasyā sāmagrayā yatkāryaṃ tattadariktānapekṣamiti sādhanārthaḥ tadirma ko nāma nānumanuta kārya mevatu vināśa iti | kenānurodhena vyavahartavyaṃ kiṃ tadvirahavatvāt kāryasya | nādyaḥ, sahakāriṣvapi tathā vyavahāraprasakteḥ | virahasvarūpānirukteścetyā (2) di | yathā mukhasukhamanabhimatārthamādāya dāridrayādyupetā dṛṣṭabalamiti durmanasthāya tandrāmandirasaṃmadaparispandakandalitamanoharaḥ manorājyaḥ niyatakālātmanā janma (3) janmavatpareṇa niveśito bisaprasūnādivaditi darśitaiva nirukti tāṃ punarapya kṣaṇasthitidharmatāṃ svabhāvaḥ | svahetoreva tathotpatteḥ paśyannapimandabuddhiḥ | saho-(4)-palambhena sarvadā tadbhāvasaṅgavipralabdho na vyavasyati sadṛśāparāparotpattiḥ | vipralabdho vā antyakṣaṇadarśanāḥ niścayān | paścādasyānupalabdhyā vāsthiti (5) (ra) (pratipatteḥ) | niścayakāla iti | tadā anityatā vyavasthāpyate | kāryotpādanaśakteḥ kāraṇasvabhāvatve 'pyadṛṣṭatatkāryakaraṇadarśane yadi-(6)....prasiddhatadbhāvasya kāryadarśanāt tatpratipattivat | ityevamativiśadavibhramabhrājisvābhiprāye 'pi yaścaratā pratisapramāṇakaṃ prakaṭite kledamatidīnamudritaṃ (7) udayanasya pratyāspadaṃ udīkṣate-
body.translated_text: Therefore, 'by whatever aggregate whatever effect is produced, that [effect] does not depend on anything other than that [aggregate]' — this is the meaning of the proof. Who would not infer this? Let there be destruction rather than [mere] effect. By what rationale should convention be conducted? Is it because the effect possesses the absence of that [cause]? Not the first, because such convention would follow for the auxiliary conditions too. And because the essential nature of absence is unexplained... Just as one who, seizing an undesired meaning with ease of speech, endowed with poverty etc., [is like] one who, thinking 'the evidence is seen,' becomes dejected — [so this] delightful kingdom of the mind, whose stirring buds of intoxication sparkle in the palace of lethargy, [is such that] birth is established by the cause as having a nature of momentary duration, placed [in sequence] by another possessing birth, like a lotus-fiber flower etc. — thus the explanation has been shown. [But returning to the point:] momentary-duration-nature is itself its essential nature. Even a dull-witted person, seeing that [an entity] arises thus from its own cause, always deceived by co-observation into attachment to that entity's [continued] existence, does not ascertain [that what arises is] the successive production of similar [but different entities]. Or, being deceived by the perception of the final moment, his certainty — [that is, certitude] arising from the non-apprehension of [the entity] afterwards — [establishes] impermanence. Even when the power of producing effects is the nature of the cause, and [even] when the production of that unseen effect is observed — if [...] from the observation of the effect of what is well-established as existing — just so [is the inference]. Thus, even in this view, whose intent shines with exceedingly clear clarity, what has been made manifest by the one who proceeds — [namely,] a meagre, pitiably stamped dampness of [the counter-argument by] <s>Udayana</s> — looks for a foothold.

body.text: nahi paṭo jāta ityukte tantavo naṣṭā iti kaścidvyavaharati paṭasyānatirekāttantṛmātrajanmani ca bhedāgrahādavyavahāra iti cet na tarhi vyava-(4)-hārābalambanamapi visabhāgasantatau tāvadvyavahārāvalambanamastīti cet naitadevaṃ yadi tantumāleva paṭanivṛttiḥ | tarhi kathaṃ tathāśrayastadātmako vā paṭaḥ prāk anyaivāsāviti cetanatāvajjā (7) tikṛtmanyatvamupalabhyate vyaktikṛtaṃ tu nādyāpi siddhayatītyādi yat sphaṭikākṛtasya maṭhasya hastavitastiparimitabhāgabhāvanātaḥ svaghaṭitasandhi-bandhanaghaṭavighaṭanaprakaṭanapaṭuranyatkaṭakapāṭavopi sphuṭaṃ sphurati |
body.translated_text: For when one says 'a cloth is born,' no one conventionally asserts that the threads are destroyed — because the cloth is not different from the threads, and because in the birth of the threads alone, there is no convention [of a new entity] due to non-apprehension of difference. If [one says]: then the convention has no support [either]; but in a dissimilar continuum, there is indeed this much support for convention — [the reply is:] this is not so. If the cessation of cloth is nothing but the thread-series [itself], then how [is it called] cloth — [is the cloth] a substrate of such [threads], or identical in nature with them? If [one says] that [the cloth] was previously something different — [the reply is:] just as with sentience, the otherness is apprehended as produced by kind (<s>jāti</s>), but that produced by the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) is not yet established — and so forth. [This argument], like a crystal-built monastery, from the contemplation of its handful-measured portions, is skilled in displaying the fastening and unfastening of its self-constructed joints, and also shines clearly with the cleverness of another bracelet [of argument].

children.translated_text: In some cases, non-recognition of that [difference] is due to the arising of a similar [subsequent entity];
for one who does not see the difference due to error — like the difference in magical balls.
For thus: seeing [an entity that is] without a mark, without a grasping [character], whose subsequent arising is unconnected,
a person recognizes [it] as perishable, by means of a lamp and the like.

body.text: iti niyatabhāvābhāvavyavahāranibandhanapratyakṣādyanulambhasambhavādapi pragalbhagarvvaḥ pragalbhate, garbhāṃrbha-(3)-kopi kiṃ punaranyo dhīradhīko 'ntyakovidaḥ vyaktikṛtaṃ ca sphaṭikapaṭapaṭalavilokane pratyakṣataḥ prekṣate prekṣaḥ na khalu sphuṭita eva sphuṭitaḥ eva vā sphuṭito na bha-(4)-vati iti vyavaharaṇajanyatvavyavaharaṇaṃ tattvavyāvṛttameva hi na tvaṃ etamarthamādāya darśitā vyāptiranityatayā kṛtakatvasya |
body.translated_text: Thus, even when there is the possibility of non-apprehension by perception etc. — which is the basis of the convention of determinate existence and non-existence — one boldly holds forth with proud confidence; even an infant in the womb [may do so], let alone another who is of steady intellect and expert in finalities. And the [distinction] produced by the individual is observed directly by a discerning person when examining the array of crystal cloths — for indeed, what is shattered is not [said to be] 'not shattered,' nor is what is 'not shattered' treated as shattered — the convention of the [entity's] being conventionally produced is distinguished from its ultimate reality. [The opponent] has not taken up this meaning and shown the pervasion of being-produced with impermanence.

body.text: sattāmātrānubandhitvānnāśasyānityatā dhvaneḥ ||
body.translated_text: Because destruction follows mere existence, the impermanence of sound [is established].

children.translated_text: And if there were an inner production [within fire], there should be the perception of wood.
If [one says] 'since there is no destruction, that [fire] is itself the destruction of this [wood]' — then how?
Let one thing be the destruction of another — [but then] why is the wood not perceived?
If [one says] 'because of the inclusion of that [wood in fire]' — then, because of that, there is no obstruction.

body.text:
vināśasya vināśirtva syādutpattestataḥ punaḥ
kāṣṭhasya darśanaṃ hantṛdhāte caitrāpunarbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The destructive nature of destruction — from that, once again the perception of wood [would follow]; if the slayer's nature [ceases], then <s>Caitra</s> would not be reborn.

body.text:
yathācāpyevamiti cet (7) hanturnāmaraṇatvajataḥ
ananyatve vināśasya syānnāśaḥ kāṣṭhameva tu ||
body.translated_text: If [one says] 'just as it is, so [it is]' — [the reply is:] because of the non-mortality of the slayer. If destruction is non-different [from the entity], then destruction would simply be the wood itself.

body.text: tasya sattvādahetutvaṃ nātī'nyo vidyate gatiḥ

children.translated_text: even in the absence of causation for destruction, because of the permanence of both entity and destruction,
there would be the contingency of simultaneous existence — [but] whence the permanence of the non-existent?
If in non-existence, the contingency of non-entity not being destroyed — that too is not consistent.

body.translated_text: Because of its existence, the absence of causation — there is no other course;

children.translated_text: For it is not held that by the destruction of an entity, there is [further] annihilation;
the perishing entity does not depend on another — this [statement about destruction] is for making that known.

body.text: avasthāheturuktāsyā bhedamāropya cetasā ||
body.translated_text: The condition (<s>avasthā</s>) is said to be the cause of this [destruction]; [it is only] by superimposing a difference mentally

body.text: na bhāvo bhūto bhūtrāntarātbhartsanabhāgī bhāvyate |
body.translated_text: that an entity, having been, is imagined to be subject to reproach from another [subsequent] entity.

body.text: tathābhūtasyaiva svayaṃbhūterityaparāpekṣadharmapratiṣedhārthaṃ tattsvabhāvajñāpanenārthāntarameva dharmiṇaṃ cetasā vibhajya tanmātrajijñāsāyāṃ svabhāva eva tathocyate | (2) tadetanmandabuddhayaḥ kvacittathā darśanāyopamātravipralabdhanāśaṃ guṇaṃ tasya bhāvamāropya sahetukamahetukaṃ vāpratiṣṭhitaṃ taddvayābhāvacintayātmānamākalayanti |
body.translated_text: Since [the entity] is of such a nature and arises of itself (<s>svayaṃbhū</s>) — for the purpose of negating the property of dependence on another, by making known its own nature, one mentally distinguishes a separate object as the substrate. When one wishes to know only that [nature], the own-nature itself is so designated. This [point] the dull-witted, deceived by seeing [destruction] as such in some cases merely as an example, superimpose upon the entity [the attribute of] destruction as a property — either as caused or uncaused — and, being unsupported, torment themselves with the thought of the absence of both.

children.translated_text: If there is a conceptual alternative of non-existence even when the entity exists of itself — this [argument] is equal [in force on both sides];

children.text: na tasya kiñcadbhavati na bhavatyeva kevalami || tyādi
children.translated_text: nothing whatsoever arises of it, nor does it simply not arise at all — and so forth.

body.text: na bhāvo bhavatī tyādi nyāyanāthasya subhāṣitamukhopyapāpīyasā prabandhenākāla-(4) ku=ṭipaṭalenebāndhakāraprakhyaṃ dhānyaṃ dhī (vanepi vī) vivarddhayatyayamityanamanalamanalasavicāre vacanacarcayā | na ca pramāṇābhābo 'ntyakṣaṇadarśināṃ niścayā(5)t sāvadhitve notpattereva śakalavalayavilokane vilokro na ghaṭamālokayati | na hi yo yatra kāle nāsti sa tatra dṛśyate | deśāntara ivānyadeśani-(6)-veśitadravyam | vyavahārarītiramaṇīyaśaraṇiranupalabdhirūpavisadṛśadaśāsya svabhāvabhābanābhaṇitaiva bhūriśaḥ | kārakahetuvyūhavyastyā vikhyāpitamanapekṣatvaṃ jñāpa-(7)-kāpekṣayā sāpekṣamevedaṃ | tatkiṃ bravīti vicārakavṛddhaḥ | raṇḍākaraṇḍapiṇḍitatantubhyaḥ kuvindanandakarapaṭṭha- sitātānavitānāvasthā sthavīyāṃsaṃ bhedamā-vibhrato 'nubhūyagte paṭādivyapadeśaviṣayāḥ prāva (ra) ṇādikriyāviśeṣaśālino yadavasthāṃ dravyavṛddhiprāgalbhyagarvvaguravo gaṇyante pareṇa |
body.translated_text: 'An entity does not arise' — and so forth. This well-spoken [verse] of <s>Nyāyanātha</s> [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], even from its very face, with a faultless composition, adorned with a curtain of unseasonable [objections] — [yet] the darkness-like [counter-argument] nourishes grain even in the forest of intellect; this [one] does not [succeed] — [enough] with the chatter of words in examination devoid of effort. And the absence of evidence — from the certainty of those who perceive the final moment, when there is a limit [to existence], production itself [is not established] — in the observation of fragments and circles, the observer does not see a pot. For what does not exist at a certain time in a certain place is not perceived there — just as an object placed in another location [is not seen] in the current one. The method of convention, whose charming refuge is non-apprehension — [this] has been repeatedly stated as the proclamation of the nature of [the entity's] own dissimilar state. The non-dependence proclaimed by the arrangement of the array of causal factors is dependent indeed with reference to the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>). What then does the elder of investigation say? The threads compacted in the basket of the widow [weaver] — the state of a spread canopy, like a white cloth delighting the weaver, not manifesting the greater difference, is experienced [as such]; the designations 'cloth' etc. are applied to objects possessing particular activities of covering and the like; those [entities] are counted by others as heavy with the pride and confidence of material increase.

children.translated_text: It operates without preventing the distinctions of capacities for form and the like;
the word 'pot' is used to exclude [other] causes that produce the same type of result.

body.text: bandhanādikriyānibanthano hi dhvanistanturiti tatsamudāyaviśeṣaṃ sampādya prāvarādyarthaṃ sāmarthyamatathāvidhasamudāyāntaravyavacchedena sa-(3)-marthanīyamarthanavaiḥ paṭa iti prakaṭitaḥ śabdaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the thread is the sound [i.e., verbal designation] whose basis is the binding and such activities; having produced that particular aggregate, the capacity for [the function of] covering etc. is to be established by excluding other aggregates not of that kind — [thus] the word 'cloth' (<s>paṭa</s>) has been made manifest by those skilled in meaning.

body.text:
taistantubhiriyaṃ śāṭīnyuttaraṃ kāryamucyate
tantusaṃskārasaṃbhūtaṃ naikakālaṃ kathaṃcana |
kāraṇāropataḥ kaścit, ekāpoddhārato 'pivā
tantvākhyāṃ vartayetkārye darśayan nāśrayaṃ śrṛteḥ |
body.translated_text:
By those threads, this cloth or upper garment is said to be the effect,
born from the refinement of threads, never at one time.
Someone may apply the name 'threads' to the effect, either
by superimposition of the cause, or by abstraction of each one — showing that [the name] does not [refer to] the substrate, [as taught] by scripture.

body.text: tantukāryo hi paṭa eva, tadānīṃ na tantavaḥ tantupratyayastu kāraṇasvarūpāropataḥ pūrvasmaraṇa-(5)-sāpekṣatvāt | ekaikāpohane vā lakṣyaikaikāpohe paṭī nāmāparo 'sti tadevaṃ kāliko viśeṣaḥ samastavastustomaviṣayo viśeṣato 'nyatve kathanīyaḥ | (6) kathamanyathā pratyabhijñāpadaikatvasiddhau tena tūṣṇīkṛtametat, api ca tantuvināśa sāmānyatastantuvirahasvabhāvo vā syādityādivicāravaśena ca kalitaḥ (7) vināśyasvarūpāsvarūpa kāraṇākāraṇatvameva bādhakaṃ sakalakalākalāpaprāptapradārthasārthasya sarvadā vināśanāmapadārthāntaraprādurbhāvabhāṣaṇe-(8)-bibhyata iva vināśapūrvakālapratijñāsamaparaparyālocanayā'pratinivṛttaṃ manyamānena uktameva kāṣṭhaṃ kāsmānnadṛśyata ityādi padārthāntarasyābhāvasaṃjñākaraṇaṃ vā, (9) lokavyavahārasammatyā vā, pramāṇapravṛtyā vā, maheśvarasamīhāhetuprahitaprabhāvādvā, ātmecchānucaratvādvā bhāvānāṃ bhāvānāṃ bhartsitaṃ sarvatra ca sudarśanaḥ samādhiriti kimayaṃ caurārcanamiva pracapalapadaspandasamandarpyamapasarpya | 'tatkālasatvaṃ cettarhi tadabhāvo jāta ityādi bhāṣayā, tasmāt |
body.translated_text: For the effect of the threads is indeed the cloth; at that time there are no threads. The cognition of 'threads,' however, is due to superimposition of the essential form of the cause, because it depends on prior memory. Or, when each one is removed — when each indicated [thread] is removed — there is another [thing] called 'cloth.' Thus this temporal distinction, which has the totality of entities as its object, must be stated as different from [each] particular. How otherwise? When the identity of the word is established through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), this [question] has been silenced by that [argument]. Moreover, by the force of investigation — whether the destruction of threads is in general, or has the nature of the absence of threads, etc. — [it is concluded that] the very nature of the destructible, [whether it is] its own essential form or not, [and whether it is] a cause or a non-cause — this alone is the defeater for one who has obtained the mass of all artistic achievements and the caravan of objects of conveyance. Always fearing to speak of the appearance of another category [called] 'destruction,' [the opponent], thinking that [the matter] has not been reversed by the consideration of the prior-to-destruction thesis and its counterpart — the very thing that was stated: 'Why is the piece of wood not seen?' etc. — [this is explained] either by making the non-existent [entity] bear the designation of 'absence,' or by agreement with worldly convention, or by the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s>, or by the power dispatched from the purpose of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), or because entities follow the will of the self — all [these] have been rebuked. And everywhere the resolution is easy to see — what is this [argument], like worshipping a thief, slipping away with the restless trembling of nimble words? 'If existence at that time [is granted], then its absence has arisen' — thus by this statement, therefore:

children.translated_text: Because destruction is causeless, [there is] connection from [its] essential nature;
for entities that are dependent, the inevitable is not observed.

body.text: bāhulyepihi taddhetorbhavetkvacidasambhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: For even when its causes are abundant, non-occurrence sometimes happens.

body.text: yadyapi ca kṣaṇāni vināśakāraṇakāraṇāni santi, teṣāmapi svapratyayādhīnasannidhitvānnāvaśyaṃ sannidhānamiti mahī-(3)-madhīdhārādiṣu kaścinna vinaśyedapi niyamānavadhāraṇameva hi vyabhicāracamatkāraścetasi vicāracakrasya | ata evāha-
body.translated_text: And even though moments are causes of the causes of destruction, because their presence too depends on their own conditions, their presence is not necessary — therefore, even in [cases like] the earth, rivers (<s>madhīdhārā</s>), etc., someone may not be destroyed. Indeed, the marvel of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in the mind is precisely the non-determination of restriction within the wheel of investigation. Therefore he says:

body.text: etena vyabhicāritvamuktaṃ kāryāvyavasthiteḥ ||
body.translated_text: By this, the deviation (<s>vyabhicāritva</s>) has been stated, because of the non-fixity of the effect.

body.text: sarveṣāṃ nāśahetūnāṃ (4)hetusannāśavādinām ||
body.translated_text: Of all those who maintain that the causes of destruction have causes for [their own] destruction —

body.text: tasmānnidhanavivandhanacaṇḍadaṇḍābhighātāgnisaṃyogāditaḥ samanantarabhagavatakapālāṅgārādivisadṛśavikāravīkṣaṇavelāyāmapi ghaṭakāṣṭhādi-(5) kaṃ vastu svabhāvata eva vinaśvaramutpannamiti na dṛśyate tadvastu aṃta eva vinaśvaratvarūpasya bināśasya vyāpakatvaṃ kṛtakatvaṃ pratyanapekṣatvādhruvabhāvitvena pratipādi (6)-tam | tasmāt |
body.translated_text: Therefore, even at the moment of observing a transformation resembling the blessed [deity's] skull-fragments, embers, and the like — [a transformation occurring] immediately after the contact with the fierce staff-blow of the bond of annihilation, fire-conjunction, etc. — entities such as pots, wood, etc. have been produced as inherently perishable by their very essential nature, and [yet] that entity is not seen [to be destroyed]. The pervasiveness of destruction — in the form of [the entity's] very nature of perishability — has been demonstrated through [its] being produced-ness (<s>kṛtakatva</s>), non-dependence, and inevitable occurrence. Therefore:

body.text:
bhavatyeva svabhāvataḥ |
yatra nāma bhavatyasmāt anyatrāpi svabhāvataḥ |
body.translated_text:
It occurs indeed by its very essential nature;
where indeed it occurs, therefore elsewhere too, by essential nature.

body.text: soyaṃ bhavan kvaciddraṣṭo 'napekṣatvāt svabhāvata eva bhavati tathānyatrāpi svabhāva-(7)-viśeṣābhāvāt | iti vyāpakatvamuktamasyānyathākāramutthāpya dūṣayato na svahṛdayasyāpi paritoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: This [destruction], seen somewhere, occurs by essential nature alone because of non-dependence; and likewise elsewhere too, because of the absence of a distinction in essential nature. Thus, the pervasiveness has been stated. For one who raises an objection in a different form against this — there is no satisfaction even for his own heart.

body.text: astu tarhi dhruvabhāvitvaṃ vyāpakatvamiti cet na atādātmyādatatkāra-(8)ṇatvāccetyādi, tādātmyaṃ tadekakāraṇasambhavaśca pratipādyate sma samanantarameva, na vā bhāvatvādabhāvo na kriyata iti kaścidāha | kiṃ tarhi prasajyaparyudāsovābhāva i-(9)-tyābālamālāpaḥ kartavyaścābhāvaḥ kataro 'stu na tāvatprasajyaḥ kriyāpadena tatra nañaḥ sambandhāt kriyāpratiṣedhamātratvamekapramāṇavyāpārapratyayajñātatvādavidyāvaśena parāpekṣapratyanīkākāratvaṃ bhāvaparihārasvabhāvatvañca(jñānamiśrayati) jñānaśrīmiśratrāti kalpanā | siddhasyāsiddhaṃ vā pāratantryaṃ sambaṃdho rūpāśleṣaḥ tathāparopi na pāramārthikaḥ (2) iti sambaṃdhaparīkṣāyāṃ khyāpitam | tena śeṣaprabandho vidhi eva dhīvidhūta iti tadaparaprabandhavidhūtaye yatāmahe | pratyabhijñākeśakuśakardalakāṇḍaprabhṛtau padārthe pradīpavadvi (3)cchinnapunaḥ prarūḍhe samapauḍhakatve 'pi ghaṭasphaṭikapratyabhijñayā na bhidyate sambandhabhāvatvāt | samasvabhāvatvamasiddhamavabuddhaṃ viruddhadharmāsaṃsṛṣṭaviṣayatvena ghaṭasphaṭikaku-(4)-ṇḍakuṇḍalamaṇḍalamaṇḍanānusandhitvāndhānapi yo 'dhikatvāt baddhvā pracyuta viracāyīrti cet, na-pratyabhijñā sāmathyametat | siddhā vāśrayato 'nyo 'nyasaṃśrayadoṣo (5)na doṣasahasreṇāpi saśakyaḥ saṃkocayituṃ pramāṇāntarañca śatamāsitvāpi samāḥ samārthona kaścana prapañcayituṃ kṣaṇabharṅgaṃ saṅgatamānanā nivedi-(6)-taiva | na ca pramāṇanivṛttāvapi viprakṛṣṭaviṣaye tadbhāvavibhāvanā prabhuḥ prekṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Let there be, then, inevitable occurrence as pervasiveness' — if [the opponent says] thus, [we reply:] No — 'because of non-identity and because of not being its cause' etc. Identity and arising from a single cause were being demonstrated just immediately [before]. Or, someone says: 'From entity-hood (<s>bhāvatva</s>), non-existence is not produced.' What then? Is the absence [understood as] <s>prasajya</s> (simple negation) or <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion)? — thus begins a childish prattle. And [regarding] the absence that is to be effected — which [type] should it be? Not <s>prasajya</s> in the first place, because of the connection of the negative particle with the verb therein, [yielding] mere prohibition of action — this being known through the cognition produced by the operation of a single <s>pramāṇa</s>; and under the influence of ignorance, the nature of being opposed to the form dependent on another, and the essential nature of the elimination of existence — [this is] the fabrication of <s>Jñānaśrīmitra</s>. The dependence of what is established on the unestablished, or [the nature of] relation, or the contact of forms — that too is not ultimate. This has been proclaimed in the examination of relations. Therefore, the remaining composition is positive affirmation alone, [being] purified by understanding — thus we endeavor to purify that further composition. Regarding the object such as the hair-tip, the reed, the plantain-stalk, etc. in recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) — like a lamp, [which is] extinguished and then rekindled — even though there is equality of being extinguished, [the cognition] is not split by the recognition of a pot, a crystal, etc., because of the existence of [a] relation. The identity of essential nature is unestablished and wrongly understood — because its object is not conjoined with contradictory properties, even one who is blind regarding the investigation of pots, crystals, earrings, circles, and ornaments — because of [the opponent's] superiority [claim], [the opponent], having bound and fallen and been scattered — if [he says] thus: No — this is the power of recognition. Or [if] it is established — from the substrate, the fault of mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>) cannot be contracted even by a thousand faults, and no other <s>pramāṇa</s>, even if it resides for a hundred [years], is able to elaborate [against] the momentariness that is coherent with the capacity [of its own proof] — this has indeed been demonstrated. And even when <s>pramāṇa</s> has ceased to operate, no competent observer can demonstrate the existence of that [entity] regarding a remote object.

body.text:
abhinnavedanasyaikyaṃ yannaivaṃ tadvibhedavat |
siddhayedasādhanatve 'sya na si-(7)-ddhaṃ bhedasādhanam |

children.translated_text: The sky etc. [which appear] differentiated, and white, pain, etc. — [while] cognition and experience [are] undifferentiated.
If the undifferentiated [appear as] differentiated and the differentiated [as undifferentiated] — what is the basis for difference and non-difference?
Because even for those who are concealed, the sharp-witted one [perceives] non-difference at some point.
In the stream of mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>), the establishment of difference is accomplished.

body.translated_text:
The unity of undifferentiated experience —
that which is not thus, being of the nature of difference,
would be established; when this [argument] is unestablished, no proof of difference is established.

body.text: iti ācāryavacanamavahartuṃ prabandhāntareṇa na śakyam, svaragītaphalocchvāsamaprāpta prāpyate
body.translated_text: Thus, the words of the teacher cannot be stolen away by another composition; the fruit of one's own melody is attained [only when it is] not yet attained — [like] the exhalation of the fruit of a song.

children.text: sādhugītaṃ suṣṭugītaṃ labdhaṃ (9) gītasya te phalam |
children.translated_text: Well-sung, excellently sung! You have obtained the fruit of your song.

children.text: goputrā iva gāyanti sāmo dātumayaiḥ svaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like the sons of cows, they sing the <s>Sāman</s> in metallic tones.

body.text: etenaitadapi piṣṭamaniṣṭam vivādādhyāsito bhāvaḥ kālabhedepi na bhidyate | viruddhadharmāsaṃsṛṣṭatvāt yo yadbhedepi viruddhadharmāsaṃsṛṣṭo nāsau tadbhedepi bhidyate | yathā pratisandhiparamāṇubhedepyekaḥ paramāṇustathā cāyaṃ vivādādhyāsito bhāvastamātkālabhede 'pi na bhidyate iti | atra vyāptau na kaścidapi vipratipadyeta | pakṣadharmatā te prasādhitaiveti sthiratāsthiratā bhāvārnām | tadanantaraprakaraṇanihatapakṣadha(3)rmatā siddhitvādasādhanamasādhanīyam | tadevaṃ sattvaṃ prāgabhāvapradhvaṃsābhāvamadhyamadhyāsīnasya bhāvasyāntarālabhede nisatvamavagamayitumalamutkalitānukūlaprasaṅga-(4)-tadviparyaparyavasitasapakṣatve kvacidbījādau darśitasvasādhyapratibandhamiti prabandhena prasādhitaṃ sādhīyaḥ sudhībhiravadhāryamiti sthitam | pūrvasarvanyāyasanyāsamāśri-(5)-tya laghuparalaṅghana jaṃghālahetuhatiṃ prahiṇumaḥ | yadyasya yatravyavaharaṇakāraṇamapasaraṇaparācīnatayā cintitaṃ tatra tasya vyavaharaṇakāraṇajananīyaṃ nī-(6)-latā vyavaharaṇakāraṇanīli | bhavati tadvayavaharaṇavat | nīraje pūrvāparakālayaurapikaraṇākaraṇaviruddhadharmākhyānau bījabhede vyavaharaṇakāraṇa (7) mapasaraṇaramaṇatvena mataḥ, tadatra karaṇākaraṇaṃ nāsiddhayā grastamadhyakṣaprekṣitatvāt, viruddhatā viśeṣagaṇapi pramathitapradūṣaṇagaṇaṃ prācīnapragalbhapraba-(8)-ndhatvena nāpyanaikāntikatvaṃ antikamasya gantuṃ santanoti sāmarthyam | anyavyatirekapratyākalanayā hi kāraṇatvaṃ kiñcidapi pratiparyālocanīyamu(1) pāyāntarātarkaṇāt | ayameva bhedo bheda heturvvā yaduta viruddhadharmādhyāsastasya janananibandhanañca sāmagrīlakṣaṇakāraṇasājātyavijātyaparyava sitau bheda iti abhidadhānena cācāryacaraṇena pratidarśanaṃ darśitadikkālādiguṇadravyavyāyāvyayādibhedavyavahārahetuhastakatvāt nyastau viruddhadharmādhyāso vastusvabhāvanānātve nibandhanasamastavādivyāptyavyāptiprasarānākrāntapauruṣasato 'yamevabheda i-(2)-ti vyavasthāne sthirastadvyavaharaṇeṃ kāraṇaṃkalpanāropitadharmāṇāmapi bhedo viruddhadharmādhyāsalakṣaṇa evetyavyāptirasambhāvinī, nacobhedepi vimṛśyate kvā-(3)-pi viruddhadharmādhyāsa ityativyāptivyastirasti virodhabodho bahudhā bahuṣviti na sambhavaviparyayo hṛdi dheyaḥ | na ca viruddhadharmadvayabhedānupapattistatrāpi nityasa-(4)-māṃ jātirītyā viruddhau padārtho vyudasya nānyo dharmonāma kintarhi dharmāntarapratikṣepākṣepābhyāṃ dharmmadharmmivyapadeśepi na vastubhedastenānavasthā (15) na manasi niveśyā yathākalpanamasya sambhavāt |
body.translated_text: By this, the following too is ground and rejected: the entity superimposed upon in the debate is not differentiated even through temporal difference, because it is not conjoined with contradictory properties (<s>viruddhadharma</s>). Whatever is not conjoined with contradictory properties in any given difference is not differentiated even through that difference — just as one <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom) remains singular even through the difference of reconnecting atoms, so too this entity superimposed upon in the debate is not differentiated even through temporal difference. In this <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), no one would disagree. The property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) has already been established by you — thus the stability or instability of entities [is settled]. Since the establishment of the property of the subject is defeated in the immediately following section, this is a non-proof that need not be proven. Thus it is established in sequence that <s>sattva</s> (existence), being seated in the middle between prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) and destruction-absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>), is sufficient to make known the non-existence of the entity in the intervening difference — [this is shown] through the favorable implication (<s>prasaṅga</s>) that has been raised and its converse, resulting in the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>), with the invariable connection to its own thesis demonstrated somewhere in seeds and such — [all this] is most excellent, to be ascertained by the wise, and so it stands. Relying upon the summary of all previous arguments, let us dispatch a blow from a reason nimble-legged enough to leap lightly over the opponent. If the cause of the application of something somewhere is considered as having departed and turned away, then what is to be produced as the cause of application there — blueness as the cause of the application 'blue' — exists as having that application. In a blue lotus, in prior and subsequent times, the declaration of contradictory properties consisting in producing and not-producing, in the difference of seeds, is regarded as the cause of application having departed and being delightful. There, the producing and not-producing is not swallowed by non-establishment (<s>asiddhi</s>), because it is observed by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). The contradiction, even in the particular instances, having crushed the array of refutations through the force of the bold earlier exposition, does not have the capacity to extend inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatva</s>) to a proximate reach. For causality is ascertained through the method of elimination of other [factors] by negative correlation (<s>vyatireka</s>) — [it is] something to be reconsidered through reasoning by alternative means. This very difference is the cause of difference — namely, the superimposition of contradictory properties (<s>viruddhadharmādhyāsa</s>), and the ground of its production is the cause characterized as the aggregate of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>). As the venerable master (<s>ācāryacaraṇa</s>) has stated, showing that the result concludes in homogeneity and heterogeneity as difference — the superimposition of contradictory properties has been demonstrated as the cause of practical application of differences such as direction, time, quality, substance, gain, loss, and so forth. It is the foundation for the diversity of the nature of real things, firm in the determination 'this alone is the difference,' its scope of pervasion and non-pervasion unencroached upon by the endeavors of all rival theorists. Since the difference of even conceptually superimposed properties (<s>kalpanāropitadharma</s>) is characterized precisely by the superimposition of contradictory properties, under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) is impossible. And since the superimposition of contradictory properties is never examined even in non-difference, there is no over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) either — the cognition of contradiction operates in many ways in many [cases], so no impossibility should be held in the mind. And there is no impossibility of difference from a pair of contradictory properties, for in that case too, the contradictory entity is to be rejected in the manner of an eternal universal (<s>jāti</s>) — there is no other thing called a property (<s>dharma</s>); rather, even in the designation of property and property-bearer (<s>dharma-dharmin</s>) through the exclusion and inclusion of other properties, there is no real difference, and hence no infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) should be entertained in the mind, since the occurrence of this [distinction] is merely as conceptually constructed.

body.text: yatpunaruktam-bhedo hi virodhaṃ vyabhicarati, na virodhau bhedamiti tatpāramārthikāpāramārthikabhedabha-(6) ṇyābhāṣitaṃ viruddhatāhetoḥ savidhasambandhanibandhasambandhāvyāptisiddhau hi sapakṣe pakṣapātī viruddho nopalabdhaḥ bhedavyavahārajñāpakahetuśca prati (7) bhāsa bhedaḥ | dvitoyopi prayogaḥ-sa evāyamiti parāmarśaḥ so 'sadṛśaparāvṛttapadārthadhyavasānavyāpāraḥ, yathā keśapāśe cchinnodbhinne sa evāyamiti parāmarśasya vivādapade ghaṭādau atyantasadṛśe sa evāyamiti mandasādṛśye sa iveti prakaraṇavaśāt atyantasādṛśya-(9)-mihopāttaṃ jātyekatve dīpādau pratyabhijñeti vadatātadvyāvṛttiviṣayā syātprakāśitā, yadyatītena saha vartamānasya ekatvaṃ nāsti kartha citpūrva paścāddṛṣṭārtha kriyā bhavati | na | yathā ghaṭamekaṃ vighaṭaghaṭāṅkurāropaṇe prekṣate yathā puradhāraṇaṃ tatheva pūrvānurodhe 'asambhave yataḥ bhaviṣyati tādṛśārthakriyā taccekārthakriyākaraṇādekatvantu tadakārivyavacchedalakṣaṇaṃ sāmvṛtamiṣyata eva tena kṣaṇabhaṅgo ghaṭādīnāṃ dharmastenaiva sādhanahetubhirityapakṛtam | ekamiti hi vyapadeśavikalpāstadarthasāmarthyamā-(3)-treṇa samaṅgīsajātayo na punarartharadritasāmānyadyarthasāmānyadyarthaviṣayā vyapadeśavikalpāḥ prekṣāvadbhirādriyante tatastādṛgarthakriyākāritayaikatvaṃ pratyabhijñānaviṣayaḥ tasmādyā (4) pratyabhijñā sā tadarthakriyākārivyāvṛtta sadṛśārthakriyāsamarthaviṣayāḥ yathā ghaṭānayane 'pi itarābhiprāyeṇa anyamānayeti niyoge ghaṭāntarānayane punaḥ-(5)-sa evānīta iti pratyabhijñā | pratyabhijñā ceyaṃ sa evāyaṃ ghaṭa iti ājanmanaḥ praṇāśāvadhipratibhāsaprasavaprasaṅgaḥ, pratikṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇabhaṅge sati bhāvasya bhavedata-(6)-viparyaye bādhakaṃ asti ca pratibhāsaḥ prāgabhāvapradhvaṃsābhāvayormadhyārūḍhasya vastutaḥ pūrvāparakālakalatātikrāntaḥ | saḥ krāntaniścayo nikhilavastu (7) sujanānubhavabhūmiḥ | ataeva sthavīyasi svabhāve bhāvānāṃ kālaniyamau'pi siddhaḥ | atadrūparāvṛttiviṣayastvekatvādhyavasāyonāvasthābhāvamākarṣati pratyayabhijñā (8) tantu sāṃvṛtaikatvaṃ vyavahārayati | paravyāmohāpanayanena yathādṛśyānupalabdhibalimahilāgopālādigamye 'pi pratiṣedhe śaṅkayaṃ lakṣyīkṛtya vyāmohaśuddhatantraṃ (9) prakṣipyate |
body.translated_text: Now, what was said — 'Difference indeed deviates from contradiction, but contradiction does not deviate from difference' — that is to be spoken of in terms of ultimate and non-ultimate difference. For when the non-pervasion of the proximate connection that is the ground of the reason of contradiction is established, the contradictory [reason] is not found to be partial in the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>), and the reason that indicates the practical application of difference is the appearance of difference. The second formulation too [is as follows]: the recognition 'this is that very same [thing]' has the operation of determining an object that has turned away from dissimilar [things]. Just as in the case of a severed and re-grown braid of hair, [there is] the recognition 'this is that very same [thing].' In the subject of debate, such as a pot and the like, which is extremely similar, [there is] the recognition 'this is that very same [thing]'; in [cases of] slight similarity, [the recognition] 'this is like that' — according to context, extreme similarity is taken up here. If one says that in the case of a lamp and such, where there is unity of universal (<s>jāti</s>), this is recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), then it would have as its object the exclusion of that [unity]. If there is no unity of the present with the past, then some purpose-serving activity (<s>arthakriyā</s>) that was previously and subsequently observed does occur. No — just as one observes a single pot in the planting of pot-fragments and pot-sprouts, just as [there was] the prior holding, so too in the impossibility of conformity with the prior, whence will such purpose-serving activity arise? And if from performing a single purpose-serving activity there is unity, then that [unity] is accepted as merely conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>), characterized by the exclusion of what does not perform that [activity]. By that, momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) is the property of pots and such — by that very [reasoning] and by the proving reasons [it is established] — thus it has been addressed. For the designations and conceptual constructions [expressed as] 'one' are assimilated merely by the capacity of their referent-meaning — but designations and conceptual constructions that have as their object a real universal apprehended in the referent are not respected by the discerning. Therefore, by virtue of producing such purpose-serving activity, unity is the object of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>). Hence whatever recognition there is, it has as its object what is capable of similar purpose-serving activity, excluded from what performs that [specific] purpose-serving activity. Just as even in the bringing of a pot, when commanded by another's intention 'bring another one,' upon bringing a different pot, [there is] the recognition 'this very same one was brought.' And this recognition 'this is that very same pot' — from birth to the limit of destruction — entails the consequence of the appearance [of identity]. When there is momentary destruction at every instant, if the entity exists, [then] in the absence of the contrary there is a ground for invalidation (<s>bādhaka</s>). And the appearance [of identity] of what is established in reality as seated between prior absence and destruction-absence has transcended the temporal extension of prior and subsequent moments. That ascertainment having been crossed over is the ground of experience of all good people regarding all real things. Precisely therefore, even the temporal regularity of entities with a more enduring essential nature is established. But the determination of unity, which has as its object the exclusion of what is not of that nature, does not attract the defect of infinite regress — recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) indeed operates with conventional unity. As for dispelling the delusion of the opponent — just as in the case of prohibition that is accessible even to <s>bali</s>-offering women, cowherds, and the like through the force of non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>), targeting the doubt, the method purified of delusion is introduced.

body.text:
ḥtadatyantavimūḍhārthaṃ āgovālādimasaṃvṛteḥḥ
iti vacanāt |
body.translated_text:
'That is of utterly confused meaning, [applicable] up to cowherds and such, in the conventional [realm]' —
thus it is stated.

children.translated_text: Cognition, however, [arises] from the appearance of the object.
It is said to manifest that [object] — even in its absence, [the cognition] is produced by it.

body.text: tathā dukūlanīlanalina-(10)-dalāvalivalimadhyapramadānandimandirakundasindūrārtha valabhīprabhṛtīnāṃ madhyāvasthākhya grāhyākāravedanāvṛtyaikaṃ pratisaṃdhātārameva bhāṣitaṃ sakṛdatra pratibhātīti pāścātyānuvyavaśāyavaśena sphuraṇañca pūrvānubhūtasya grāhakākārasya atadrūpaparāvṛttaviṣayaikavimarśavaśena vyāptyādikañca parikalpitādrūpa (2) parāvttavastustomākāreṇa kṣaṇakṣīṇatānukūlamilitavinyāseneti na kvāpyaṃśe śaṃśanīyadoṣamanityatāsādhanamava dhātavyaṃ bhavyabhāvena tathā-
body.translated_text: Similarly, in the case of fine silk, blue lotus petals, a series of creepers, the waist of a beautiful woman, a pleasure-garden, <s>kunda</s>-flowers, vermillion, the meaning of <s>valabhī</s> and so forth — through the grasping-aspect (<s>grāhyākāra</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), and cognition (<s>vṛtti</s>) of the intermediate state, a single connecting agent alone is spoken of. 'It appears here just once' — and by the force of subsequent reflective cognition (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>), the manifestation of what was previously experienced, which is the apprehending-aspect (<s>grāhakākāra</s>), occurs through a single reflective determination whose object is the exclusion of what is not of that nature. And the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) and so forth are constructed through the aspect of [what is] excluded from the constructed non-that-nature, with an arrangement favorable to momentary cessation (<s>kṣaṇakṣīṇatā</s>). Thus in no respect whatsoever should there be any suspicion of a defect — the proof of impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>) is to be understood with a receptive mind. Likewise —

children.translated_text: 'Even diamond, stone, and the like — if stable, being independent of other [conditions],
would produce all cognitions of the entire world simultaneously.
Those [cognitions] arise successively for it, due to the assistance of cooperative conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>).'
'They declare momentary difference — the fault here too is as before.'

body.text: ityādyapi yathā prastāvamapahastitrāsamupanyasanīyam |
body.translated_text: These and other [verses] too are to be presented with the fear removed, as occasion arises.

body.text: yatpunarucyate kāladidravyaguṇakarmādikamantareṇa na kaścit vyapadeśastaṃ cāntareṇa na vacanaṃ tasmādvacanādeva kāladikamastīti kṣaṇikatāsiddhiriti, tadapi nirasyate, kālaḥ parāparavyatikarayaugapadyāyaugapadyacirakṣiprapatyayaliṅgaḥ teṣāṃ viṣayeṣu (9) pūrvapratyayavilakṣaṇānāmutṣattāvanyanimittāsaṃbhavāt | yadatra nimittaṃ sa kālaḥ yatraivāparapratyayodigapekṣayā tatraivaparapratyayaḥ kālakṛtaḥ ya-(7)-trai va ca parapratyayo digapekṣayā tatraivāparapratyaya kāla kṛta iti vyatikaraḥ śleṣaḥ | yugapadetāni kṛtāni krameṇa ca etāni kṛtāni | ciraṃ kṛtaṃ kṣipraṃ kṛtamiti na rūpādyatireke kāle pratyakṣāpravṛttaḥ mandatā hi niṣpatteḥ kāraṇakrameṇa virodhaḥ, kramopi bhāvābhāvādeva bhāvasya na kālaḥ rāṃhoḥ śira itivat, punara-(9)-bhāvasyāyaṃ kāla iti vyapadeśaḥ-
body.translated_text: As for the further statement — 'Without time, substance, quality, action, and the rest, no designation is possible; and without that, there is no statement; therefore from statement alone, time and the rest exist — hence momentariness is not established' — this too is refuted. Time (<s>kāla</s>) is inferred from the marks of interchange of prior and posterior, simultaneity and non-simultaneity, and long and short duration. Among those [marks], in their respective objects, because of the impossibility of any other cause for [cognitions] that are different from the prior cognition upon their arising. Whatever is the cause here, that is time (<s>kāla</s>). Where there is the cognition of 'posterior' relative to direction, there itself is the cognition of 'posterior' produced by time — and where there is the cognition of 'posterior' relative to time, there itself is the cognition of 'posterior' produced by direction — this is the interchange, i.e., the interlocking. 'These were done simultaneously and these were done in sequence; this was done slowly, this was done quickly' — [in all such cases] there is no operation of perception upon time as something beyond form and the rest. For the slowness of production, through the sequence of causes, is contradictory [to permanence]; and the sequence itself is [determined] only from the existence and non-existence of entities, not by time — just as [the saying] 'the head of speed' [means speed is the entity's own nature]. And the designation 'this is the time of the subsequent non-existence' —

body.text:
'dṛṣṭatātītakālatvaṃ dṛśyatā vartamānatā
bhāvitā dṛśyamāṇārcāmiti vyavasthitiḥ' |
body.translated_text: 'Having been seen, the state of past time; being seen, the state of present time — thus is the determination regarding [an entity] that was, is being, and [will be] perceived as a form.'

body.text: rūpamapi cakṣurvijñānajanakatvena evaṃ śa-(10)-bdādikamapi sve svendriyanidānadarśananibandhanatvena vedyam | dravyavyavasthāpi tatsamudāyasādhyaphalāhetuvyavacchedena darśitaiveti na tadāsti vyavaharaṇaṃ na yat pakṣe tad anityānubandhīti |
body.translated_text: Form (<s>rūpa</s>) too is to be cognized through its capacity to generate visual consciousness; similarly sound and the rest are to be cognized through their being grounded in perception caused by their respective sense organs. The determination of substance (<s>dravya</s>) too has been shown through the exclusion of [all] other causes of the result accomplished by that aggregate. Therefore, there is no convention that is not accompanied by impermanence in [any] thesis.

body.text: udayananirākaraṇe vādarahasye vyatirekārthabhāvārdinyāyanirṇayo dvitīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: In the <s>Vādarahasya</s> [entitled] 'Refutation of <s>Udayana</s>,' [this is] the second [chapter], the determination of the meaning of absence in the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).

body.text:
apohapratyūhavyūhanirāsaḥ
tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text:
Removal of the Assemblage of Objections to <s>Apoha</s> (Exclusion)
Third Chapter

body.text: ihāpohe pratyūhavyūho vyudasyate | iha jagati jāgrato jīvalokasya nīlavipulacalacetanīyanicūlanicayādau cakṣuṣo vikṣepādanantaraṃ nīlādisvalakṣaṇaniṣṭho (2) nirbhāsastadanusandhānadhīrasādhāraṇabodhapratibaddhanīlādīnirbhāsaśca niścīyate etacca dvayamapi nīlādiparicchedadakṣamakṣatamabhīkṣṇamabhilakṣyate | sārūpyavaśa-(3)-gā hi paricchedaśaktiḥ samvedanānāmasti cānayornīlabhirbhāsatā nīlanirṇayanibandhanaṃ tenobhayamapi bhayabhraṣṭaṃ nīlameva paricchinattīti sampratyayaḥ sāṃvya-(4)-vahārikalokasya | tattvatarkavitarkaviśrṛṅkhalāśrayastu vyākhyātā samaḥkhyātiprathamamavyapadeśyaṃ vyavasāyātmakamiti | prathamamālo-(5)canājñānaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ bālamūkādijñānaprakhyam, tataḥ paraṃ punarvastu dharmerjātyādibhiryayā buddhayāvasīyate sāpi pratyakṣatvena sammateti vikalpakamadhya(6)kṣaṃ jātyādiyojitajalajādivastuparicchede dīpyate | bauddhastvavadhayvasitavān, prathamameva pramāṇaṃ dvitīyantu smaraṇābhogādisāmagrījalpanārthāt (7) utpadyate netrādisamagrāt | kintarhi madhyāvasthālakṣaṇajñānagrāhyākārātsmaraṇābhogādisahitādaniṣṭhitamitīṣṭaṃ nirṇayanibandhanaṃ punaratranetranīlādyarthāpāye 'pi nīlākṣismaraṇasaṃkāntanīlādinirbhāsaḥ kutaḥ saṃbobhavīṃta | nārthāttasya niruddhatvāt | na jalāde vyāpyarūpādisvabhāvatvāt | idaṃ hyuktam-
body.translated_text: Here, the assemblage of objections to <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is being dispelled. In this world, for the living being who is awake, upon the eye's casting [its gaze] upon the mass of blue, vast, moving, sentient clusters of <s>nīcūla</s> trees and the like, [there arises] first a manifestation (<s>nirbhāsa</s>) grounded in the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of blue and the like, and then a manifestation of blue etc. that is bound to the common understanding established by the reflective awareness of that [particular] — and this pair [of cognitions] is both ascertained and constantly observed as competent to determine blue and the like. For the power of determination belongs to cognitions by virtue of their conformity [with the object]; and both of these have the manifestation of blue as the ground for the determination of blue. Therefore the conviction of the ordinary (<s>sāṃvyavahārika</s>) world is that both determine blue alone. But for one whose refuge is the unfettered [analysis] of truthful reasoning and counter-reasoning, it is explained: the first [cognition] is described as the <s>samākhyāti</s> (co-designation), which is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) and of inexpressible [nature], having the character of a determination. The first awareness (<s>ālocanajñāna</s>) is non-conceptual, resembling the cognition of infants, mutes, and the like. Then subsequently, the cognition by which an object is determined through properties such as kind (<s>jāti</s>) and the like — that too, being accepted as perceptual, is a conceptual perception (<s>savikalpaka pratyakṣa</s>) that functions in determining objects like lotuses etc. joined with kind and the like. But the Buddhist (<s>Bauddha</s>) has determined [otherwise]: the first alone is a means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>); the second, however, arises from the aggregate of memory, reflection, and the like — not from the aggregate of the eye and the like. Rather, [it arises] from the aspect grasped by the cognition characterized as the middle state, combined with memory, reflection, etc. — it is not grounded [in perception] — this is what is maintained. The ground of determination, however, [is this:] when the external object such as blue etc. has disappeared, whence could the manifestation of blue etc., which has migrated through the memory of the blue eye[-consciousness], possibly arise? Not from the object, because that has ceased. Not from water etc., because [those are] of the nature of forms etc. that are pervaded [by something else]. For thus it has been said—

children.translated_text: And that universal cognition (<s>sāmānyavijñāna</s>) is understood as conforming [to the object].

children.text: nīlādyākāraleśo yaḥ sa tasmin kena nirmitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever trace of the blue etc. aspect [remains] — by what is that created in that [cognition]?

body.text:
śabdebhyo yādṛśī buddhirnaṣṭe 'naṣṭepi dṛśyate,
tādṛśyeva sadarthānāṃ naitacchotrā (3) dicetasām ||
body.translated_text: The cognition that arises from words — whether the [referent] has perished or not — is the same; this is not [a product] of the ear and other sense-based cognitions, [but] of actual objects.

body.text: iti tathā
body.translated_text: Thus:

body.text:
yadapyanvayivijñānaṃ śabdavyaktyavabhāsiyat |
varṇākṛtyakṣarākāraśūnyaṃ gotvaṃ hi varṇyate |
body.translated_text: And the cognition of a persisting [entity] that manifests as a word-instance — <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) is described as devoid of the form of letters, script, and syllables;

body.text: dravyādyarūpādirūpam | idaṃ tu vikalpakaṃ nīlādyākṛtisākṣarākāraṃ ca sujñātamantarmātrādipari (4) vittirvirbhāvyate | tena na jātyādiparicchedadarpo dvitīyapratyayasya tatpratyanīkarūpādiḥ rūpatvāt | na hi yatra yasya pratibhāso 'saṃbhāvī sa tasya grāhakaḥ pratya-(5)-yasparśākāraśūnya iva rūpa samvedī na sparśasya | tathe damapi nīlādinirbhāsi na tatsvabhāvaśūnyajātyādisaṃvedi vyavasthāpyamāpadyate | tadetarayāṃ ve-(6)-danavivartamātrāyām |
body.translated_text: [It has] the form of substance etc. as non-form etc. But this conceptual [cognition], well-known as having the form of the shape of blue etc. and the form of syllables, manifests as the inner experience etc. Therefore, the pride of determining kind (<s>jāti</s>) etc. does not belong to the second cognition, [because it is] of the nature of form etc. which is the opposite of that [kind]. For where the manifestation of something is impossible, that [cognition] is not the apprehensor of it — just as a cognition empty of the aspect of touch-contact is not a cognizer of touch. Similarly, this [cognition] too, which manifests blue etc., is to be established as not cognizing kind etc. which are empty of the nature of that [blue etc.]. This then, in the mere transformation of that other awareness—

body.text:
'apohaḥ śabdaliṅgābhyāṃ prakāśyata iti lthitiḥ
sādhyate sarvadharmāṇāmavācyatvaprasiddhaye, |
iti sādhyatvamanūdyate |
body.translated_text: '<s>Apoha</s> (exclusion) is illuminated by word and inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>)' — this is the position; it is established in order to prove the inexpressibility of all <s>dharmas</s> (properties).' Thus the status of being provable is being restated.

body.text: rahasyaṃ punaratra, yena nī-(7)-laṃ anīlāpohamparicchidyate pratyayena na tenaivāpohaviṣayatvamātmano vyavasthāpyate, kintarhi, pratyayāntareṇa bādhamātanvatā nīlasvakṣaṇavilakṣaṇatvādetannirbhāsasya | tenedaṃ paraprauḍhaśāstrakṛdbhirapitatpratyayamadhikṛtyocyamānaṃ na mānasasparśiprekṣasya kṣaṇikatvānupapattiścānugata vyavavahārānanyathā siddheḥ śabdaliṅgavikalpāhi sādhāraṇaṃ rūpamanupasthāpayanto na tṛṇakubjīkaraṇe 'pi samarthā ityavivādaṃ, bāhyārthasthitau sthirāsthiravicārāt | taccālīkaṃ vā, ākāro vā, bāhyaṃ vastu veti trayaḥ (2) pakṣāḥ | tatra na prathama pakṣaḥ taddhi tāvadanubhabādeva tathā vyavasthāpyaṃtasyālīkatvenānullekhāt | tathātve vā pravṛttivirodhāt | na hyalīkametadityanubhūyāpyarthakriyārthī pravartate (3) anyanivṛttisphuraṇṇānnaiṣa doṣa iti cet, etadevāsat vidhirūpasyaiva sphuraṇāt | nahi śabdaliṅgābhyāmiha mahīdharoddeśe 'nagni rna bhavatīti skuraṇamapi tvagnirastī-(4) ti | yadyapi nivṛttimahaṃ pratyaimītyādi |
body.translated_text: The secret here, moreover, is this: the cognition by which blue is determined as the exclusion of non-blue (<s>anīlāpoha</s>) — by that very [cognition], the <s>apoha</s>-object-hood of itself is not established. Rather, by another cognition, which extends a sublation (<s>bādha</s>) [of the first], because of [the subsequent manifestation's] being different in nature from the unique particular of blue. Therefore, even when stated by the authors of the opponent's mature treatises with reference to that [first] cognition, it does not touch the mind of the discerning examiner — the impossibility of momentariness, and the impossibility of establishing convention otherwise than through persisting [entities] — verbal and inferential conceptual constructions, presenting a common form, are not capable of even bending a blade of grass — this is undisputed, [but only relevant] in the investigation of stable and unstable [entities] when external objects are accepted. And that [external object] is either illusory (<s>ālīka</s>), or an aspect (<s>ākāra</s>), or an external thing — these are the three positions. Among these, not the first position: for that [object] is to be determined as such precisely from experience — because it is not described as illusory [in experience]. Or if it were so [described], there would be a contradiction with activity [toward it]. For no one who experiences 'this is illusory' still engages [with it] seeking practical efficacy. [Objection:] 'There is no fault, because of the manifestation of the exclusion of the other' — [reply:] that itself is wrong, because what manifests is precisely of a positive form. For from word and inferential mark, in this mountain region, the manifestation is not 'fire does not not exist here,' but rather 'fire exists here.' Even if [one says] 'I apprehend the negation' and so forth—

body.text: yasmādiha dharādharaviśmbharāyāṃ vibhāvasurastīti dhanañjayākāradhāritvādvodhasya tena bodhena dhanañjaya evāvabuddhaḥ | (5) tena vidhereva smaraṇāditi sammatamevāsmākam | alīkamiti tu loke 'prakāśabhṛdbādhyamalīkamāhuriti vacanāt | prakāśyamānaṃ bādhitamucyate | tatkimucyate na (6) tāvattenaivānubhave netyādi bhāṣāmapi tāvadabhyasya nirākāravādinā hi dravyavadekānekavicāracakranikṛttatayā nīlādyākārameva cetaścakramalīkamabhilapyate tadapi na svānubhavaprabhāvādapi tu bādhakabodhādhīnaṃtat | tathā nīla jalajākārākrāntameva svāntamanīlavyāvṛttirityucyate | vyatiriktāyāṃ nīlavyākṛttau tato vyā-(8) vartamānaṃ nīlamanīlameva miledanīlavatā apitu tasmāt-
body.translated_text: Because in this earth-bearing world, fire (<s>Vibhāvasu</s>) exists — since the cognition bears the form of <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (fire), by that cognition, <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (fire) itself is cognized. Therefore, 'from the memory of the positive [form] alone' — this is indeed accepted by us. But 'illusory' [means the following] in common parlance: 'what is sublated while being illuminated is called illusory' — this is the maxim. What is being illuminated and is [simultaneously] sublated is called [illusory]. What then is said? — not merely by that experience itself 'it is not' etc. — having practiced even this much of speech, [we note that] by the proponent of formless [cognition] (<s>nirākāravādin</s>), since [the cognition] has been cut down by the wheel of investigation into one and many like a substance, the very aspect of blue etc. of the mind-wheel is declared illusory — but that too depends not on the force of one's own experience, but on the sublating cognition. Similarly, the mind itself, pervaded by the form of blue lotus etc., is said to be 'the exclusion of non-blue' (<s>anīlavyāvṛtti</s>). If the exclusion of blue were something separate from that [blue], then what turns away from it, [being] blue, would be non-blue, just like the non-blue entity — but rather, from that—

children.translated_text: And therein too, 'the exclusion of the other' [applies] to what is [itself] 'excluded from the other.'
And words, being fixed, conform to the [designative] cause.
The exclusion of another type — the exclusions of those two [word and object]
are the ground of the difference of convention (<s>saṃketa</s>), in conformity with the wish of the knower.

body.text: tatrāpyanyāpohe śabdārthena vyāvṛttiranyānya eva vyāvṛttestu vyāvṛttairnivartamānasya tadabhāvaprasaṅgāt | tathā ca (2) pravṛttera pyabhāvaḥ tasmādya eva vyāvṛtta sa eva vyāvṛttaśabdapravṛttibhedaśca rsaketabhedānuvācyabhedo 'sti |
body.translated_text: And therein too, in the exclusion of the other (<s>anyāpoha</s>), the exclusion through the word-meaning is from the other alone; but if the excluded were to be excluded from [other] excluded [things], then there would be the contingency of its absence. And thus there would also be the absence of activity. Therefore, what is excluded is itself the excluded — and the difference in the application of the word [arises from] the difference of convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) that is to be expressed.

body.text: nanu ca vācyaviśeṣābhāvāt saṃketabhedo 'pyayuktaḥ dvayorekā (3) calanāt, tathā ca vyatirekiṇyā vibhakteraprayogaḥ tasyābhedāśrayatvāt |
body.translated_text: Objection: Since there is no difference in what is to be expressed, the difference of convention too is unjustified, because both are one [and the same]; and thus the use of the negative suffix (<s>vibhakti</s>) would not apply, because it depends on non-difference.

children.translated_text: Even when there is a single designation for both, the negative suffix (<s>vibhakti</s>)
follows as if [applied to] a different meaning, due to the distinction of [even] a trace of what is to be expressed.

body.text: na vai śabdārtha kācidviṣayasvabhāvāyattā vuttirityato vṛttyabhāvaprasaṃgāt yathā vyatirikte 'vyatirikte vā prayoktumiṣyante tathā nirmuktāstamarthamapratibandhena prakāśayanti | tena gau rgau (5)tvamityekārthābhidhāne 'pi kasyacidviśeṣasya pratyayena virudhyate saṃketabhede vyatiriktārthā vibhaktirarthāntaramivādarśayantī pratibhātyanarthāntare 'pi tathā prayoga (6) darśanābhyāsāt | na tāvat sarvatra bhedaḥ anyatrāpi puruṣa iva tasya pratibandhābhāvāt | yathaikaṃ kvacidekatra cānena khyāpyate tadaviśeṣe 'pi gauravādi khyā- (7)-panārthaṃ bahuvacanena prayogābhāvāttu saṃketabhedo na syāt anyasyaiva, tathāhi bhedāntareṇa yadi bhaṇitasyārthaḥ yadāyaṃ pratipattā tadanyavyavacchedabhāvānapekṣaḥ (8) piṇḍaviśeṣe 'śvavyavacchedamātraṃ jijñāsate tathābhūtajñāpanāt tathā ca bhedasaṅketena śabdena bodhyate 'naśvatvamasyāstīti yadā punarvyavacchedāntaranirāṅkṣyastaṃjñā-(9)-tumicchati tadāparityakta vyavacchedāntaraṃ tamevāśvaparicchedāntaraṃ tamevāśvaparicchedaṃ tathā prakāśanāya pramucyate anaśvāyamiti | ata eva pūrvatra pratiṣṭhitapadāntaratvācchabdapravṛtterna samānādhikaraṇyaṃ viśeṣyabhāvo vā gotvamasya śuklamiti tanmātraviśeṣeṇa vuddhe stadāśrayabhūtāyā ekatvenāpratibhāsanāt | nirākāṃkṣatvācca dvitīye tu na bhavati | tathā saṃketavyavahāreṇa saṃketasakalavyacchedadharme vibhāgavat ekasya bahujanena pratibhāsanāt vyavacchedāntarasākāṃkṣatvācca |
body.translated_text: Indeed, no operation of words with respect to their referents is dependent on the essential nature of the object — therefore, because of the contingency of the absence of [any] operation, just as [words] are wished to be employed in what is distinct or non-distinct, so, being released, they illuminate that meaning without obstruction. Thus, even when 'cow' and 'cow-hood' designate one and the same object, [the usage] is contradicted by the cognition of some distinction, [for] when there is a difference of convention, the case-ending, denoting a distinct meaning, appears as if showing a different meaning, even when there is no different meaning — [this is] due to habituation through the observation of such usage. Not everywhere is there difference — elsewhere too, like [the word] <s>puruṣa</s> (person), because of the absence of obstruction to that [identification]. Just as one [thing] is expressed by one [word] in one [place] and by another — even though there is no distinction, because of the absence of usage with the plural for the purpose of expressing heaviness and the like, there should be no difference of convention for another [case]. For thus: if by another difference [of usage] the meaning of what was stated — when this listener, without regard to the exclusion from everything else, merely wishes to know the exclusion from non-horse with respect to a particular individual [horse], then, because [the word] informs him of such a nature, he is informed by a word with a difference-convention [that] 'this is not a non-horse.' But when [the listener], desiring to know [more] without abandoning the other exclusion, wishes to know that very determination-of-horse — at that time, for the purpose of illuminating that very determination-of-horse without abandoning the other exclusion, [the word] 'this is not a non-horse' is released. For precisely this reason, in the former [case], because of being established in another position, the word does not have co-reference (<s>samānādhikaraṇya</s>) or the status of qualifier — [as in] 'cow-hood of this [is] white' — because, in the cognition tinged by that specific qualifier alone, [the qualifier] does not appear as one with its substratum. And because of the absence of further expectancy. But in the second [case], this does not [obtain], because, like a partition, [the word] — through the conventional practice of convention — appears as manifold to many people with respect to the property pertaining to the complete exclusion of convention, and because of the expectancy of further exclusion.

children.translated_text: This alone is the difference everywhere between the two words, the one denoting substance (<s>dravya</s>) and the one denoting a property (<s>bhāva</s>);
there is no [real] distinction whatsoever in the referent of those two [words].

body.text: tasmānna sarvatra dharmadharmivācinoḥ śabdayorvācye 'rthe niścayapratyayavirodhatvena kaścidviśeṣaḥ ekastameva pratyāyanapratikṣiptabhedāntaraḥ pratyāyati (3) anyau'pratikṣepeṇaityayaṃ viśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, not everywhere between the two words — the one denoting the property (<s>dharma</s>) and the one denoting the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) — is there any distinction in the denoted meaning in the sense of contradicting the cognition of certitude. One [word] conveys that very [object] with the other exclusion rejected by the act of conveying; the other [conveys it] without rejection — this is the [only] distinction.

children.translated_text: If one who wishes to inform would speak of that meaning either by a <s>taddhita</s> [secondary derivative suffix] or by a <s>kṛt</s> [primary derivative suffix],

children.text: anyena vā yadi brūyāt bhedo nāsti tato 'paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: or by another [word] — there is no further difference beyond that.

body.text: etāvantameva ca bhedaṃ darśanaṃ śuddhistena....vāde jā-(4)-yeta pācakatvamiti kadā vā pāa iti anyena vā tathābhūtajñāpanāya svayaṃkṛtena samayena na punastathā mūtābhidhānamātreṇārthāntaramevaitadbhavati tathābhūtasyaiva jñā-(5)-panāya śabdasya kṛtasaṃketatvāt | na ca pācakatvamiti tathā ucyate, na pācaka eva atra pākena anya eva kaścitpācako nāmābhidhīyate pāka vicintyate | yat pu-(6)-narasyāmidheyaṃ tat kaścittaṃ taveva pācakatvenāpītyayam |
