body.translated_text: And this much difference is all [there is]: the observation of the purification... in [the example] 'cooking-hood' — or 'when is the cooking?' — or by another [word] for the purpose of informing [someone] of such a nature, by a convention made by oneself. But merely by the designation of something that has become such, it does not become a different meaning, because the word has been conventionally established for the purpose of informing of that very nature. And 'cooking-hood' is not said such that the cook is [something] other [than the cooking]; here 'by cooking, someone else called the cook is being denoted' — [this] does not refer to cooking [as separate]. And what is the denotatum of this [word] — some person is [denoted] by you as having cooking-hood too — this is [the meaning].

children.translated_text: There is no single aggregate from this; even in multiplicity, as before,
because of non-distinction, and because [it does not arise] from atoms — if there is no course [of reasoning], it is not established.
The non-distinction of the distinguished [entities] is their sense-perceptibility (<s>aindriyatva</s>); therefore [they are] non-atomic.
By this, the absence of obstruction (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) and the like has been refuted.

body.text:
saṃkhyāsaṃyogakarmāderapi tadvat svarūpataḥ |
abhilāpācca (8) bhedena rūpaṃ vuddhau na bhāsate |
body.translated_text: Of number, conjunction, action, and the like too, in the same way, from their essential nature and from verbal designation, the form through differentiation does not appear in cognition.

body.text: āvaraṇaṃ hi paramāṇūnāṃ upalabdhaṃ, asaṃsargātkathamiti na yuktam | na hi avayavī pratiṣedhasādhāraṇaṃ kvāpi upalabdhaṃ yena tattvābhāve paramāṇuṣu na syāttathā pratighātādayaḥ | atha
body.translated_text: For the obstruction of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>) is perceived. [To say] 'because of the absence of contact, how [can there be obstruction]?' is not valid. For the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is never perceived anywhere as the common ground for negation — by which, in the absence of that reality, the atoms would not have such [properties as] resistance and the like. Now then —

children.translated_text: From the variegatedness of atoms, the aggregate should [produce] cloth and the like;
how then [would there be] obstruction, whether of heat or of water, for that [aggregate]?

body.text: avayavaiḥ santyāgamantareṇa parimāṇuṣu ca (10) kevalā avyāhataparasparāntarānupradeśāḥ kathamāvaraṇatvāt jātasya vātra ucyate | asaṃsṛṣṭāḥ kathamavayavinaṃ jāyante saṃsargaśca naikadā tadabhāvāt na sarvātmanāṇumātrapiṇḍaprasaṅgāt saṃyogasya padārthāntarasya jananena cet tameva saṃyogaṃ sāntarāḥ kathaṃjayantīti samānaḥ prasaṅgaḥ | saṃsargaścet kiṃ saṃyogenāpare-(2)-ṇa tathā vāpi nā | atha sāntarā eva saṃyogamavayavinañca janayanti tathā satyavaraṇādikāryamapi kiṃna janayanti |
body.translated_text: How, without recourse to anything other than atoms — and among the atoms, [which are] mere [entities] with mutually unobstructed spatial points of each other — can [obstruction] be stated for what has arisen from the nature of obstruction? How do they, being uncontacted, produce a whole (<s>avayavin</s>)? And contact is not [possible] at one time, because of the absence of that [simultaneity]; nor [is it possible] in every respect, because of the unwanted consequence of being a mere atomic mass. If [contact is produced] by the generation of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) as a separate category — how do those [atoms], having intervals between them, produce that very conjunction? The same contingency [applies]. And if there is contact — is it through another conjunction or not?

children.translated_text: Even without the contact of atoms, there is a superior aggregate (<s>saṃhati</s>)
in which, even upon impact, there is never the separate state — that is it.

body.text: na khalu saṃyogaḥ pratibhāsate saṃyoge vyatiriktaḥ, kevalamasaṃyuktayoḥ sāvasthānopalabhyate tau punarupalabhyete tato 'nvayavyatirekābhyāṃ kalpa-(4)-nāmātrametaditi nirṇayaḥ | apratyakṣeṇa te tathābhūtaṃ sacaivaṃbhūtaṃ jātamiti pratītiḥ | tataḥ saivāvasthā pṛthagbhāvena jñāpyate saṃyoga iti | ataeva |
body.translated_text: Indeed, conjunction is not perceived as distinct in [what appears as] conjunction; rather, [merely] a state with a position is apprehended of two things not conjoined. Then those two are [again] apprehended; from that, through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), the determination [is reached that] this is merely a conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāmātra</s>). Through that which is not directly perceived, the cognition [arises that] something of such a nature has indeed come into being as such. From that, that very state is made known through separate existence as 'conjunction.' For this very reason —

children.translated_text: In the cognition [arising] from words, through conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) that follows the distinctions of real entities,
as in the case of qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and the like — [this applies] to the conceptually constructed object, or to those that have perished and [those that have] arisen.

body.text: na śabdajñānena vailakṣyamātrādeva padārthabhedo 'pitu pratyakṣalakṣaṇajñānabhedāt vikalpi-(6)-kāhi buddhiranādivāsanāsāmarthyādupajāyamānā tathā tathā plavate tato nārthatattvaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ labhate | tathānvayavyatirekeṇa parikalpitaṃ bhedamāśritya saṃyogādibūddhayaḥ tataḥ parikalpitasyaiva cotpādanārthatatvasya kalpitārthabhedastu tīrthyāntaradarśanādapyupajāyate | tato 'pyarthatattvavyaksthāyāmanavasthā (8) tathā (8) tathābhyupagamanena parasparāpavādaḥ syāt | tato bhinnaśabdaḥ jñānañca vikalpite vastuni vāsanāyā anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ pravartate kiṃ bhūto 'sau vikalpo vastu-(9)-bhedānusārī vastūnāṃ bhedo vyāvṛttiratathābhūtāt | na vyāvṛttādanyā vyāvṛttiḥ tataḥ sa eva santānāpekṣayārthāntarabhedo bhedena pratibhāti vastubhedama-(10)-ntareṇa ca kalpanā bhedānugā gamyante, yathā eko guṇaḥ ekaḥ samavāyaścaturviśatiḥ guṇāḥ |
body.translated_text: Not from mere distinctiveness of word-cognition is there a difference of category, but rather from the difference of cognitions having the character of perception. For conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpikā buddhi</s>), arising by the power of beginningless latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), floats about thus and thus — therefore the true nature of the object does not find a firm ground [in conceptual cognition]. Likewise, the cognitions of conjunction and the like, resting on the difference conceptually constructed through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) — the difference of conceptually constructed meaning pertaining to that very conceptually constructed productive reality also arises from the view of other schools. From that too, there would be infinite regress in the establishment of the true nature of objects through mutual acceptance this way and that way, [and] there would be mutual refutation. Therefore, differentiated words and cognition operate with respect to a conceptually constructed object through the positive and negative concomitance of latent impressions — what then is the nature of that conceptual construction that follows the distinctions of real entities? The distinction of real entities is exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) from what is not of that nature. There is no exclusion other than the excluded [entity itself]; therefore, that very [entity], with reference to the continuum, appears as a different meaning through differentiation — but without [any real] distinction of entities, the conceptual constructions are understood as following the distinction. Just as: one quality, one inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), twenty-four qualities.

children.translated_text: If you hold that there is secondary usage (<s>upacāra</s>) here, that [usage] whose basis is accepted [by you],

children.text: sa eva sarvabhāveṣu hetuḥ kinneṣyate tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: that very [basis] is the cause in all entities — why is it not accepted for those two?

body.text: ājātāḥ putrā sthaviraṃ tāpayantītivat, atītājātayoryannibandhanamupacārasya niru-(2)-paṇānusmaraṇagṛhītatvena kṣaṇaṃ tadeva nimittamastu vartamānepi saṃyukto ghaṭa ityādāvapi ||
body.translated_text: Just as [in the expression] 'the sons who are yet to be born torment the old man' — for the past and the yet-to-be-born, the basis of secondary usage, being grasped through examination and recollection, let that very moment be the occasion — [this applies] also to the present, as in 'the conjoined pot' and the like.

children.translated_text: If secondary usage (<s>upacāra</s>) is not [present] everywhere, if there is a different qualifier,
if [the meaning is] primary — then from where [comes] the sense of different meaning in the non-different?
Even when there is the property of not being a different meaning, there is non-synonymy in [cases like] 'white' and the like;
words that are connected with number, conjunction, etc. — if there too [you say] there is a different meaning,
there would be no distinction between quality (<s>guṇa</s>) and substance (<s>dravya</s>); [they would be] different due to the difference of exclusions (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>).
Even when there is the property of not being a different meaning, [it could be] like the words for action, substance, and the like.

body.text: nanūpacāro hi nāma mukhyanibandhanaḥ sa kathamasati mukhye bhavet | mukhyañca bhinnaviśeṣaṇaṃ daṇḍyādivat | abhinnaviśeṣa-(5)ṇatve maulī vyavasthitiḥ bhavatastu pūrvapūrvakalpanākṛtaviśeṣaṇayogādabhinnaviśeṣaṇatvenamukhyatvaṃ kvaciditi nopacārasaṃbhavaḥ | bhinnaviśe (5) ṣaṇaṃ mukhyamityeva kṛtaḥ | abhinnaviśeṣaṇamapi kalpanākṛtabhinnaviśeṣaṇamatyantābhyāsāt rūḍhimupagataṃ mukhyameva |
body.translated_text: But secondary usage (<s>upacāra</s>) is by definition based on the primary [meaning] — how can it exist when there is no primary [meaning]? And the primary [meaning] has a different qualifier, like <s>daṇḍī</s> (staff-bearer) and the like. When there is a non-different qualifier, the primary [designation] is the [default] determination. But for you, because of the connection of a qualifier produced by prior conceptual constructions with a non-different qualifier, there is primary status somewhere — hence the impossibility of secondary usage. [You say] 'the primary [meaning] has a different qualifier' — that is stipulated. [But we say:] even that which has a non-different qualifier, being a different qualifier produced by conceptual construction, having attained conventional currency (<s>rūḍhi</s>) through extreme habituation, is itself primary.

body.text:
buddhehaskhalitā vtti rmukhyāropita (7) yoḥ sadā
siṃhe māṇavake tadvadghoṣaṇāpyasti laukikīṃ ||
body.translated_text: The unfailing operation of cognition — [whether applied to what is] primary or superimposed — always, just as in the case of a lion and a boy, there is also a worldly proclamation [that makes the same point].

body.text: iti vacanāt | askhalan gatipratyayaviṣayo hi mukhyaḥ tadaparastu gauṇa iti kinna paryāpyam | yadi viśeṣa-(8)-ṇamaparaṃ nāsti viśeṣyameva tarhi sarvatra vācyam | ityabhinnārthatā paryāyatā rūpābhedena sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ bhinnaviṣayatve hi tadbhavati na buddhaya evahi sva vāsa-(9)-nānurodhādupajāyamānā bhedābhedasāmānādhikaraṇyādivyavahāramuparacayanti na paryāyatādiprasaṅgaḥ anarthāntaratve 'pi dṛśyante aparyāyā akarmmadravyam, adravyaṃ karmmeti prabhṛtayo vyapadeśāḥ | tatra kiṃ vyāvṛttibheda eva nibandhanaṃ nāparaḥ pravṛttinimittabhedaḥ gauḥ śuklo gauḥ śabdatvamiti | punaḥ
body.translated_text: — because of this statement. For the primary [sense] is the object of the cognition of unimpeded movement, and the other is secondary — is that not adequate? If there is no further qualifier, then the qualified [thing] alone is to be denoted everywhere. Thus, synonymy (<s>paryāyatā</s>) is identity of meaning, co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) through non-difference of form. For it [co-referentiality] occurs when the referents are different; but cognitions, arising in conformity with their own latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), construct the conventions of difference, non-difference, co-referentiality, and the like — [hence] there is no unwanted consequence of synonymy. Even in the case of non-difference of meaning, non-synonymous expressions are observed — such as 'non-action substance,' 'non-substance action,' and so forth. [The question is:] is the basis [of convention] the difference of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) alone, or is there another difference in the grounds of application — [as in] 'cow,' 'white,' 'cow,' 'sound-ness'? Furthermore—

children.translated_text: And what is indicated, as if by negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), by entity-denoting words,
by words such as number etc. that denote [something] possessing that — that discriminates another property.
The [verbal] cognition of one who desires to know only that [property], not invoking everything else,
speaks as if of a separate property — like the application of a finger at a particular [point].
The applied finger, because it invokes all [properties] of all [entities], indicates the substrate;
even in the expression of a single meaning, its arrangement is so constituted.

body.text: gauriti tadekākāraparāmarśayogī sakala eva padārtha ucyate | śukla iti tadekadeśaḥ parāmarśāntarayoginī ca vartamānā vyatirekaśca anvayavyatire-(4)kābhyāṃ apovṛtaḥ | tatastasya gauḥ śuklo guṇa iti vyatirekavibhaktistadyathā ḥśilāputrakasya śarīraṃ rāhoḥ śiraḥḥ | yadā ca gavākārāvagrahau nāsti śuklatvameva kevalamupalabhya-(5)-te sambandhiviśeṣarahitam | tadā praśnayati kasyedaṃ śuklatvamiti tadāpūrvadarśanāt avadhṛtagosvabhāvo nirdiśati gauriti tādātmyasambandha evāsya vivakṣito-(6)-vyatirekastu kalpakapravalasya prathamaṃ niścayāt | yadā tu kevalenānena bhavitavyaṃ yadi nāma viśeṣopalakṣaṇamandatā mandalocanānāṃ tathāpi śuklenānena gavānyena bha-(7) vitavyamiti praśnayati | kī'yaṃ śuklo gauranyo veti tadā prativacanaṃ gauriti | samānādhikaraṇatayā tadantarbhāvenaiva praśnabhāvāt | tadanurūpameva prativacanaṃ mūkaṃ ayañca tattvārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Cow' — that entire entity is denoted which is associated with the apprehension of that single form. 'White' — that is a part of it, standing in association with another apprehension, and the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is excluded through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>). Hence the convention 'a cow is white, [white is] a property' is the separation by negative concomitance — just as 'the body of a stone doll' or 'the head of <s>Rāhu</s>.' But when there is no apprehension of the cow-form, and only whiteness is perceived bare, devoid of a particular relatum — then one asks 'whose is this whiteness?' Then, one who has ascertained the cow-nature from previous observation indicates [it as] 'a cow' — the identity relation (<s>tādātmya</s>) alone is intended here. The negative concomitance, however, [arises] from the initial certainty of the powerful conceptual constructor. But when it must be [determined] by this alone — even if the discernment of the particular distinguishing mark is dim for those of dim vision — still, 'with this white [thing], it must be a cow or something else' — thus one asks. The reply is 'a cow' — through co-referentiality, since the question itself involves the inclusion of that [whiteness within the cow]. The reply corresponds exactly to the question — [this is as natural as a reply to] a mute [questioner]. And this is the true meaning.

children.translated_text: When, through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), the determination of negative concomitance [is made],
in the absence of a distinguishing mark, [even] from some [other] cause,

body.text: ayaṃ śaklo ṇuṇo 'śvasya prativākyaṃ vipaścitāt |

children.translated_text: because the question concerns negative concomitance; the conclusion in this matter is precisely so.
But when, without negative concomitance, the particular [property] being subsumed,
the questioner's question arises from considering the course of the evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>),

body.translated_text: 'This is white, a property of a horse' — [this is] the reply of the wise,

children.translated_text: then, one who does not know its nature, [gives] a reply of just such [a kind];
the giver of another [reply] who has not proceeded [to investigate] — there is no occasion for him here.
Having considered the difference [apprehended by] perception, there is no determination of difference;

body.text:
na mūlamanumānasyābhedasyāsambhavo mataḥ |
anvayavyatirekau tu yadānādī vyavasthitau |
tadā bhedasya sadbhāvāt vyavahārastathaiva saḥ |
anādivyavahāro 'yaṃ evameva jarāṅgataḥ |
vastucintā tu lokasya neti bhedo na bādhyate |
body.translated_text: it is not held that inference has no basis, nor that non-difference is impossible. But when positive and negative concomitance have been established as beginningless, then, because of the existence of difference, convention is just so. This convention is beginningless, having reached [the state of] old age. But the world's investigation of reality is not [of this kind] — so difference is not sublated.

children.text: evamapi dravyābhāve ghaṭasya (2) rūpaṃ rūpasya rūpamiti vat syāt tadvyatiriktasyābhāvāt na |
children.translated_text: Even so, in the absence of substance, [one would have to say] 'the form of the pot,' 'the form of form' — and so forth — [this follows] because of the absence of anything distinct from that [form]. [The reply is:] no —
Without preventing the distinctions of capacities such as form and the like, it operates;
the word 'pot' (<s>ghaṭa</s>) [serves] to exclude [other] causes of the same type of result.

children.text: ato na rūpaṃ ghaṭa ityekādhikaraṇā śrutiḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the co-referential expression 'form is a pot' does not [hold];
this is the [nature of] difference — between one denoting a universal (<s>jāti</s>) and one denoting an aggregate (<s>samudāya</s>).
'The form and the like of a pot' — because of being subordinate to that universal,
the distinctions of capacities of that [pot] are made known; by this method, another [entity] too is expressible.

body.text: nanu samāsakṛttaddhiteṣu samvandhā-(4)-bhidhānamanyatra rūḍhi abhinnarūpā 'vyabhicarita sambandhebhyaḥ | yathā rājapuruṣatvaṃ kārakatvamaupagavatvamiti svasvāmisvakriyākārakāpatyāpatyavatsambandhāḥ | asyāpavādaḥ | (5) samāsādrūḍhātkṛṣṇasarpatvam, kṛtasamaratvaṃ taddhitāt hastitvam atra jātimātramucyate na sambandhaḥ taddhitādabhinnarūpācchuklatvaṃ matvarthīyāntopi prakṛtyā tulyarūpatvāt | a (6) trāpi guṇa evābhidhīyate | kṛdanto 'vyabhicaritasambandhaḥ saditi na sattāṃ padārtho vyabhicarati tena sa eva sambandho vācya iti śābdanyāyāt | kathaṃ pācakapācakatvayoreka evārtha iti cet na kriyāsamavāyayornirākṛtatvāt, kalpanākṛtabhede 'pi tādātmyākṣateḥ, kimanupapannaṃ nāma vyāvṛttivyāvṛttaśabdayorekārthatvena tenānyāpoha vi (8) ṣaye tadvatpakṣopavartalūnam |
body.translated_text: Objection: In compounds (<s>samāsa</s>), <s>kṛt</s>-suffixes, and <s>taddhita</s>-suffixes, relation is denoted; elsewhere, conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) is of the same form as [the relations] that are unfailing. For example: 'being a king's man' [denotes] the master-servant relation; 'being an agent' [denotes] the action-agent relation; '<s>aupagavatva</s>' [denotes] the descendant-ancestor relation. Exceptions to this: from the conventional compound, '<s>kṛṣṇasarpatva</s>' (being a black snake); '<s>kṛtasamaratva</s>' (having fought a battle) — from the <s>taddhita</s> suffix, '<s>hastitva</s>' (being an elephant), where only the universal (<s>jāti</s>) is denoted, not the relation. From a <s>taddhita</s> of the same form: '<s>śuklatva</s>' (whiteness) — even with the possessive (<s>matvarthīya</s>) suffix, because the form is similar to the base. Here too, only the quality is denoted. The <s>kṛt</s>-ending [word] has an unfailing relation: '<s>sat</s>' (existing) — the word-entity does not deviate from existence (<s>sattā</s>); therefore, by the principle of verbal [denotation], that very relation is to be denoted. If [one asks] how the agent (<s>pācaka</s>) and the agent-ness (<s>pācakatva</s>) have one and the same meaning — [the reply is:] no, because the action and inherence [relation] have been refuted; even when difference is constructed by imagination, since the identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is unharmed — what is untenable? Since exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) and the word for the excluded have a single meaning, therefore, in the domain of <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other), the position [of the opponent] is correspondingly diminished.

body.text:
'pratyākhyātaṃ pṛthaktvehi syāddoṣo jātiṃtaddhatoḥ' |
taddhato na svatantratvāt asyāyamarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'It has been rejected; for in [the case of] separateness, there would be the fault of [infinite regress regarding] universal (<s>jāti</s>) from a <s>taddhita</s> [suffix].' From the <s>taddhita</s>, because of [its] non-independence — this is the meaning of that.

body.text:
evamiti sacchabdo jātisvarūṣamātropasarjanaṃ dravyamā (9) ha | na sākṣāditi tadbhūtadhaṭādibhedānākṣepāt | sa evātadbhedatve samānādhikaraṇyābhāva na hyasatyāṃ vyāptau sāmānādhikaraṇyamasti | tadyathā śuklaśabdena svābhidheyaguṇa (10) mātraviśiṣṭadravyābhidhānāt | satāmapi dravyamadhurādīnāmanākṣepastataścātadbhedatvamevamanyatrāpi prasaṅgaḥ | jātiśca svarūpañca śabdasya ca upasarjanaṃ dravyamuktaṃ na tadvat ghaṭādibhedastadubhayavyavadhinā ṣāratantryaṃ tataścana ghaṭatvāīnākṣipati | ghaṭatvayogācca, sattāśrayo ghaṭo bhavati | svataḥ yathā rūpaśabdenānākṣiptairmmadhurādibhinnasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ śuklamambumiti tadvat pakṣopavandanaṃ tatpratyākhyātamityācāryavacanai bhāṣyakāra vyākhyāne ca pracarati | kathamayamanucitacintācamatkāritvāt samucitacetā ṇitavān |
ḥna ca nivṛttimātrapratibhāse 'pi pravṛttisambhavaḥ, na hyaghaṭo nāstītyeva ghaṭārthī pravartate api ghaṭo 'stītyādiḥ yato 'ghaṭo nāstītyanyanivṛttirghaṭo vāstīti aghaṭādanyā ihāstīti aghaṭalakṣaṇā-(4)-nyavyāvṛtta ityeka evārthaḥ | ghaṭākāraghaṭitaghoṣonmīṣitamanīṣāyā eva ghaṭaviśeṣe apratiṣṭhitāyāḥ aghaṭavyāvṛttaghaṭe pravṛttinimittatvena nirūpaṇāt | tatpa-(5)-ricchinattitato 'nyavyavacchinatti tṛtīyaprakārābhāvañca sūcayati ityekapramāṇavyāpāra eṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, the word '<s>sat</s>' (existent) denotes substance (<s>dravya</s>), which is subordinate to the mere essential nature of the universal. Not directly — because of the non-prevention of distinctions such as pot etc. that are of its nature. If that [substance] were not of that differentiated nature, there would be no co-referentiality — for co-referentiality does not exist when there is no pervasion. Just as, by the word 'white,' because it denotes substance qualified only by the quality that is its own denotatum — [and yet] there is the non-prevention of [qualities] such as sweetness etc. of substances that exist [alongside] — from that, this very state of not being of that differentiated nature [follows]; the same unwanted consequence applies elsewhere too. Both the universal and the essential nature, and substance as subordinate to the word — it is not the case that the distinctions such as pot-ness etc. [are prevented by that]; since [the universal is] the principal [referent], therefore it does not prevent pot-ness etc. And from the association with pot-ness, the substrate of existence (<s>sattā</s>) becomes a pot. Just as, by the word 'form,' there is co-referentiality with sweetness etc. that are not prevented — 'white water' — so too the position is conciliated. That has been rejected — as the words of the Master (<s>Ācārya</s>) [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] and the Commentator's (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s) explanation proceed. How this [thinker], because of being astonished by inappropriate reflection, has [wrongly] considered [it] with a properly collected mind. And in the appearance of mere cessation too, there is no possibility of positive engagement — for one seeking a pot does not engage [merely thinking] 'a non-pot does not exist,' but rather 'a pot exists' — and so forth. Because 'a non-pot does not exist' [means] the exclusion of what is other, and 'a pot exists' [means] what is other than a non-pot exists here, [i.e.,] what is not excluded from what is characterized as non-pot — this is a single meaning. Since the intellect, whose light is stirred by the sound fashioned in pot-form, which is not established in a particular pot, is analyzed as having as its ground of engagement a pot that is excluded from non-pot — it determines that, and thereby excludes the other; and it indicates the absence of a third alternative — this is a single operation of a [single means of] valid cognition.

body.text: tena aghaṭasyaiva nivṛttiriti pratītau nāyaṃ doṣa iti cet, ghaṭanivṛttyapratikṣepe niyamasyaivāsiddheḥ | tatprakṣepe tu kastato 'nyo vidhiḥ, niṣedhapratikṣepasyaiva vidhitvāt iti vivakṣitamevodyotitam | yato ghaṭa sārūpyasphuraṇādevaṃ taditaranirākaraṇaṃ, tadanupalambharūpatvā diti kathitamevaṃ prathamaṃ bādhakapratyayāduttarasamayasambhavinaḥ punastadalīkatvakalpanamekeṣām |
body.translated_text: If [one says:] there is no fault in this, because the cognition is the cessation of non-pot alone — [the reply is:] because the restriction itself is unestablished when the exclusion of pot-cessation is not admitted. But when that exclusion is admitted, what positive [content] is there other than that? — since the exclusion of negation is itself the positive [content]. Thus what was intended has been illuminated. Since the flashing of similarity to a pot [leads to] the negation of what is other than that, and since that [negation] has the form of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) — this has been stated. First, from the sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka-pratyaya</s>), some [thinkers] construct the falsity of [entities] arising at a subsequent moment.

body.text: yatpunarucyate-svarūpabheda e (8) vānyāpoho 'nyāpoḍharūpatvādvidhiriti cet na alauṃkapakṣe tadabhāvāt tasya svarūpavidhānavalīkatvaprasaṅgāt | svalakṣaṇasya vikalpānarohāditi-tadapyetena dūṣitam-(9) ghaṭasārūpyasphuraṇenāghaṭanivṛttasthūlamūlavastuvidhiravibhūta eva buddhayāpyavasīyate tadūrdhvaṃ dhvaṃsate bādhakāditi ko 'parādhaḥ prathamabodhasya prathamabodhāpekṣayā(10) ca idamudīryate tvayā vikalpe svalakṣaṇānārohāditi na saṅgataṃ sajātīyavijātīṃyavyāvṛttapratiṣṭhitaghaṭākārapaṭu pratyakṣāpekṣayā vastu svalakṣaṇamucyate | tadeva vastuvijātīyatvāvṛttamullikhatā vikalpena samārūpyavaśāt sāmānyalakṣaṇamadhyavasāyaṃ vikalpamityucyate-tadapi sthūlamūlasvarūpa [2] sparśādyatiriktajātyādipadārthānupalambhāt, bhede ca ghaṭādikamidānīmevaṃvidhamadhyavasīyate, ityarthamabhisaṃdhāya vikalpe svalakṣaṇametat vyāvṛttamābhātīṃtyucyate | ubhayato vyāvṛttasya hitadekasmādapi tasya vyavacchedo 'stīti na hyanīlamutpalaṃ na bhavatīti bhaṇyate | tathā coktamḥ-
body.translated_text: As for what is further stated — 'The exclusion from others (<s>anyāpoha</s>) is nothing but the differentiation of essential form; because it has the form of what is excluded from others, it is a positive determination (<s>vidhi</s>)' — if so, [we reply:] No, because in the Buddhist thesis that is absent, [and] because [such a claim would lead to] the unwanted consequence that its positive determination of essential form would be illusory. 'Because the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) does not ascend into conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>)' — that too has been refuted by this: through the manifestation of the resemblance to a pot, the positive determination of the gross, fundamental entity — which has turned away from non-pot — is ascertained by the intellect even without being manifested [directly]. Afterward it collapses due to a defeating cognition — what is the fault of the initial cognition? And with reference to that initial cognition, this is stated by you: 'Because the particular does not ascend into conceptual construction' — [but] this is not coherent. With reference to a perception that is sharp [in apprehending] the pot-form established through the exclusion from what is homogeneous and heterogeneous, the entity is called a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). That very entity, being scratched by a conceptual construction that excludes it from what is of a heterogeneous kind, is called a general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) by force of resemblance — [this is] the determination called conceptual construction. That too, because of the non-apprehension of categories such as universal (<s>jāti</s>) etc. that are distinct from the gross, fundamental, essential form, touch, etc., and because in difference, a pot etc. is now determined as being of such a kind — with this meaning in mind, it is said: 'In conceptual construction, this particular appears as excluded.' Since what is excluded from both [homogeneous and heterogeneous] — even of that [entity], there is delimitation from even one [of them], for indeed it is not said 'what is not blue is not a lotus.' And thus it has been stated:

children.translated_text: What is the opposite of what has been described — that is called a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>);
the general (<s>sāmānya</s>) is threefold — based on existence, non-existence, and both.
If the cognition based on existence [is proposed], the entity [would exist only] in conformity with entity;
it is not [so], because of not being a reply to what was stated, and because of what has been observed; and regarding the past etc., it would be otherwise.
If [one objects that] there is a loss of entity-property-hood — [the reply is:] preceded by the apprehension of the entity,
that cognition [arises] — this is no fault. But the measurable (<s>meya</s>) is one: the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: tasya svapara rūṣābhyāṃ gatermeyadvayaṃ matam |
body.translated_text: Because of its movement through its own and other forms, the dual measurable is accepted.

body.text: vidhirapi vidhirūpatāyāmavidhi dharmatvaṃ vyavacchinnasvabhāvamapekṣamāṇaḥ kathaṃ [6] na sāpekṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Even positive determination (<s>vidhi</s>), in the [state of having] the form of positive determination — [when it] requires the property-hood of non-determination, [which has] a delimited essential nature — how is it not dependent [on something else]?

body.text: ḥtataḥ pratītāvitaretarāśrayatvamuktaṃ saṅketesañcārya yatparihṛtaṃ jñānaśriyā tadetat grāmyajanadhandhīkaraṇaṃ golakādiṃvat, sthānāntarasañcārānḥ iti mitrapādān prati upālambho na śakyaḥ vidhisphuraṇasyaiva svīkārāt sa ca vidhiḥ śabdāt pratīyamānaḥ saṃketānusāreṇa pratyetavyaḥ, saṃketaśca nāpratīte 'rthe tasmāt [8] saṅkete kathaṃ sañcārya parihṛtaḥ parasparāśrayadoṣaḥ tathā coktam
body.translated_text: Therefore, the mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśrayatva</s>) in cognition has been stated. What was resolved by <s>Jñānaśrī</s> [<s>Jñānaśrīmitra</s>] by transferring [the problem] to convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) — that is [merely] a bewildering of village people, like [a trick with] a ball etc. [The objection:] 'Because of transfer to another locus' — the reproach against <s>Mitrapāda</s> is not possible, because of the acceptance of the very manifestation of positive determination. And that positive determination, being cognized from the word, must be understood in accordance with convention; and convention does not [apply] to an object not [yet] cognized. Therefore, how is the fault of mutual dependence resolved by transferring [it] to convention? And thus it has been stated:

children.translated_text: In apprehending the meaning 'tree' through the exclusion from non-tree, a pair [is needed];
there is mutual dependence — in the absence of the apprehension of one, there is non-apprehension of both.
'Therefore, convention is impossible' — thus some declare.
In their [view], are the non-trees delimited in the convention, or not?
If delimited, how are they known without prior apprehension of 'tree'?
If they are not excluded in the convention, then for those who engage in usage,
there would be no activity [directed at] the exclusion of those [non-trees] — like the location of a tree.
Without positively determining [anything], prohibiting the other, and displaying the one [object] present before [oneself] —
'This is a tree' — thus convention is made, [and] one understands that.
'Even in conventional usage, this is no fault' — if [one says this about] the tree,
the unwanted consequence that 'this too is just this' does not cease;

children.text: eka pratyavamarśākhye jñāne ekatra hi sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for in the cognition called 'reflective awareness' (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>), [the object] is established in one [cognition] alone.
Having reached that, [the mind] itself distinguishes the objects that are causes of that and non-that;
entities that abide in the cognition of that appear as the cause of the cognition.
Those of a non-causal form, deficient, as if of manifold form,
[the mind] apprehends as different — this statement applies [only] to [the case of] difference.

body.text: idameva paramasubhāṣitāmṛtamapi ca te sādhūriti piṣṭaṃ piṣyate [3] yatpunaratī(ti)viśaṅkarakaleva mīlanādidhana pratyayādudbhāṣitam | vidhyalīkamiti cet | ḥ
body.translated_text: This alone is the supreme nectar of well-spoken [words]. And moreover, 'you are excellent' — [but] this is grinding what is already ground. As for what was further uttered — as if from the cognition of the property of closing the eyelids etc. [described as] extremely <s>Śaṅkara</s>-like skeleton — 'the positive determination is illusory' — if [one says] so:

body.text: ḥna vyāghātāt | kiñciditi hi vidhyarthī na kiñciditi cālīkārthaḥ | atadrūpaparāvṛttimātreṇālīkatve svala[4]kṣaṇasyāpyalīkatvāditi (prasaṃgāt) | ḥ tadapi kaḥ spṛśantu | yathātatvamanavasāyo yathāvasāyamatattvāt | sāmvṛto vidhipratyakṣapratibhāsavidheranya evāyam | tataśca dvividho vidhiḥ pāramā [5] rthi ko yasyārthasya sannidhānā sannidhānābhyāṃ jñānapratibhāsabhedastatsvalakṣaṇaṃ asādhāraṇaṃ tattvaṃ vastutaḥ tadeva paramārthasat arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatvā [6] dvastunaḥ | anyatsāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ so 'numānasya viṣayaḥ grāhyaviṣayabhedaścāyam | adhyavaseyaviṣayabhedastu tiryagūrdhvatātmakāni yatropayogā tadrūpaparāvṛ[7] ttaghaṭādisvabhāvaḥ svalakṣaṇamevaikato vyāvṛttamucyate utpalavat |
body.translated_text: [We reply:] No, because of self-contradiction. For the one who intends positive determination [says] 'something [exists],' while the one who intends illusion [says] 'nothing [exists].' If by mere exclusion from what is not of that form there were illusoriness, then even the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) would be illusory — because of [this] unwanted consequence. But who cares even about that? [For] as [the object] truly is, so it is not determined; as it is determined, so it is not the true [object]. The positive determination [appearing in] convention is [from] the manifestation of perception — this [conceptual] positive determination is quite different from that. And therefore, the positive determination is twofold: the ultimate (<s>pāramārthika</s>) — that by whose object's presence or absence there is a difference in the manifestation of cognition — that is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), the uncommon reality, which is in truth the ultimately real, because the nature of an entity is characterized by the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>). The other is the general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>); that is the object of inference (<s>anumāna</s>); and this is the distinction of the apprehended object. But the distinction of the determined (<s>adhyavaseya</s>) object — whether oblique or vertical in nature — where there is application, the pot etc. whose essential nature is excluded from what is of another form, being the particular excluded from one [side], is said [to be the svalakṣaṇa], like a lotus.

children.translated_text: The non-entity form is not of that [particular] itself, because of the means of proof for what is thus established;
if elsewhere there is no establishment of another — [then] not from the establishment of that itself.
Due to non-conformity [with the object], the second [cognition] is accepted as erroneous;
and if [there is] movement through another's form — but there is no validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>) for error.
Even from non-discordance with intention, there is validity of error;
movement is also seen otherwise; and this thesis has been internally resolved.

body.text: pratyakṣavikalpe ca ghaṭa eva sphurati kevalaṃ ekatra sphuṭatayā anyatrāsphuṭatayā na ca viśeṣaṇabhedena viśeṣyamapi bhidyate | tenobhayathāpi ghaṭa evāyamudayanācāryaḥ dṛśyavikalpyāvarthau ekīkṛtya vyavahārapravṛttiriti vyākhyātarambha alīkānalīkatvādiyathāruci racayanti na vyavahartāraḥ iti puruṣadvayāpekṣayā pi tu jñānasya svākāravaśādgrahaṇaṃ [2] sādhāraṇameva | anyathā hi bādhakapratyayabalāt alīkākāravikalpacalanādeva tathātva kathaṃ sthāpyaṃ tadarthākāratvañca | atha grahaṇanibandhanaṃ pratyakṣetarayoḥ samānam | parastu pāramārthi [3] kaḥ śabdajñānagṛhīto ca iti manyate tena tadabhimānasthalo 'yaṃ bādhakāvatāraḥ tadevamubhayato vyāvṛttaghaṭākāraṃ jñānagrāhyaṃ grahaṇamekato vyāvṛttākāraṃ jñānaṃ grahaṇam [4]vyavasāya iti pratītidvayavyavasthā | avidyamāne 'tyarthe 'nubhavāvidmāvāsanāvaśagavikalpākāravaśāt grahaṇamatrāropaṇaṃ tadviṣayaścāropita ucyate | sa ca vidhirapi pratītyartho [5] pi na sambhavati, vikalpe svalakṣaṇasyānyavyāvṛttatayā saṃsparśāt virodhāt ubhayato vyāvṛttasyāpi ghaṭasya vijātīyavyāvṛttaghaṭamātragrahaṇāt sajātīyabhe-[5]-dagrahaṇa sāmarthyāt | na ca svalakṣaṇasya bhāvanāvidhitvaparihāreṇa sphuraṇam | na cālīkamapyalīkatvena tenaiva jñānena gṛhyate,
body.translated_text: In both perception and conceptual construction, it is the pot alone that appears — merely in one case with clarity, in the other without clarity. And the qualified object (<s>viśeṣya</s>) is not split by the difference in the qualifier. Therefore, in both cases, it is the pot alone. The revered teacher <s>Udayana</s>, having unified the perceived and the conceptually constructed objects, has explained [that] conventional activity [proceeds thus]. The [Buddhist] commentators fashion at will the illusoriness or non-illusoriness etc. [of the conceptual object] — but those who engage in convention do not [care about that]. And with reference to both persons [i.e., both the Buddhist and the realist], the apprehension by cognition through the force of its own form is common. For otherwise, how could the nature of being of that object's form be established [for cognition] merely by the wavering of the illusory-form conceptual construction, through the force of a defeating cognition? Now, if the basis of apprehension is the same in both perception and the other [i.e., inference], but the opponent considers [that] the one is ultimate and the other apprehended by verbal cognition — therefore, this [is where] the defeating cognition enters at the locus of that [opponent's] conceit. Thus, the pot-form excluded from both [homogeneous and heterogeneous] — apprehended by cognition — is the apprehension; the form excluded from one [side] — the cognition is the apprehension, [i.e.,] the determination (<s>vyavasāya</s>). Thus the two cognitions are [respectively] established. When the object does not exist [as conceptualized], the apprehension — through the force of the form of conceptual construction [arising] under the power of the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the experience of ignorance — is here a superimposition; and its object is said to be superimposed. And that positive determination too, even as the intended meaning, is impossible — because in conceptual construction, the particular is touched [only] through its being excluded from others, [which involves] a contradiction; and because even the pot excluded from both [sides] is apprehended merely as a pot excluded from the heterogeneous, [there exists] the capacity for apprehending homogeneous difference. And it is not the case that the particular manifests without the removal of the positive determination of being the object of meditation. Nor is the illusory apprehended as illusory by that very cognition —

body.text: 'apramāṇāṇāmapi svārthe pramāṇamiva lakṣyate' iti nyāyāt |
body.translated_text: 'Even of non-<s>pramāṇas</s>, regarding their own objects, it is observed as if [they were] a <s>pramāṇa</s>' — by this principle.

body.text: ubhayorāpi grāhakavikalpaāsthākāravilāsāt prakārāntatveṇāprathanām prathamā na rūpasambhavavācyakālpanikasyāpyaṃśa(8) bhāvasyāta eva na mūlo niṣṭhuranyāyakṣaṇaraprahāra pratyāśāparasya |
body.translated_text: In both [cases] — from the play of the form of the apprehending conceptual construction — through the non-manifestation of a different mode, the first [cognition] is not [established] as having the possibility of the form, even of a fictional portion — for precisely this reason, [the argument] is not the root [refutation], for one whose expectation is for the blow of [the opponent's] harsh logical argument.

body.text: anyopohalakṣaṇaśabdārthe jātidharmmāpi kalpyamānā ekatvanityatva nityatvapratyekaparisamāptatvalakṣaṇā vya-[9]-vatiṣṭhante | abhedāśrayā vicchedāt kaścārtha (tenārtha) pratīteśca | tathāhi |
body.translated_text: Even the universal (<s>jāti</s>) as a property — when imagined in the word-meaning characterized by exclusion from others (<s>anyāpoha</s>) — is established as having the characteristics of unity, eternality, and completeness in each instance. From non-difference [as] the basis, because of [its] severance — what meaning [is there] by that (meaning)? And because of the cognition [arising]. For thus:

children.translated_text: Whatever cognition follows non-difference, [there is] some [cognition] in the perception of two entities,
without convention, having proximity as its basis in relation to the essential meaning.

body.text:
pratyāsattirvinā jātyā yatheṣṭā cakṣurādiṣu |
jñānakāryeṣu jātirvā yathānveti vibhāgatḥ |
body.translated_text:
Proximity without universal (<s>jāti</s>) is accepted as desired, as in the eye etc.;
or how the universal follows in effects of cognition — this is [to be understood] from analysis.

body.text: yathā tāvadabhedapratyayajananasāmagrī yadutārthamekaṃ śrāvaṇeyaṃ avalokya dvitīyaṃ cākaleyaṃ anyaṃ vā govyaktibhedamavadhārayanna bhinnapratyayavān bhavati ayamapi gaurayamapi gauriti aparāparālokane ca vardhamānā bhinnabuddhitvādvardhamā (2) naṃ sāmānyamāmnāyate abhedaśca gopiṇḍamaṇḍalānāṃ khaṇḍamuṇḍādibhede 'pi vijātīyamātrābhinnārthapratīteḥ | padārthānāmeva dharmmaḥ sajātīyādapi viśeṣapratītau bheda pratītiriti vyavahāraḥ samastagopiṇḍamaṇḍalapradhvaṃsābhāvān, kālākalākalāpakalamānnityatvamapi vijātīyāpohapadārthasya sarvātmanā ca pratyekamanyāpoḍha (4) pratyaya ḍhaukanāt | pratyekaparisamāptiḥ sudṛḍhā alīkatvañca asya bādhakādhīnamiti, tadapekṣayāmi yadamunā pratītaṃ tadātadanyathākartumaśakyaṃ alīkakalpanayā vastupratibaddha(5) metat nabhavati pratyakṣapratibhāsavat, tadabhāve 'pi smaraṇavadasyotpatirityeva syāt, yatratu pratibaddhā vyavasāyaprasavastatra bhāvikatvamevālīkatve 'pyākārasyāpoḍhatva-(6)-sya bhāvepi bāhye bhāvāt anyopoḍhatvamevānugamaḥ, sa ca vāstavo 'pi samvādāt kālpaniko pi kalpanā buddhau vivartanāt | nahi kṣaṇikābuddhirananugamāvā bāhyapadārthā (7) gamamakṣikatcaṃ vā pratyetuṃ akṣamāsmaraṇavat, yathā hi smaraṇamanatītamapi svayamatītatvaṃ smarati tathedamapi āropitastūcyate, yacca padārtho vikalpārūḍhagrāhyākārapratibhāsādgahītaḥ sa āropita ucyate, yathā bāhyārthābhāve 'piṃ saṃnidhāne 'saṃnidhāne vā śītārthena vahniñcintitastatra vahnirubhayavyāvṛtto nāsti vijātīyavyāvṛttastvāsti cintā sā-(9)-rūpyavaśāt pratītaḥ sa āropita ucyate asatvyāpītyapi bādhakapratyayavaśena tathātvāvasthābhedāgraho 'pi vijātīyabhedapratīte sajātīyādbhedagrahaṇasāmarthyam |

tenevaṃ nirastaṃ ḥsādhāraṇaṃ ca rupaṃ vikalpagocaraḥ, na cālīkaṃ tathā bhavitumarhati | tasya hi deśakālānugamo na svābhāvikaḥ, tuccharūpatvāt | na kālpanikaḥ tasyākṣaṇikatvāt | nāropitaḥ anyatrā(2)pyaprasiddheḥ |

bhedāgrahādekatvamātramanusandhīyate iti cet na bhāvikasyabhedasyābhāvāt, bhāve vā kālpanikatvasya vyāghātāt | paramārthāsataḥ paramārthābhedaparyavasāyitvāt | āropitasyāgrahānupapatteḥ abhedāropānavakāśācca | āro pitāsattvasya paramārthasatveprasaṅgam catuḥkoṭivinirmuktasyāpratisañjakatvāt | tadagrahasya trailokye 'pi sulabhatvāt |

anyatrāpi pāramārthikabhedapratīto kathamabheda āropyatāmiti cet evaṃ tarhi yasya pratibhāse yannāropyate niyamena tasyaivāprakāśe tadāropyaṃ na tvevannāmamātrakasyātiprasañjakatvāt | ata eva na vyadhikaraṇasyāpi sato 'sato vā bhedasyāgrahī'bhedāropopayogīti |

ṭīkākāramatamavagamya kiṃmava valayitabhava anena tanmate (6) kilāropo nāma sādharmyadṛgapekṣaḥ kvaci t kasyacidupacāro rajatasyaiva śuktau vivākṣitaḥ | tato 'yaṃ kugrāmavāstavya baṭujavyapetavyaḥ | jalpanīyamanalpaṃ pa (7) ryante kimapi bhaviṣyati labdhaṃ tāvat granthakārayaśaḥ ityāśayenābhihitavān | 'nāpinyāyādapohasiddhitadabhāvādityādyapi prativihitam |

yatpunarbhāvābhāva-(8)-sādhāraṇyaṃ vikalpitaṃ na tāvat ubhayarūpatvaṃ virodhāt | na taddharmatvam anamyupagamāt | nahi gotvamabhāvasyāpi dharma ityamyupagamyate | na taddharmitvam, anekāntāt | vyakti(9)rapi hi bhābābhāvaśālinī na niṣedhaikarūpeti | na tadubhayāsādṛśyamasambhavāt | atannivṛttyaiva tathātve sādhyāviśeṣāt | nāpyasti nāsti sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ vi (10) rodhādanyathā siddheśca | nahi yadasti tannāstīti pratyayagocaraḥ syāt | prakārāntaramāśritya syādeveti cet evaṃ tarhi tameva prakārabhedamupādāya vidhivyavasthā yāṃ ko virodhaḥ yena pratibandha siddhayet | ḥtasya vidhirūpatāyāmastinā kimadhikamupaneyamiti cet niṣedharūpatve 'pi kimadhikamapaneyamiti samānam | ata eva sādhāraṇyamiti cet tathāpi kimetadubhayātmakamubhayaparihāro veti aśakyametat | tasmādastināstibhyāmupādhyantaropasaṃprāptiḥ prāptopādhi niyamo beti sārthakatvaṃ tayoḥ | tadetadvidhāvapi tulyam | śāntā (3) śeṣaviśeṣatvādalīkapakṣe kvopādhyantaravidhistanniyamoveti viśeṣadoṣaḥ | tato gośabdo gotvaviśiṣṭavyaktimāyābhidhāyī paryavasitaḥ | tāstu viprakīrṇadeśakālatayārthakriyā (4) rthiprārthanāmanubhavitumīśata iti pratipattā viśeṣākāṃkṣaḥ | sā ca tasyākāṃkṣāsti goṣṭhe kālākṣī dhanurghaṭoghnīmahāghaṇṭānandinīnyādibhirniyāmakai rvidhāyakairvā nivāryata iti (5) vidhau na kaściddoṣaḥ | iti | tadapi nirlakṣaṇaśaramokṣaprakhyāmīkṣyate | tathāhi vṛkṣa, śabdena vṛkṣavidhireva kṛtaḥ, satuvidhiryathā pratyakṣeṇa anupālambhātmanā vā tena (6) pratiṣedhaḥ kriyamāṇaḥ śakyate naivāsti nāstiśabdābhyāṃ sambaddhamasti niyatatvāt nāsti niyatatvādeva vā tathā kimayaṃ śabdo vidhiḥ 'ābhyāṃ padābhyāṃ sambaddhaṃ yogyaṃ (7) upadarśyate' | tathā cedasti nāsti padasambandhasādhāraṇa upadarśitaḥ | tat sādhāraṇañcāvṛkṣavyāvṛttaṃ vā vṛkṣārthavidhāyitayā tathābhūtaścārthaḥ bāhyapadārthasya (8) abhāvaniyatasya bhāvaniyatasya vā sajātīyavyāvṛttayā tathākhyātasyānena tathākhyānābhāvātaṃ | sa ca śabdārthaḥ sādhāraṇo vā bhāvābhāvayordṛṣṭatvāt sādhāraṇaṃ tu (1)ko yathā nityāninyayordṛṣṭatvāt, prameyatvaṃ vastutvaṃ vā sādhāraṇamuktaṃ tadvat | na tu bhāvābhāvātmakatvādubhayasādhāraṇaḥ śeṣamapi kalpanaṃ aphalamanyathaiva vivakṣitatvāt | sarvasyaiva hi dharmarūpasya śābdasya tādṛśadharmmadvaye dṛṣṭatvāt | sādhāraṇyamābālamavagatam | tathāhi |
iti bhaṭṭamatam |
dṛṣṭiṃ bhedāśrayaiste 'pi tasmādajñātaviphlavāḥ ||

bhāvābhāvayordarśanādvikalpa prati (5) bhāsasya sādhāraṇyamuktaṃ pūrvārddhena | dvitīyārdhena aparamārthaviṣayatvasādhyadharmābhāvena sādhanadharmasya bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyasyābhāvo darśitaḥ | śrotrādi (6)cetasi vipakṣadharmiṇi tataścāyaṃ prayogaḥ prajāyate | yaḥ pratyayo yasyārthasya bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇapratibhāsaḥ sa paramārthatastadviṣayo na bhavati | yathā (7) saṃśayapratyayapratibhāsaḥ svārthasammataḥ śarkarādyarthabhāvābhāvasādhāraṇapratibhāsaśca śarkarādivikalpapratibhāsaḥ vyatirekeṇa yaḥ paramārthataḥ (8) pratyayo yadviṣayaḥ sa tasyārthasyānvayavyatirekāvanuvidhatte | yathā madhuragāndhāradhvanibhāvābhāvānu vidhāyīśrotrabodhaḥ | śarkarālakṣaṇasvārthabhāvābhāvā (9) nuvidhāyī ca na bhavati śarkarāvikalasya pratibhāsaḥ paramārthatastadviṣayatvaṃ tadutpattisambadhanibaṃdhanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrotraprarūpa pratyayapratibhāso yadi tadabhāveti (10) paramārthatastadviṣayatvaṃ syāt | tadā saṃśayaviparyāsapratyayapratibhāsasyāpi syāt na ca tayostathātvamanumanyate prāmāṇikena nāvālambanapratyayatvā bhāvādaparamatau kāraṇaṃ śakyaṃ kalpayitum | yathā go jñānaṃ tāvat viṣayaṃ aparamapi ca na yuktam |
body.translated_text: By the first half [of the verse], it was stated that the conceptual appearance (<s>vikalpa-pratibhāsa</s>) is common to both existence and non-existence (<s>bhāva-abhāva</s>) — [this is] from the perception [of both]. By the second half, the absence of the property to be proved — namely, non-ultimate objecthood — demonstrates the absence of the proving property, namely the commonality of existence and non-existence. In the counter-example (<s>vipakṣa</s>) subject — [such as] the ear and mind — the following argument then arises: whatever cognition has an appearance common to the existence and non-existence of a [given] object, that is not ultimately an object of that [cognition] — just as the appearance in a cognition of doubt is accepted [by both sides] regarding its own object; and the conceptual appearance regarding sugar etc. has an appearance common to the existence and non-existence of the sugar etc. object. By negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>): whatever cognition is ultimately an object of a [given] entity, that follows the positive and negative concomitance of that entity — just as the auditory cognition follows the presence and absence of a sweet <s>gāndhāra</s> note. But the appearance of the sugar-conceptual [cognition] does not follow the presence and absence of its own object characterized as sugar — [therefore] its ultimate objecthood [is denied]. That [ultimate objecthood's] basis is seen to be the connection with the arising of that [object]. The appearance in auditory cognition — if that [object] is absent, then there would be ultimate objecthood [for the conceptual cognition too]. But then the appearance of doubt and erroneous cognition would also have [ultimate objecthood] — and that is not accepted by one who relies on evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Because of the non-existence of the causal-condition relation (<s>ālambanapratyayatva</s>), no other cause can be imagined. Just as cow-cognition, for the time being, [has] an object — but another [object] is not justified.

children.translated_text: And that [cognition] is seen to be in conformity with the universal cognition (<s>sāmānyavijñāna</s>);
the trace of form such as blue etc. that [appears] — by whom is it created in that [universal cognition]?

body.text: iti yat yat pratibhāsaṃ vijñānaṃ na bhavati na tattadviṣayaṃ vyavahartavyam | yathā go jñānaṃ aśvaviṣayaṃ na vyavahṛyate varṇakṛtyakṣarākārābhāsaṃ kalpavijñānaṃ, na varṇakṛtyakṣarākāraśūnyaparasammatasāmānyapratibhāsaṃ tadviṣayatvaṃ hi pratibhāsatvena vyāptarūpābhāsasya rūpaviṣaye dṛṣṭaṃ rase (4)canopanaddhaṃ paramārthata iti viśeṣaṇāt sāṃvṛtaṃ na pāryate | paramārthaśca pratiṣṭhito bhāvasvabhāvo 'rthakriyāsamarthaḥ | pratyakṣapratibhāsitaḥ sarvavyavahartṛṇāṃ hānopādānasamī (5) hāviṣayaḥ prakāśyate-
body.translated_text: Thus, whatever cognition does not have a [particular] appearance, that should not be conventionally treated as having that [particular] object. Just as cow-cognition is not conventionally treated as having a horse as its object. Conceptual cognition (<s>kalpavijñāna</s>), whose appearance is of letters, case-endings, and syllable-forms, [is not] an appearance of the universals accepted by others that are devoid of letter, case-ending, and syllable-form — [therefore it does not have] objecthood of that [universal]. For objecthood is seen to be pervaded by appearance-ness, in the case of form-appearance having form as its object — [this] is ultimately [so], by the qualifier 'ultimately'; the conventional [objecthood] is not thereby defeated. And the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) is the established essential nature of an entity, capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>); it is directly manifested in perception and is disclosed as the object of the endeavors of acceptance and rejection of all who engage in conventional practice —

body.text:
arthakriyāsamartha yattadeva paramārthasat |
anyat saṃvṛtisat proktaṃ te svasāmānyalakṣaṇe | ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'That which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>) — that alone is ultimately real (<s>paramārthasat</s>). The other is declared to be conventionally real (<s>saṃvṛtisat</s>). Those two are [respectively] the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) and the universal (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>).' — This is the meaning.

body.text: tenedamasaṃlagnam 'tadyadigovikalpasyāśvaviṣayatvameva tadbhāvāsādhāraṇyaṃ gavyapi bāhye tathā, tataḥ sādhyaviśiṣṭatvam' |
body.translated_text: Hence this [objection] is not connected: 'If the cow-conceptual [cognition] has a horse as its object, then there is commonality with the existence [of that object] — and the same would apply to an external cow; hence [the proof] would be no different from what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).'

body.text: arūpādiviśeṣākāṅkṣā tadāsādhāraṇyam, nahyudāhṛto govikalpo 'śvāityādiviśeṣamākāṅkṣati | niyamavidhau tu virodha eva | na hyatadviṣayasya tadviśeṣaniyamākāṅkṣā nāma, gojñānasyāśvaviśeṣa niyama' kāṃkṣāprasaṅgāt | tadīyasadasatvānupadarśanaṃ cet tato 'siddhirdoṣaḥ | nahi govikalpo gośvarūpaṃ nopadarśayatīti mama kadāpi siddham, tava cādyāpi | upādhya (9)ntaraṃcedanekāntaḥ | na hi yo yasya upādhyantaraṃ nopadarśayet nāsau tadapītiniyamaḥ' iti |
body.translated_text: The desire for a particular [form] such as form etc. without [that particular being provided] — that is the uncommonness. For the cow-conceptual [cognition] cited as an example does not desire the particular 'horse' etc. But in the rule of restriction, there is indeed a contradiction — for there is no such thing as the desire for a particular restriction [applied to] what is not an object of that [cognition], since there would be the unwanted consequence that cow-cognition would desire the restriction of horse-particulars. If [one argues:] because of the non-observation of the existence and non-existence of that [object] — then the fault is non-establishment (<s>asiddhi</s>). For it has never been established for me that cow-conceptual [cognition] does not show the essential nature of a cow — and for you, [this is] not [established] even today. If [one argues from] another adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>) — [then there is] inconclusiveness (<s>anekānta</s>). For there is no rule that 'whatever does not show an adventitious condition of something, that does not [show] that [thing] either.' — Thus [it has been stated].

body.text: punaścoktaṃ kathaṃ pūreta asya agotvavyavacchedaḥ, śabdaliṅgābhyāṃ (10) pratipādyate na viśeṣaḥ vastusvarūpayeveti pramāṇantarasya śabdāntarasya ca vṛtteḥ | tathāhi-
body.translated_text: And again it was said: 'How is the exclusion of non-cow-ness to be fulfilled for this [cognition]?' [The answer is:] it is conveyed through word and logical mark (<s>śabda-liṅga</s>); the particular [entity] is not [established] merely by the essential nature of the thing — because of the operation of another means of evidence and another word. For thus —

children.translated_text: Of a single entity whose nature is the object, and which exists as directly perceived (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) by itself —

children.text: ko 'nyo bhāvo na dṛṣṭaḥ syāt yaḥ pramāṇaiḥ parīkṣyate ||
children.translated_text: what other property could there be that is not seen, which would be examined by the means of evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>)?

body.text: sahi-pratyakṣaḥ prasiddho dharmiṇi sādhanāsambhavāt | yathā pratyayatvasādhye śabdastathā pratyakṣeṇaiva siddheḥ sarvākārasiddhe tadanyasya'(2) siddhasyābhāvāt, bhāve vā na tatsvabhāvatvaṃ nahi yat..........na bhavanti sa tatsvabhāvoyuktaḥ tanmātranibandhanatvāt bhedavyavahārasya | anyathā abhāvaprasaṃgādi (3) ityuktam, tasmātpratyakṣeṇa dharmiṇi tatsvabhāvāsākalyaparicchedāt atrānavakāśaḥ pramāṇantarabuddhiḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: For that [entity] is directly perceived and well-established — [hence] in the substrate (<s>dharmin</s>), there is no possibility of [further] proof. Just as verbal testimony [has no role] when perception is to be proved — because [the entity] is already established by perception alone. When everything is established [by perception], there is nothing else that is unestablished. Or, even if [some property] exists [but is not established by perception], that is not of the nature of that [entity] — for what [properties] do not exist [in it] cannot reasonably be its essential nature, because the convention of difference is based on that alone. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-existence etc. — as stated. Therefore, since perception ascertains the totality of the essential natures in the substrate, there is no room here for the cognition of another means of evidence.

body.text:
ḥno cedbhrāntinimittena saṃyojyetaḥ guṇāntaramḥ
'śuktau vā rajatākāro rūpasādharmyadarśanāt ||
body.translated_text: 'Unless it were conjoined with another property through a cause of error' — as in the case of the silver-form in a shell, from seeing similarity of form.

body.text: yadi dṛṣṭasarvatatvasyāpi bhrāmyaddhetoḥ niścayapratirodhinā bhrāntinimittena guṇāntarā na saṃyojyeta, yathā śuktau rajatākārau, na hi śuktau te rūpe samānaṃ viśiṣṭañca tathāpratipattiprasaṅgāt | apratipattau vā vivekena tvavikalpāyogān atiprasaṅgācca | tasmāt paśyan śuktirūpaṃ ca (6) viśiṣṭameva paśyati niścayapratyayavaikalyāt |
body.translated_text: If, even for one who has seen every aspect [of the object], that [property] were not conjoined with another property through a cause of error that obstructs certainty — as in the silver-form in a shell — for in the shell, those forms that are common and distinguished would not be so apprehended [if error were absent]; otherwise there would be the unwanted consequence of non-apprehension; and in non-apprehension, through discrimination, there would be the impossibility of conceptual cognition and the unwanted consequence of over-extension. Therefore, one who sees the shell-form sees it only as distinguished — because of the deficiency of the certainty-cognition.

body.text: aniścitaṃ tava sāmānyaṃ paśyāmīti manyate '
body.translated_text: '[One] thinks: I see your uncertain universal' —

body.text: tato 'sya rajatasamāropaḥ tathā sadṛśārtharopi notpatte(7)ralakṣitanānātvasya bhrāntisamāropāt sthitibhrānti yāvanto 'sya parabhāvā tāvanta eva yathāsvaṃ nimittabhāvinaḥ samāropāiti tadvayavacchedakāni (8) bhavanti pramāṇāni saphalāni, teṣāntu vyavacchedaphalānāṃ tu nā pratītavastvaṃśapratyāyane pravṛttistasya dṛṣṭatvāt | phalāṃ śasya caikadeśena darśanāyogāt |
body.translated_text: From that arises the superimposition of silver upon it. Likewise, even from a similar object, [the superimposition arises] not from production but from the superimposition of error upon that whose multiplicity is unnoticed. The duration of error — as many adventitious properties of this [entity], so many [superimpositions], each arising from its respective cause — are superimposed. The means of evidence that exclude those [superimpositions] are fruitful. But those that have the fruit of exclusion — [they have] no engagement in revealing the aspect of the real entity that has not been [previously] cognized, because that [aspect] has [already] been seen. And because it is not possible to see [only] a part of the fruit [separate from the whole].

children.translated_text: Therefore, of an entity that has been seen, every property has been seen;
because error is unstable — the proof proceeds accordingly.
In the apprehension of a real entity by inference too, when one property is ascertained,
the apprehension of all properties [follows] — in [the theory of] <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), this fault does not arise;
therefore, the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is proclaimed as having exclusion (<s>apoha</s>) as its domain.

children.text: anyathā dharmiṇaḥ siddhau kimataḥ sādhakaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, when the substrate (<s>dharmin</s>) is established [through perception], what further proof is there beyond that?
Even when something is seen somewhere, the cognition that conceptually constructs a universal meaning,
in the aspect where another [property] has not been superimposed, has as its domain the exclusion of that alone.
The object of a mind with determinate superimposition — from the relationship of the sublated and the sublating,
the engagement of this [mind] in discriminating the superimposition is understood.
As many aspects as the superimposition [has], so many are the determinate [cognitions] that negate it;

children.text: tāvanta eva śabdāśca tena te bhinnagocarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and so many are the words — therefore they have different domains.
Otherwise, by a single word, pervading a single real entity,
the cognition would not have another object — and there would be synonymy.
Thus, having shown one's own position, this has been spoken for the destruction of the delusion of others regarding the subject.
Even for one whose cognition grasps the effect-entity differentiated by multiple adventitious conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) —
in the apprehension of [an entity] whose nature is undifferentiated from [its] capacities, the assistance of the multiple conditions is the instrument.
What difference could there be of the effect-entity of all [such conditions] — [this is] not determined;
because of the relation of both [condition and entity] in [a single] nature, there is the apprehension of both in a single cognition.

body.text: atmabhūtasyopādhestadvatorūpakāryopakārakabhāvasya grahaṇāt | ekajñāne dvayorapi grahaṇamiti ekopādhiviśiṣṭepi [4] tasmin gṛhyamāṇe sarvopādhīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ tadgrahaṇanāntarīyakatvādupādhikṛdgrahaṇasya | anyathā tathā na gṛhyeta | na hyanyaevānyopakārako yo na gṛhī [6] taḥ syāt | na cāpyapakārake tathāgṛhīte tadupakāryāgrahaṇaṃ tasyāpyagrahaṇaprasaṅgāt | tasmādarthāntaropādhivāde 'pi samānaḥ prasaṅgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Because of the apprehension of the adventitious condition that is identical with the nature [of the entity] — its nature being that of an auxiliary cause of the form-effect — in a single cognition, there is the apprehension of both. Even when that [entity] qualified by a single adventitious condition is apprehended, there is the apprehension of all adventitious conditions — because the apprehension by adventitious conditions necessarily entails the apprehension of that [whole entity]. Otherwise it would not be so apprehended. For it is not the case that one thing is the auxiliary of another [thing] that is not apprehended. And when a non-auxiliary is so apprehended, the non-apprehension of its auxiliand [would follow] — because of the unwanted consequence of the non-apprehension of that [auxiliand] too. Therefore, even in the view of adventitious conditions as separate entities, the same contingency [applies].

children.translated_text: If, when there is a difference in the capacities to assist properties,
those [capacities] do not assist that [entity] — then there would be instability for them.
When one auxiliary [capacity] is apprehended, the other auxiliaries are not [separately apprehended] from that;
when that [one] is seen, those that are unseen — in the apprehension of that [one], there is the apprehension of all.

body.text: ityanena pāramārthikapāratantrya lakṣaṇopādhisambandhayonyasvabhāvāṅgīkāre sakalagahaḥ ekenāpi pramāṇena śabdena vā pravṛttena syāt | yadā tu
body.translated_text: Thus, by this [argument], when the ultimately real relation of adventitious conditions — whose nature is mutual dependence — is accepted, there can be the apprehension of all through even one means of evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>) or word that has been employed. But when —

children.text: bhāve bhāvini tadbhāvo bhāva eva ca bhāvitā |
children.translated_text: The existence of what exists in an existent, and the existent nature of existence itself,
the well-established relation of cause and result — from perception and non-apprehension —
conceptual constructions whose objects are [merely] cause and effect, having [only] this much as their true content,
display their objects as if fashioned [together] — [but they are] objects of false [construction].
In what is different, what conjunction [is there]? In what is non-different, what cause-effect relation?

children.text: bhāve hyayanyasya viśliṣṭau śliṣṭau syātāṃ kathaṃ na tau ||
children.translated_text: For when the entity [of one] exists, [if] the other [exists too], the disjoined would become conjoined — how could they not?
Conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and the like — all this has been considered by this [argument].
Because of the mutual non-assistance [of ultimately separate entities], and because a relatum of such a kind does not [exist].

body.text: iti kalpitopakāryāpakārakabhā [2]ve sambandhenāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ, kena hi kāryāṃpekṣya paścāt kāryakāraṇabhāvabhājaṃ bhāvamakalpamapi pratyakṣamīkṣate yenāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ syāt | ata evoktam apohenāyaṃ doṣaḥ prasaṅgataiti | sūryavadevā (sūryādervā) viśvopakārisvabhāve grahe viśvagrahaḥ [3] syāt | ata evāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, this <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) [arises] in [the context of] the conceptually constructed relationship of beneficiary and benefactor. For by what [means], having considered the effect, does one perceive through perception an entity that partakes of the cause-effect relation, [even one that is] not conceptually constructed — such that this <s>prasaṅga</s> would arise? For this very reason it was said: 'This fault arises through <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), [merely] as a contingent [consequence].' If the sun etc. had the essential nature of being universally beneficial, then the sun would be an 'all-grasper.' For this very reason he says —

body.text: 'yadi bhrāntinivṛnttyarthaṃ gṛhīte 'nyadiṣyate'
body.translated_text: 'If, for the purpose of removing error, when [something] has been grasped, another is indicated' —

body.text: syādetannirbhāgasya vastuno brahe ko 'nyastadā na gṛhīto nāma sa tu bhrāntyā nāvadhāryate iti pramāṇāntaraṃ yadyevaṃ-tadvyavacchedaviṣayaṃ siddhaṃ tadvattato 'param |
body.translated_text: this might [be valid] for a partless entity; in [its] apprehension, what other [entity] has not been apprehended? But that [other entity] is not ascertained due to error. If so, another means of valid cognition [is needed] — thus: 'What has the exclusion of that as its object is established as possessing that, [and] beyond that —'

children.translated_text: 'What has the exclusion of that as its object is established as possessing that, [and] beyond that —'
'even in the operation [of cognition] whose object is what has not been superimposed, through certitudes,

children.text: yanna niścīyate rūpaṃ tatteṣāṃ viṣayaḥ katham ||
children.translated_text: whatever form is not ascertained — how is that the object of those [certitudes]?'

body.text: yattarhi bhrāntinivṛttyarthaṃ pravṛttaṃ pramāṇāṃanyasya samāropavyavacchedaphalamiti siddhamanyāpohaviṣayaṃ tadvadanyadapi asa [5] māroparviṣaye vṛtteḥ yatrāsya samāropo na tatra niścaya iti samāropābhāve rktamāno 'nyāpohaviṣayaḥ siddhaḥ, pratyakṣantu pratiṣṭhitapratibhāsavaśāt gṛhṇīta pāratantryādi svabhāvabhraṣṭhaḥ [6] akaṣṭena apakarṣitaprakṛtāvadyasaṃdohamadehamevaṃ samarthayate |
body.translated_text: Since what operates for the purpose of removing error has as its result the exclusion of the superimposition of another — [it is] established as having the exclusion of the other (<s>anyāpoha</s>) as its object. Likewise, another [means of cognition] too, in [its] operation whose object is what has not been superimposed — where there is no superimposition of it, there is no certitude — hence, in the absence of superimposition, the means of valid cognition that is being examined is established as having the exclusion of the other as its object. But perception, by the force of the appearance established [within it], grasps — [perception,] fallen from its own essential nature of dependence etc., effortlessly, with the mass of fault inherent in its [original] nature drawn away, establishes [the matter] thus:

children.translated_text: Even though grasped by perception, [the object is] devoid of the particular [as a] portion;
whatever cognition there is in the ascertainment of the particular — that is [what is] cognized.

body.text: iti vikalpapratyayahetuścāyaṃ abhyāsa pā[7]ṭavā santi tāratamyādiḥ | yathā
body.translated_text: And this [is] the cause of the conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpapratyaya</s>) — the gradations of proficiency (<s>pāṭava</s>) through practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and so forth. Just as:

children.translated_text: With respect to the body of a single beautiful woman, for an ascetic, a lover, and a dog,
[there arise] three conceptual constructions: 'a corpse,' 'a beloved,' 'food.'

body.text: ityādi vartikakāradarśite prasaṅge yannipuṇamasṛṇamanīṣayā dharmmā [8] na na sarpavadapaviṣavisarpaṃ sphāraphūtkāraprāyaṃ pralapitamamunā lekhitumapi (likhitumapi) urjjāmahe | maheśvarapraṇatalabthavarṇavarṇitatvena na prahasanāya prastūyate |
body.translated_text: And so forth — in the <s>prasaṅga</s> shown by the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> [<s>Kumārila</s>], that which was prattled by him with sharp, smooth intellect — [speech] predominantly consisting of loud hissing, like the spreading of venom from a non-venomous serpent regarding <s>dharma</s> — we do not have the energy even to write [a refutation of] it. Because it is described with the coloring of words obtained through prostration to <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), it is not presented for the purpose of ridicule.

body.text: upādhyantaraṃ cedanekāntaḥ | na hi yo yasya [9] upādhyantaraṃ nopadarśayet nāsau tadapīti niyamaḥ | nanu niyama eva, tathāhi yanna yatsamevatadharmabodhanaṃ na tat tatsvarūpabodhanaṃ yathā govikalpaśabdauturage | tathā ca tau gavyapi nīlatvā[10]pekṣayeti vyāpakānupalabdhi dharmibodhe 'pi ki dharmāṇāṃ kasyacidbodhaḥ kasyacidabodhaścetyupakārabhedānniyamaḥ syāt | upakārabhedaśca śaktibhedāt bhavet | na caiva prakṛte anavasthāprasaṅgāt | tataḥ śakternabhedāt | upakārābhede sarvopādhisahitabodhi'bodhoveti dvayī gatiriti pratibandhasi ddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: If [one says] there is another limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), [then we have] an inconclusive reason (<s>anekānta</s>). For there is no rule that 'one who does not show another limiting condition of something does not [thereby establish] that either.' Objection: There is indeed such a rule. For thus: what is not co-present with something is not a means of knowing its essential nature — just as the conceptual construction of a cow and the word [for cow do not reveal the nature] of a horse. And likewise, those two [cow-word and cow-concept] too, with respect to cow, depend on [the exclusion of properties like] blue-ness etc. — [this is] non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). Even in the knowing of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), could there be a rule [arising] from the difference of benefit — that some properties are known while others are not known? And the difference of benefit would arise from the difference of capacity (<s>śakti</s>). But this is not so in the present case, because of the unwanted consequence of infinite regress. Therefore, because of the non-difference of capacity, [and] because of the non-difference of benefit — the two courses are: either cognition of all limiting conditions together, or non-cognition [of all] — this is the establishment of invariable concomitance (<s>pratibandha</s>).

body.text: duṣprayuktametat, upādhiṃ prakalpya mede pratiniyatasāmagrīvodhyatvasyāpi svabhāvavaicitryanibandhanatvāt, tasyāpi svakāraṇādhīnatvāt, tasyāpyanvayavyatirekasiddhatvāt tasyāpi kāryonneyatvāt iti |
body.translated_text: This is poorly applied, because even the fitness-for-cognition by a restricted aggregate of conditions [is] based on the diversity of essential nature — [and] because that [diversity] too depends on its own causes — [and] because that too is established through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) — [and] because that too is to be inferred from the effect.

body.text: yattu śakterabhedādityādi, tattadā śobheta yadi dharmimātrādhīnastadbodhamātrādhīno vā, tāvanmātrabodhasāmagrayadhīno vā yāvadupādhibhedabodhaḥ syāt, na caivam |
body.translated_text: As for what was said 'because of the non-difference of capacity' and so forth — that would be fitting only if the cognition of that [property] depended on the property-bearer alone, or on the cognition of that alone, or on the aggregate of conditions [sufficient] for the cognition of just that much as [is sufficient for] the cognition of the difference of limiting condition. But this is not so.

body.text: yayā [4] kayāpi sāmagryā jñānamutpadyatāṃ tat kiṃ pāramārthikasvarūpadvayaniṣṭhopakāryopakārakabhāvabhāgidravyaṃ dṛṣṭamiṣṭaṃ na vā, tena jñānenayadi dṛṣṭaṃ, sarvātmanā upādhibhiḥ sārdham | yadyaṃśenāpoha vi [5] ṣayatvasya svīkṛtamapāramārthikopādhyapakārayogyasvabhāvatvasya bhāvasyātadvyāvṛttiniṣṭhasya tena nirūpaṇāt nipuṇaṃ nirūpaya tāvat | grāhakajñānāpekṣayā prasaṅge datte ke [6] śe spṛṣṭa śiraśca nayasi sāmagryā vaicitryāditi tataḥ ki jñānameva sakalopādhi upakārayogyavastusvarūpamanyonyāpekṣaṃ na lakṣayasi | vastusvarūpameva cānyathākṛta (7) svabhāva eṣa jñānasya kṛtastena tatpadārthamekopādhiviśiṣṭaṃ niṣṭaṃkayati | paryantavikalpaviśvāse dantaniṣṭhoṣikāyāḥ kimetadanyat | anyavikalpālambane tu vyaktameva prakṛtadoiṣānatikra-(8)-maḥ kārakahetuprasaktiśceti yatpunarūpahāsya evaṃ upahasati |
body.translated_text: By whatever aggregate of conditions a cognition arises — does that [cognition] see, or is it desired [to see], a substance partaking of a beneficiary-benefactor relationship grounded in the ultimate essential nature of both [parties]? If it sees [it] through that cognition — [it sees it] in its entirety, together with [all] the limiting conditions. If it is accepted that [only] partially [the object has] the status of having <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) as its object — since the entity, whose essential nature is fitness for non-ultimate-limiting-condition-benefit, and which is grounded in <s>atadvyāvṛtti</s> (exclusion from what is not that), is examined by that [partial cognition] — examine [this] carefully. When the <s>prasaṅga</s> is given with reference to the apprehending cognition — [saying] 'you grasp the hair and lead away the head too' [i.e., 'you are grasping at straws'] — because of the diversity of the aggregate — what then [follows]? You do not observe that cognition itself is the essential nature of the real entity fit for the benefit of all limiting conditions and is mutually dependent. And the essential nature of the real entity itself, having been made otherwise in nature — this has been done by cognition — therefore it ascertains that object as qualified by a single limiting condition. If one trusts the final conceptual construction — what else is this than [biting] the lip with one's teeth? But in the case of [its] resting on another conceptual construction, there is clearly no transcending the faults in question, and there is the attachment of the fault of the efficient cause — and so, one who mocks thus is himself mocked.

body.text: etena bhedāddharmiṇaḥ pratītāvapi śabdaliṅgadvārā dharmāṇāṃ bhedapratītirindriya dvārāpi mā bhūta ityādikaṃ tu karṇasparśeṃ kaṭicālanamapāstam | tattadupādhyupalambhasāmagrīvirahakāle prasañjitasyeṣṭatvāt | vicitraśaktitvācca pramāṇānāṃ, liṅgasya prasiddhapratibandhapratisandhānaśaktikatvāt, śabdasya samayasīmavikramatvāt, indriyasya tu arthaśaktera pekṣaṇāt na tu sambaddho 'rtha ityevaṃ pramāṇaiḥ pramāpyate, atiprasaṅgāditi-tadapi samyak pūrvavicārānatikramāt, api ca tadasyaparihāreṇa pravartateti ca dhvaneḥ ucyate | tena te syāt vyavacchede kathaṃ ca sat śabdastathāyuktaṃ anyacca niṣparihāreṇa pravartate 'tiprasaṅge, tatrānyatra ca pravṛttyanujñāyāṃ tannāmagrahaṇavaiyarthyaṃ sat pravṛttinivṛtyanujñāyāñca ekacodanā, nā (2) nātva etadvacanameva syāt vyāvṛtyākhyāne tasmādavaśyaṃ śabdena vyavacchedaścodanīyaḥ | sa cābhinnastadanye vyaktijātidharmāpyasti tanniyatāsūpagamaṃ, niyatacodanaṃ jātyarthaprasādhanañca, paritya (3) jya avāntaraparikalpanaṃ anarthanirbandha eva yathākalpanamasyāyogāt | na vai vyavacchedo na kriyate, pravṛttiviṣayantu kathayanti jātirūpā, vyavacchedo 'sti bhedasya nanvetāvatprayojanaṃ śabdānāmiti | (4) kiṃ tadasāmānyo nāpareṇa vaḥ | na jātirarthakriyāyogyeti pravṛttiviṣayaḥ | taddvāreṇa codite na pravṛttirapi pratyuktā, tadvat codane ca vyavadhānaṃ jātivatoḥ pravṛttiviṣayatve vyāvṛtti taccānto (5) kinneṣyate vyāvṛtteravastutvenāsādhanatvāccet tattulyaṃ jāteḥ tadvatsādhanādadoṣa iti cet tulyaṃ tadvyāvṛttimataḥ avastugrāhī ca vyāvṛttivādināṃ śābdaḥ pratyayaḥ sacitramavajātajanma kārake 'pi kārakāvyavasāyī pravartayati, vastusaṃvādastu vastūtpattyā tatpratibandhesati bhavati, anyathā naivāsti vastutpatte rna bhrānteriti cet nātat pratisiddhastatastadavyavasāyāt | maṇipra [7] bhāyāṃ maṇiprabhāyāṃ maṇibhrāntidarśanena vyabhicārācca bhrānteravastusaṃvāda iti cet na yathoktenaiva vyabhicārāt | vitathapratibhāso hi bhrāntilakṣaṇaṃ tannāntarīkatayā saṃvādo na pratibhāsā-(8) pekṣī jātergrahaṇamevaṃ bhrāntigrahaṇe vā na tatra pravṛttiriti kiṃ tenānyavyāvṛtā ca kriyāyogyanīlādyarthākārapratyayaprādurbhāvāt, tadupanīte 'nyapravṛtti nivṛttī samañjasa janmāno vināpi ca sā (8) mānyena prakṛtibhinneṣvartheṣu bhede cedamiti pratyabhijñānaṃ yasmāt-
body.translated_text: By this, even when the property-bearer is cognized as different through the medium of word and logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>), [the objection] 'let there not be the cognition of the difference of properties through the medium of the sense organs' and the like — [this] is dismissed as a mere twitch of the waist at the touch of the ear. Because [the opponent's point] is accepted as contingently entailed at the time of the absence of the aggregate of conditions for the apprehension of each respective limiting condition. And because the means of valid cognition have diverse capacities: the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) has the capacity of reconnecting with an established invariable concomitance (<s>pratibandha</s>); the word has the scope of the boundary of convention; the sense organ, however, depends on the power of the object — [and] it is not the case that the connected object is cognized by the means of valid cognition in just this way — because of the unwanted consequence of over-extension. And that too [is refuted], properly, because of not transcending the prior investigation. Moreover, 'it operates for [the sake of its] remedy without escape' — this is what the implicit purport (<s>dhvani</s>) conveys. Therefore, for you, in [the case of] exclusion, how can the word, being [so] constituted, [operate]? And the other [word] operates without escape in the [case of] over-extension; in granting the operation [of the word] there and elsewhere, the specification of that [word's] name would be useless. And in granting operation and cessation, [there would be] a single injunction (<s>codanā</s>) — the diversity of this very statement would be [merely] in the description of exclusion. Therefore, exclusion must necessarily be enjoined by the word.
