And that [exclusion is] non-different [from the object]; in things other than that — particular (<s>vyakti</s>), universal (<s>jāti</s>), property — there is acceptance [that the word applies] to restricted [objects], restricted injunction, and the establishment of the universal meaning. Abandoning [all this and] engaging in sub-constructions is nothing but an insistence on what is pointless, because of the impossibility of this [approach] as [correctly] constructed. It is not the case that exclusion is not performed; but those in the form of universals speak of the object of positive engagement. 'There is exclusion of difference — is not this much the purpose of words?' — [we reply:] is that [exclusion] not common [to all words], [and] unmatched by yours? The universal is not the object of positive engagement as 'fit for causal efficacy' (<s>arthakriyāyogya</s>). And when [someone is] enjoined through that [universal] medium, positive engagement too is answered [for]; just as in the injunction, the interposition of the universal is [the basis of] the object of positive engagement through exclusion, and that [exclusion has] as its end [the positive engagement] — why is this not accepted? [To say:] 'because exclusion is a non-entity and hence cannot be a means of proof' — [we reply:] the same applies to the universal; just as from proving 'that which possesses that' — [there is] no fault. If [you say] 'the same [applies] to what possesses that exclusion' — [we reply:] the verbal cognition of the proponents of the exclusion theory grasps a non-entity. [This cognition,] whose birth is wonderful and variegated, even in [the case of] an agent, impels the determination of agency [despite agency itself being conceptually constructed]. But the conformity with reality occurs when there is the production of the real entity and the invariable concomitance of that [cognition] with [the entity] — otherwise, it simply does not exist, [neither] from the production of the real entity nor from error. If [one says:] 'that is not refuted, because of the non-determination of that from that' — [this refers to] the error in the cognition of a gem in the luster of a gem — [you say] because of the deviation of error from the conformity with reality. [We reply:] no, because of the deviation in exactly the way stated. For a false appearance is the defining mark of error; conformity [with reality], by the non-exclusion of that [false appearance], is not dependent on the [mere] appearance [of the universal]. That the grasping of the universal is error, or even in the grasping of error, there is no positive engagement therein — what then [is the use] of that? Because the cognition-appearance of the meaning — blue etc. — as [having] the aspect of objects that are excluded from the other and fit for causal efficacy arises, [and] in what is presented by that [cognition], the positive engagement and cessation toward another are of proper birth. And even without a universal, in objects that are different by nature,

children.text: jñānādyarthakriyāṃ tāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhede 'pi kurvataḥ |
children.translated_text: having seen that [entity] performing this and that causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) through cognition and the like, even in [the case of] difference,
objects, together with sounds that have as their domain the separation from what is other than that,

body.text: saṃyojyapratyabhijñānaṃ kuryādapya[10]sya darśane ||
body.translated_text: combining [them], would produce recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) even upon seeing this [entity again].

body.text: bhede 'pi prakṛtyaiva cakṣurādivat jñānādikā arthakriyā tathānyeṣu padārtheṣu tāmeva arthakriyāmatadrūpaparāvṛtteṣu paśyato 'nyāvṛttaviṣayatvavisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ tadevedamiti svānubhavavāsanāprabodhane saṃsṛṣṭabhedaṃ mithyājñānamā(ma) jāyate, anyathā bhedasaṃsargavatī buddhiḥ syāt daṇḍivat | na hyekadaṇḍadarśanenānyatra sa evāyami (2) ti bhavati, kiṃ tarhi, tadiheti | na caivaṃ pratyabhijñānaṃ kiṃ tadevedamiti, tanna tadekamanekatra paśyatopi bhedasaṃsargavat muktam | vibhramavaśāttu tathā jñānena virodhaḥ nimittābhāvādvibhramo na mukta iti cet (3) ta eva bhāvāstadekārthakāriṇo 'nubhavadvāreṇa prakṛtyā vibhramakalāyā vikalpavāsanāyā hetutvānnimittaṃ | marīcikādiṣvapi hi jalādibhrāntestāvevābhinnāhāraparāmarśapratyayanimittānubhava (4) jananau bhāvau kāraṇaṃ bhinnāvapi na hi tatrānyadeva kiñcitsāmānyamasti yattathā pratīyate | sattve vā sadarthagrāhiṇī buddhirbhrāntirna syāt, abhūtākārasamāropādbhrāntitve sa evākāro 'syā viṣayaḥ, (5) aviṣayasyānāropāt | sa cāroposāmānyamekakāryakārigrahaṇa iti nirarthikotpattiḥ yathāvasthitasvabhāvagrahāsāmarthyaṃ vikalpānāṃ svakāraṇapravṛtteḥ svakāra (6)ṇañca avidyāvāsanāpi keśavibhramasyeva timiraṃ tena |
body.translated_text: Even when there is difference, just as the eye and other [sense faculties] naturally [produce cognition], so too <s>jñāna</s> (cognition) and other [mental faculties] perform <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy). When one sees that very same <s>arthakriyā</s> in other objects — in those that are excluded from having that nature — due to having objects characterized by exclusion from others, there arises an erroneous cognition (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) that conflates difference, in the form 'this is that very same thing,' through the awakening of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) from one's own experience. Otherwise, the cognition would possess a connection with difference, like [the cognition of] a man with a stick. For by seeing one stick, one does not cognize elsewhere 'this is that very same one,' but rather 'that is here.' And recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) is not like this — what is 'this is that very thing'? Therefore, even for one who sees one [thing] in many, it is not freed from connection with difference. If [you say] there is no error (<s>vibhrama</s>) because there is contradiction with such cognition due to the absence of a cause — [we reply:] those very entities, being producers of that one <s>arthakriyā</s>, are the cause through the medium of experience, by being the natural cause of the faculty of error, namely the <s>vāsanā</s> of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction). For even in the case of mirages and the like, the two entities — the experience and the cognition that is the cause of apprehending an undifferentiated appearance — are the cause of the delusion of water and so forth, even though they are different; for there is no other <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) whatsoever that is perceived as such. Or, if [a universal] existed, the cognition, grasping a real object, would not be erroneous; if it is erroneous due to the superimposition of an unreal aspect, then that very aspect is its object, since what is not an object is not superimposed. And that superimposition — [namely] the <s>sāmānya</s>, the grasping of producers of one effect — is a purposeless arising, [indicating] the incapacity of <s>vikalpas</s> to grasp the nature of things as they actually are, since they arise from their own causes; and their own cause is also <s>avidyā</s>-<s>vāsanā</s> (the latent impression of ignorance), like <s>timira</s> (eye-disease) in the case of the hair-illusion.

body.text: astīyamapi yā tvantarupaplavasamudbhavā ||
body.translated_text: There exists also this [erroneous cognition] which arises from an internal disturbance;

children.translated_text: Born from a defect, it naturally manifests in a misleading manner,
Without depending on similarity of properties, like <s>timira</s> (eye-disease) in the case of the eye and other [sense faculties].

body.text: parasyāpi na sā buddhiḥ sāmānyādeva kevalāt |

children.translated_text: Because, if only that [universal] were cognized, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-cognition of <s>vyaktis</s> (particulars).
If <s>vyaktis</s> (particulars), assisted by one object, are the cause of cognition,

children.text: tadekaṃ vastu kiṃ tāsāṃ nānātvaṃ[4] samapohati |
children.translated_text: What does that one object do to remove their multiplicity?
Because of [their] multiplicity, their being the cause of a single cognition is not perceived.

body.translated_text: Even for the opponent, that cognition does not [arise] from <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) alone;

children.translated_text: Now, if [you say that] due to incompleteness there is opposition to production, and production [occurs only] when accompanied by that [universal] —
Even though many, inasmuch as they produce a cognition of non-difference in dependence on one [universal],
With respect to the cognition that is produced by each one individually even without those [other particulars],

body.text: tenaikenāpi sāmarthya tāsāṃ netyagraho dhiyā |
body.translated_text: The capacity of those [particulars] is negated by cognition even through that one [universal] alone.

body.text: atha yathā nīlādiṣu ekāpāye 'pi cakṣurvijñānaṃ bhavatīti na samūhe 'pi teṣāmasāmarthyam | tathehāpi pratye (10) kāṣāye bhavatīti na sarvvadāsāmarthyam | na,
body.translated_text: Now, just as in the case of blue and other [colors], even when one [color] is removed, visual cognition still arises, so there is no incapacity in the aggregate either. Likewise here too, since [cognition] arises when each individual [particular] is removed, there is not always incapacity. [We reply:] No —

children.translated_text: Because in the case of visual cognition of blue and the like, the capacity of each one separately is observed,
The establishment of capacity in the aggregate [follows]; but for <s>vyakti</s> (the particular), this is in no way [the case].

body.text: na hi vyaktayaḥ sāmānyarahitā anvayijñānajanane dṛṣṭaśaktayaḥ tato na tāstatra samarthā iti na tena gṛhyeran |
body.translated_text: For <s>vyaktis</s> (particulars) devoid of <s>sāmānya</s> (universals) have never been observed to have the capacity to produce cognition of a persisting [entity]; therefore they are not capable in that regard, and hence would not be grasped by that [cognition].

body.text: tāsāmanyatamāpaikṣyaṃ taccecchaktaṃ na kevalam ||
body.translated_text: The dependence of those [particulars] on any one [of them] — if that [one] is capable, it is not [so] alone;

body.text: tadekamukuryustāḥ kathamekāṃ dhiyañca na |
body.translated_text: If those [other particulars] would make that one [universal superfluous], how would they not [also produce] a single cognition?

body.text: pūrvakasahakārivicārātsāmānyamupakāryamāsāṃ prāptaṃ sāmānyāntaramivāpekṣiṇāṃ ka āsāṃ pratibandhodhiyamādhātumekānto hi tena vinotpannā mithyā svaviṣayādṛte | iti mithyā (2) tvamāśaṅkya mānasavivādā uktameva bauddhadhiyām | tathā
body.translated_text: From the analysis of the previously [mentioned] cooperative condition, <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) as what is to be assisted by these [particulars] is arrived at — as if requiring yet another <s>sāmānya</s>. What prevents these [particulars] from producing the cognition? For [cognition] produced without that [universal] is certainly erroneous, being devoid of its own object. Thus, suspecting erroneousness, the disputes about mental cognition have already been stated regarding Buddhist cognitions. Likewise —

children.translated_text: Of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), which does not have a single nature, there is no complete apprehension through the senses;
The form that is self-cognized and inexpressible is the domain of the senses.
Of that which is excluded from everything, the exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) from each and every [other thing],
That differentiation, elevated through the distinctions of that [<s>dharmin</s>], constitutes the manifold nature of the <s>dharmin</s>.
Those conceptually constructed distinctions of form are not the domain of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual) cognition;
The variegated, having brilliant appearances, is not the domain of the occasional [cognition].

body.text: yadyapyasti sitatvādi yādṛgindrayagocaraḥ | [5]
body.translated_text: Even though whiteness and so forth exist as they are within the domain of the senses,

children.translated_text: That [form] is not denoted by words, due to the difference in form between the two cognitions.
If, even when the two cognitions have the same object, [they differ] due to having different bases —
The ear and other [senses], and the mind, have different objects — whence then [is the sameness of object]?
The mutual basis of cognitions with respect to that object has indeed arisen. [But] —
How can a single [object] have a form that manifests with different aspects?

body.text: cakṣuliṅgañca śabdañcāśritya yadi citrācitrābhāsatvaṃvikalpanirvikalpakacetasorbhavati | tarhi tayorekaviṃṣayatvaṃ kathamastu paramārthataḥ athaikaṃ paramārthaviṣayamaparaṃ timirakāmalābalādiva śukle pītādyābhāsadhāyino 'vidyādyaparapratyayāditaḥ sarvato vinivṛtte 'kha'ḍātmani (8) vivakṣitārthakriyāhetopratiniyatānyavyāvṛttadharmmadharmibhāvalabdhakhaṇḍatvānarthakriyāsamarthapratibhāsavikalpakāriṇaḥ samutpannamaparamārthaviṣayakāraṇaṃ kāraṇabhedāt prati (9) bhāsabhedācca samarthyatāmityuktau kledaṃ sambadhyate |
body.translated_text: If the variegated and non-variegated appearance of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual) and <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual) cognition arises in dependence on the eye, inferential mark, and word [respectively], then how can they have the same object in the ultimate sense? If one has an ultimately real object while the other, like the power of <s>timira</s> (eye-disease) or jaundice [projecting] yellow and other appearances onto white, arises from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and other extraneous conditions — [then we say:] with respect to that which is entirely excluded [from others], having an undivided nature, being the cause of the intended <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), having obtained its fragmentary nature through the <s>dharma</s>-<s>dharmin</s> relation established by exclusion from definitively determined others — [one cognition] produces <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) whose appearances are incapable of <s>arthakriyā</s>, and is a cause that does not have an ultimately real object. Due to the difference in causes and the difference in appearances, [the objection] is answered; this is connected here.

body.text: citrācitrapratibhāsābhyāṃ mitho viruddhābhyāmekanīlaviṣayābhyāmanaikāntāt | na rhi citrādhyakṣe yannīlaṃ cakāsti tadeva vā puruṣāntarasya yenākāreṇaikaviṣayatvaṃ tayo rna tenaiva virodho, yena ca virodho na tenaikaviṣayatvam, dharmāntarākāreṇa virodho nīlamātrākāreṇa cai kaviṣayateti cet-nanvihāpi dharmāntarākāreṇa virodho gotvavatpiṇḍamātrākāreṇa ekaviṣayateti tāvanmātranirākaraṇe 'siddho hetuḥ | pūrvatra siddhasādhanam | na hi śābdalaiṅgikavikalpakāle deśa (2) kālaniyamādayo 'pi sarva eva dharmaviśeṣā viṣayabhāvamāsādayantītyabhyupagacchāmaḥḥ nirvāhabhraṃśarūpe na hyavyaktamuktavato pi prameyānusaraṇenānistaraṇameva bhavataḥ dharmmidharmatayā citrateha vivakṣitā sā kathamanekāntā | citrābhyāṃ nīlābhyāṃ tayaurnirvikalpakaṃ cet gaurarthakriyāsamarthapratiṣṭhitaṃ nīlapratibhāsayoḥ vikalpakā niyatapratibhāsavikalpena saha kathaṃ savyetaranayanadṛṣṭavadekaviṣayatvaṃ sphuṭāsphuṭāsphuṭamapi sannihitāsannihitatayā nīlasya grahaṇaṃ tatrāsannihitatayā deśakālābhyāṃ vikalpakamavaiti deśādisannihitatayā nirvikalpakam |
body.translated_text: By the two [cognitions] — the one with variegated and the one with non-variegated appearance — which are mutually contradictory, having one [and the same] blue as their object, there is no invariable [connection]. For in variegated perception, whatever blue appears is not necessarily that very same [blue] for another person; and that aspect by which there would be sameness of object between the two is not the [aspect] by which there is contradiction, and that by which there is contradiction is not [the aspect] by which there is sameness of object. [If you say:] there is contradiction with respect to the aspect of other <s>dharmas</s> (properties), while there is sameness of object with respect to the mere blue aspect — [we reply:] but here too, there is contradiction with respect to the aspect of other <s>dharmas</s>, while there is sameness of object with respect to the mere lump-aspect, as with cow-ness. In the mere refutation of that much, the reason is unestablished; in the former [case] it proves what is already established. For we do not accept that at the time of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) based on word or inferential mark, all property-particulars whatsoever — including restrictions of place and time — attain the status of being objects. Since there is no escape [from the difficulty] even for one who speaks of the indistinct, by following the object of valid cognition, the variegation that is intended here as the <s>dharmin</s>-<s>dharma</s> relation — how is it non-invariable? If <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual cognition) [apprehends] by two variegated blue [appearances] — a cow established as capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> — how can there be sameness of object between the two blue appearances of <s>vikalpa</s> and the <s>vikalpa</s> with a determinate appearance, as with [objects] seen by the left and right eyes? Even the clear and unclear [appearances] are, due to proximity and non-proximity of the blue [object], its apprehension. Therein, <s>vikalpa</s> cognizes [it] as non-proximate in place and time, while <s>nirvikalpaka</s> [cognizes it] as proximate in place and so forth.

children.translated_text: Due to the distinction of far, near, and so forth, clarity and obscurity [of perception] is not tenable;
If [you say it is] due to differences in illumination — then in the case of covering and uncovering,
The vision is the same, whether unimpaired or [impaired]; and for one whose [vision] is unimpaired, something subtle [may exist].

children.text: ālokena ca mandena dṛśyate 'to bhidā yadiṃ ||
children.translated_text: And if difference [in perception] is due to dim illumination,

body.text:
ekatve 'rthasya vāhyasya dśyādṛśyabhidā kutaḥ |
anekatve 'ṇuśobhinne dṛśyādṛśyabhidā kutaḥ |

children.translated_text: If the appearance and the cognitive difference are due to the distinction of dullness and acuity [of the senses],
When something else that is different [appears], how can that which is undifferentiated appear as differentiated?

children.text: mandaṃ tadapi tejaḥ kimāvuteriha sā na kim |
children.translated_text: Is that light also dim? Is not that [capacity of illumination] present here too?
This thinness of light also exists, and in other [cases] there is also non-thinness.

body.translated_text: If the external object is one, whence the distinction of visible and invisible? If it is manifold, with atoms not shining [individually], whence the distinction of visible and invisible?

children.translated_text: And when very near, [the object] is very clear; would that light then be exceedingly vivid?
If, relying on something unseen, there would be a different form even there —

body.text:
anyo 'nyāvaraṇātteṣāṃ syāttejo vihatistataḥ
tatrekameka dṛśyeta tasyānāvaraṇe sakṛt ||
body.translated_text: Due to the mutual obstruction of those [lights], there would be an obstruction of light; then each single one would be seen [only] singly. In the absence of obstruction of that [light], at once —

children.translated_text: One would see a form both clear and unclear; with obstruction by the unseen,

children.text: arthānarthau na yena stastaddṛṣṭaṃ karoti kim ||
children.translated_text: That which does not [serve] purpose or non-purpose — what does it do that is seen?

body.text: adṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vā kāraṇaṃ kalpyatāmekatve bāhyasya sphuṭāsphuṭaghaṭanāpāṭavāpalāpāt | pratyayasya pratiniyatākāritaiva prāptakālā | anyathā jaya (10) parājayādivyavasthāvādināṃ viparyasyet | adṛṣṭavaśājjayaḥ parājayatayā pariṇataḥ parājayo pi jayatayeti śakyamabhidhātum |
body.translated_text: [Whether] the unseen or the seen is postulated as the cause — if the external [object] is one, the arrangement of clear and unclear is rejected by the denial of [perceptual] acuity. The very nature of the cognition as having a determinate form has arrived at its [proper] time. Otherwise, for those who maintain the convention of victory and defeat [in debate], it would be reversed — it could be said that victory, through the force of the unseen, has transformed into defeat, and defeat also into victory.

children.translated_text: Therefore, cognition (<s>saṃvit</s>), arising in accordance with its causes, dependent on the object,
Possesses differentiation of appearances; the rest are the evil doctrines of the foolish.

body.text: yathā 'nanu dharmiṇyeva sphuṭāsphuṭapratibhāsabhedaḥ na kathañcit | yathā yathā hi dharmāḥ pratibhānti tathā tathā sphuṭārthapratibhāna vyavahāraḥ ityādi, dharmmadharmmitayā hi pratibhāsanaṃ deśakālābhyāṃ asaṃnihitatayā kalpanamasphuṭapratibhānamāropitārthatvādityasakṛduktaṃ paramārthatastadviṣayatā neṣyate | sāmvṛtī tu jaga (3)dgītāstyevātaḥ parāmarśāvatāraḥ, tattvadarśinaḥ samvādopi sthūlaparāmarśinā tadrūpaparāvṛttanīlaviṣayaḥ, avāntaraparāmarśena sajātīyaparāvṛttānekanīlagocaraḥ sadvastutvādayo (4) kriyāmātranibandhanā vyapadeśāstasyaiva nīlasya śliṣṭāḥ svabhāvantaratā spṛśaḥ tadvāreṇāpyabādhanaṃ gṛhītasambandhānusandhānadvāreṇa śabdaliṅgaṃ lakṣitā pratītirūtprekṣākā-(5)-ratayā parokṣaviṣayā antasambandhena vā purovartinivṛttervyaparokṣaviṣayā na tayo rapi tatvata eka viṣayatā sāṃvṛtabodhasvīkrāre kva pratītirbādhānupalambhakukṣau (6) kṣiptatvādupādhicakrasya na śakyaṃ śakrasyāpi taddvāreṇa saṃdigdhānaikāntikatvaṃ kīrtayitum |
body.translated_text: As [was stated]: 'Objection — the distinction of clear and unclear manifestation is in the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) alone, [and there is] no [such distinction] in any way. For according as the properties manifest, so [there is] the conventional usage of clear-object-manifestation' — and so forth. For manifestation as property and property-bearer — because of [the object's] not being proximate in space and time — conceptual construction is unclear manifestation, because its object is superimposed. This has been stated repeatedly. In ultimate reality, the object-hood of that is not accepted. But conventionally, it is universally acknowledged — therefore [there is room for] the entry of reflective awareness (<s>parāmarśa</s>). The agreement of one who sees the truth, even with one who engages in coarse reflection, has the blue excluded from what is of another form as its object. The intermediate reflective awareness has many blues — excluded from what is of the same class — as its domain. [Properties like] being a real entity, etc. — designations whose basis is mere activity — are attached to that very blue. The touch of its being of another essential nature — through that door too, [there is] non-sublation, through the investigation of the previously grasped relation. The verbal sign (<s>śabdaliṅga</s>), [being] observed perception through the door of inference — has a remote object, with an imaginative character; or, through the internal relation, it has [what is] presently ceased as its proximate object. Not even for these two is there identity of object in ultimate reality. When the conventional cognition is accepted — where is the sublation? Because the group of limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) has been cast into the belly of non-apprehension of sublation, even <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) himself cannot proclaim, through that door, that [the reason is] doubtful and inconclusive.

children.translated_text: Cognition, through the difference of the sense-faculty, bearing [distinctions of]
sharp, dull, turbid, etc., as the differentiation of manifestation in the [single] object, is seen as one.
Because the object is of undifferentiated form, the mind would be of a single form;
if all is for that object, and [the difference arises] from the object — then there is no such [diverse] appearance of that [object].
For [cognition] that arises depending on the object, [and yet] does not produce its [exact] form,
in some aspect, even from the other [i.e., the sense-faculty], there may be differentiation.

children.text: tadā hyāśritya pitaraṃ tadrūpo 'pi sutaḥ pituḥ |
children.translated_text: For then, just as a son, depending on the father, even though of the father's form,
takes on some difference from the father in some aspect, from some [other source].
Those of weak vision see the disc of a lamp etc.
in the shape of a peacock's tail, with blue, red, and brilliant [colors].
If that [appearance] is the external form of that [lamp] — what inability [would there be] for one with clear eyes?
And how can one who sees the real be one whose sense-faculties are impaired — [for] he does see that?
His eye, purified of the cataract, clearly [perceives] what is beyond the senses;
how then, for one who sees [an object] seen by another sense-faculty, is that [object] unclear?
Through illumination, the sense-faculty, and attention — the capacity of another single [entity] is reached;
therefore [that factor] is not another cause — and how can the object [itself] be a non-cause?

body.text: ityanyasyopādhigrahasya tadvato cānanvayavyatirekādhyāsāt, tatkathaṃ taddvāreṇāpi pratibhāsabhedo bhāvīti dharmādupādhīnāmativi jñānasadbhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Thus, because of the superimposition of the non-occurrence of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) of [both] the apprehension of the limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) by another [factor] and [the apprehension] of one possessing that [limiting condition] — how then could there be a difference of manifestation even through that door? Because the limiting conditions are distinct from the properties, [and because of] the actual existence of cognition [regarding them].

children.translated_text: Objects, being properties of real entities alone, are the cause of such cognition;
even in difference, where that cognition [arises], it apprehends those [objects] accordingly.
Cognitions too, even in difference, [engage in] the reflective awareness of non-difference;
therefore the positive concomitance of that non-essential separation does not [pertain] to a single entity.

children.text: vastūnāṃ vidyate tasmāt tanniṣṭhā vastuni śrutiḥ |
children.translated_text: It pertains to entities — therefore, the linguistic usage (<s>śruti</s>) resting on that pertains to the entity.
Even when the state rests on the delimitation of external capacity, that linguistic usage
is bound to the reflections in conceptual construction that rest on that.
Therefore, because of resting on the exclusion of the other (<s>anyāpoha</s>), it has been said that linguistic usage is produced by <s>anyāpoha</s>.

body.text: 'bāhyaśakti' ityādi ślokapūrvvabhāgaḥ pramāṇasya bādhakasya sūtra [3] kaḥ, 'vikalpa pratibimbeṣvityādi prakāśya dṛśyavikalpāvartho ekīkṛtya vyavahārapravṛtterityevamarthaḥ saṃketādikāraṇasya |
body.translated_text: 'External capacity' etc. — the first part of this verse is the summary of the defeating <s>pramāṇa</s>. 'In the reflections of conceptual construction' etc. — the meaning is thus: [this is] the meaning of the cause, [namely] convention etc., because the perceived and the conceptually constructed objects are unified and conventional activity proceeds [accordingly].

children.translated_text: That which appears in cognition as a reflection of the object, as if separate,
that too, [coming] from the word, is not of the nature of the [real] object — it is an error arising from latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>).
Through linguistic expressions (<s>śruti</s>) in its designation, a portion of the object is comprehended;
and when that [portion] arrives, the activity of convention becomes purposeless for one who desires that [object].

body.text:
śabdo 'rthāśa kamāheti tatrānyāpoha ucyāta |
ākāraḥ sa ca nārthe 'sti taṃ vadannarthabhāka katham |

children.translated_text: The effect of the word, which is connected [with the object], is [produced] by the object with which it is connected;
and that which is not connected — because of the non-difference of the cognition — is constructed from the habit of perception.
Through the superimposition of that form — again, from the cognition of [the object] being otherwise turned away —

children.text: śabdārtho 'rthaḥ sa eveti vacana na virudhyate ||
children.translated_text: the word-meaning is that very object — this statement is not contradictory.

body.translated_text:
The word conveys a portion of the object — therefore, <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) is to be stated.
And that form does not exist in the [real] object — how then can one who speaks of it be speaking of the [real] object?

body.text: iti bādhakapratyayavaśāt atadrūpavyāvṛttavirodhe 'pi śabdasyārtho 'poha kathyate | sa ca vidhi pratītyanantaraṃ vidhiguṇatvena pratibhāti | anbayavyatirekābhyāṃ lokavyavahāra pravṛtteḥ | yathā ca tatparicchinatti ityādi [2]
body.translated_text: Thus, through the force of the defeating cognition, even when there is a contradiction in the exclusion from what is not of that form, the meaning of the word is said to be <s>apoha</s> (exclusion). And that [apoha] manifests as a subordinate property of positive determination, immediately after the cognition of positive determination. Because conventional worldly activity proceeds through positive and negative concomitance. And as it delimits that — and so forth:

children.translated_text: Sometimes, for the purpose of establishing [the mind] in the object, having turned [it] away from something,
the word is employed for the intellect — because of the ascertainment of the meaning of that [word].
Otherwise, the employment would be purposeless — even in words like 'that which is to be known' etc.
In [words] that have been brought into conventional usage, there is some delimitation;

children.text: nivaśanaṃ ca yo yasmāt bhidyate vinivartyatam |
children.translated_text: and [regarding] one who is to be turned away because he differs from that from which [he should be turned away] —
in the difference of that, [among those] being differentiated, [the cognition] manifesting as having the same form —
that [same form] is cognized through the exclusion of the other — of that entity,

children.text: kaścit bhāga iti prokto rūpaṃ nāsyāpi kiñcana |
children.translated_text: it is called 'a certain portion' — but its form too is nothing at all.
Only upon its [the word's] occurrence, from words, the exclusion of the other is cognized;
no distinguished [entity] is cognized there by anything else;
nor does the word produce a duality — the other is [merely] the absence of the other.

body.text: arūporūpavattvena darśanaṃ buddhiviplavaḥ |
body.translated_text: Seeing the formless as possessing form — [this] is the derangement of the intellect.

body.text: iti vyaktamuktamapoho vyāvṛttimātramuttarakālaṃ śabdārthaḥ pratīyate | pratīyata itisādhvevoktaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus it has been clearly stated: <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) — mere exclusion — is the word-meaning cognized at a subsequent time. 'It is cognized' — this has been well said

body.text: mitrapādaiḥ

children.translated_text: 'By words, the object is primarily designated;
therein, <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is to be understood as a subordinate property of that [designation].
And the object is one from superimposition, but another from [its actual] manifestation;
the expressible is to be established — but in reality, there is none whatsoever.'

body.translated_text: by <s>Mitrapāda</s> [<s>Jñānaśrīmitra</s>]:

body.text:
etāvatyarthe vivakṣite svavodhavaidhuryaṃ bodhayannāha-
varṇakṛtyakṣarākāra śūnyaṃgotvaṃ hivarṇyate ||
body.translated_text:
When this much meaning is intended, [the author], making known the bewilderment of his own understanding, says:
'Cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>) is described as devoid of color, shape, syllable, and form.'

body.text: iti etāvatyarthe vivakṣite svabodhavaidhuryaṃ bodhayannāha- 'yadapyatyantavilakṣaṇānāmityādi, tadapi sandigdhānaikāntikamm vidhināpi tathābhūtena sālakṣaṇyavyavahārasya nirvāhāt tathāhi ayaṃ vyavahāro na nirnimittaḥ, nāpyaneka nimittaḥ nāpyanekāsaṃsargyekanimittaḥ atiprasaṅgāt | tatau'neka saṃsaryekanimittaḥ pariśiṣyate ityādi, tadapi
body.translated_text: When this much meaning is intended, [the author], making known the bewilderment of his own understanding, says: 'As for what [is stated] regarding those that are completely dissimilar' — and so forth — that too is doubtful and inconclusive, because even through positive determination of that kind, the conventional usage of similarity is maintained. For thus, this conventional usage is not without a cause, nor with many causes, nor with a single cause that has no connection with many [entities] — because of over-extension. Therefore, a single cause that is connected with many [entities] remains as the residue — and so forth. That too:

body.text: varṇākṛtkṣarākāra śūnyaṃ gotvaṃ hivarṇyate |
body.translated_text: 'Cow-ness is described as devoid of color, shape, syllable, and form.'

body.text: varṇākṛtyakṣarākāraśūnya (3) sāmānyam, (2) bahulābhisandhau dhautādhautamūlakasamānasatyatāvṛttāntapāmarasyāpi na lakṣyate ko hi viśeṣo 'bhāvo 'pohaḥ samastavarṇākṛtyakṣarākāraśūnyaṃ vā sāmānyaṃ atadrūpaparāvṛtta nī (4) lākāravikalpena pratītiviśeṣo 'dhyavasāyaśabdārthaḥ vācyaḥ, pravṛtteraśeṣāyā aṅgamityuktau, ko 'yamadhyavasāyaḥ kimalīkasya vastutayāvabhāsaḥ kiṃ cāvasthātmakatayā tato bhe(5)dāgraho vā vastuvāsanāsamutthatvaṃ vetyādyanabhimatamukhyo 'pya prastutabandhabandhutāpratānaḥ, arthasārūpyamasya pramāṇaṃ tadvaśādarthapratītasiddheḥ dṛśyavikalpyāva-(6) rthāvekīkṛtya vyavahārapravṛtteḥ pramāṇaphalavyavasthātrāpi pratyakṣavadityādivacanāt nīlākārādviśiṣṭatadviśeṣagrahaḥ | atadrūpaparāvṛttanīlākārā tanmātragrahaṇamiti vyavasthā (7) yāṃ ḥnāpiviṣayasārūpyaṃ, (tadabhāvān) kā hi paramārthasadalīkarūpayoḥ samāna rūpatā nāme tyādi guḍagorasayorekatākaraṇaṃ kvopayuktam | bādhakapratyayāddhi tadalīkatvaṃ kiṃ prāgā (8) ropya cintā kriyate śeṣaśca doṣo 'bhimānasyaiva cintyatvādityādirajatapratītiparāmarśādgataḥ | yadi rajataṃ kiṃ vācyam | tasmādbhāvābhāvasādhāraṇapratibhāsa(9)..........sādhakena vidheḥ pratyayāntareṇāstīti vā sthāpyo nāstīti bādhakena āśaṅkitasyāropitasya vā pratibaṃdho deśādipratiṣedhe prītiprasiddhameva |
body.translated_text: A universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) devoid of color, shape, syllable, and form — even in the intention of many [thinkers], even for a simpleton [who follows] the example of the washed and unwashed radish and the equal truthfulness [of both], it is not perceived. For what distinction is there? Is the absence the exclusion, or is the universal devoid of all color, shape, syllable, and form? The specific cognition — through a conceptual construction of blue-form that is excluded from what is not of that form — is to be called the determination, the word-meaning, the expressible, [which is the] component of all activity. When thus stated, what is this determination? Is it the appearance of the illusory as a real entity? Or, because of having the nature of a state, [is it] the non-apprehension of difference from that? Or is it the arising from the latent impression of the [real] entity? — and so forth. Even the primary [meaning], which is not intended [by the Buddhist], is an extension of the kinship of the unintended bond. The resemblance to the object is its <s>pramāṇa</s>; through the force of that, the cognition of the object is established. Because the perceived and the conceptually constructed objects are unified and conventional activity proceeds [accordingly] — because even here, as with perception, [there is] the establishment of the <s>pramāṇa</s>-result distinction — from such statements, the apprehension of the particular distinguished from the blue-form [is achieved]. The form of the blue that is excluded from what is not of that form — the apprehension of mere that [blue] — this is the [proper] determination. [Objection:] 'There is also no resemblance to the object' — (because of its absence) for what indeed is the identity of form between the ultimately real and an illusory form? — and so forth. What use is this conflation of treacle and cow-dung? For the illusoriness of that [conceptual form] is [established] through the defeating cognition — why engage in deliberation after first superimposing [something]? The remaining faults too are to be considered as pertaining to [the opponent's] own conceit alone — thus [this] follows from the reflective awareness regarding the cognition of silver [as in the rope-silver illusion]. If [it is] silver, what is to be said? Therefore, by another cognition that establishes through the manifestation common to existence and non-existence — positive determination is to be established as 'it exists,' or the restriction of what is suspected or superimposed is [to be established] by a defeating [cognition as] 'it does not exist' — the prohibition [of error] in the negation of place etc. is well-known indeed.

children.translated_text: If [something] is established in place and time — it is negated as it exists;

children.text: na tathā na yathā so 'sti tathāpi na ni[10]ṣidhyate ||
children.translated_text: not as it is not; not even as it [truly] is — even so, it is not negated.

body.text: yat tu jñānasārupyāt ka.....pravṛttiriti prastutya sphurita eva pravartayanīti tatsiddhameva sādhyate | yato jñānasārūpyamanumānasiddhamiṣya (1) te | sa cāvasthātuṃaparokṣarūpājñānāntargatāpyanumānena siddhā | ahaṃkārāspadagrāhakākāraparāmarśāntargatatvāt bāhyabhūtā sphuritaśabdavācyā |
body.translated_text: As for [the claim] that 'because of the resemblance to cognition... activity [proceeds]' — having propounded this, [the conclusion is:] 'activity [is directed] toward what has manifested' — that is established, and [yet] the very thing to be proved is being proved. For the resemblance to cognition is accepted as established by inference. And that [resemblance], even though included within the cognition of the imperceptible form, is established by inference — because [it is] included within the reflective awareness of the ego-sense and the apprehending form. Being external, [it is] expressible by the word 'manifested.'

children.translated_text: If activity toward the object were from error due to resemblance, it would not [occur] always;
and error regarding location does not [apply] to cognition — equally, from the arising of cognition.
Likewise, regarding positive determination — because of non-acceptance of cognition elsewhere;
or there would be invalidity (<s>apramāṇatā</s>) of the means for the appearance of an external object.

body.text: ....vasthā svabhāvabāhyamākārā paravyapadeśatā parokṣatārūpa prakāśātmakānahaṃkārasya ca nīlabhāvādeva ca tathokta tadrūparāvṛttiviṣayābuddhi svahetorālocyate prava........................śuktau rajataśuktivad tenedamapi nirdalitam |
body.translated_text: ...the state and essential nature, the external form, the designation by another, the hiddenness, the nature of luminosity, and because of the blue-nature of the ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) — the cognition whose domain is the exclusion of that form is examined from its own cause... like silver in nacre, therefore this too is refuted.

body.text: ā. ta. vi. 162-163- ḥtarhi sphurite svākāra eva pravartayatu tatra pravṛtta eva cārthī tatsadṛśamarthamāsādayati | (maṇi)prabhāyāṃ pravṛtto maṇibaditi cet 'na, abhibhatārthakriyāsāmarthyavirahiṇyapravṛtteḥ | (4) na bāhye vikalpākāropasambhavastasya tenāsaṃsparśāt | cākāre bāhyatvāropaḥ svarūpe saṃsphurati, asvarūpāropānavakāśāt | prabhāyāṃ tu maṇi buddhayaivamaṇyarthī pravartate na tu taddhuddhayeti dṛṣṭānto 'pyābhāsaḥḥ ityāditarkatattvamabedayamānena bhaṇitam |
body.translated_text: <s>Ā</s>[<s>cārya</s>] <s>Ta</s>[<s>ttvaviniścaya</s>] <s>Vi</s>[<s>bhūṣaṇa</s>] 162-163: 'Then let it [the cognition] prompt activity toward its own form alone; and one who has acted [upon that] indeed obtains an object resembling that. Like one who, having acted upon the luster of a gem, [obtains] the gem' — if so: No, because there is no activity toward that which lacks the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>), which has been overwhelmed. There is no possibility of the conceptual construction's form [being imposed] on the external [object], because of its non-contact with that. The superimposition of externality on the [mental] form flashes forth in its own nature, because there is no occasion for superimposition of what is not its own nature. But in the case of the luster [of a gem], one acts with the cognition 'this is the gem' — but one does not act with that cognition [in the case under discussion] — therefore the example too is merely an appearance.' Thus it was stated by one who was revealing the <s>Tarkatattvam</s>.

children.translated_text: Of those who rush toward the luster of a gem and a lamp with the cognition 'this is the gem',
even though there is no difference in [both being] erroneous cognition, there is a difference with respect to causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>).
Just so, even in the case of not being in accordance with the real, regarding inference and its counterpart,
validity as a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇatva</s>) is well-established in accordance with causal efficacy.

body.text:
grāhakākāravikṣiptā nīlamevetaditi sphurat |
vikalpabāhyamevaitat..........................
body.translated_text: Projected by the apprehending form, flashing forth as 'this is blue itself,' the external [object] of conceptual construction is precisely this...

body.text: nīlānyanīlanīlagocaraḥ.......... jñānamābhāti nīlākāra utyatteścet | anumānāt tayo 'nye.....vikalpyārtho hi dharmiṇi | ḥsamvedanaṃ ca yat rūpaṃ nahi tat tasya vedanamḥ vasthita na bhavatyetat | sthitamavayavina.........(8) anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ sarvabhedamidaṃ gataḥ |
body.translated_text: Blue, non-blue, and the cognition whose domain is blue... the cognition appears with a blue form... from inference, the other two... 'the conceptually constructed object is in the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>).' 'And the self-awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) which is the form — that is indeed not the cognition of that'... this is established... through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), all this differentiation has been reached.

body.text: tasmādvāhyasiddhiśca sākāraṃ ca jñānamiti bālaloluptva miti parihāsa paritārpi paratāpitahṛdayavyaktāvyaktādyutpattijñāne nīlamajñānaṃ na kriyopalakṣitasvarūpavyava-(9)-hāratvamupāyamiti tat upādhi nīlamanahaṃkārakalitamābhāsane meyabāhyatā bhāsate jñānarūpākhyaṃ anumāne neti | prathamaprāmāṇikavacanameveti lakṣaṇairūpalakṣyate...............ṣṭā sati (10)vi heturati dviyo-
body.translated_text: Therefore, the establishment of the external [object] and the cognition having form — [to call this] mere childish fickleness is a jest. [Regarding] the manifestation of entities manifest and unmanifest: in the cognition of arising, blue is not non-cognition; the essential nature characterized by activity is not the means — that is the qualifying condition (<s>upādhi</s>); blue, not constructed by ego-sense, in manifestation, the externality of the measurable appears; the nature called 'of cognition' [appears] in inference — not [so]. This is just the statement of the first authority... characterized by marks... when there is a cause...

children.translated_text: Delighting in a thicket of lotus ponds, this is not the cause of [its] lordliness;
even today, [the elephant] is still external to the ocean of the mind of that female elephant.

body.text: bālapāvakavat grāhyā bāladruma.............
body.translated_text: To be grasped like a young fire, like a young tree...

body.text: yatpunaruktam-
body.translated_text: As for what was further stated —

body.text: ḥatha ko 'yamagaurnāma | kimekasya gosvalakṣaṇa syānātmā āhosvittadgatadharmavirahī | ādye vāhuleya eva maunaṃ śāvaleya syāt | dvitīye tu tadgata dharmavirahi vyāvṛttastadvānena syāt tatra ca no vivādaḥ ityādi kṛtopi sarvadā tadapohena............darśitaṃ syāt |
body.translated_text: 'Now, what is this [entity called] non-cow? Is it the essential nature of the defining characteristic of a single cow, or is it that which is devoid of the properties belonging to that? In the first case, the offspring of a <s>Vāhuleya</s> [cow] alone would be silent [about its being a cow], and the <s>Śāvaleya</s> [cow] would [also be excluded]. In the second case, what has turned away from [and] is devoid of the properties belonging to that — it would be [one] possessing that exclusion, and regarding that we have no dispute' — and so forth. This too would be shown by exclusion from that in every case.

children.translated_text: Because of being the cause of a single reflective awareness (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>), [it is] not splitting the steadfast;
by virtue of being the cause of a single cognition, there is non-difference of the particulars (<s>vyakti</s>) as well.
For the purpose of a single reflective awareness, in accomplishing a single object through cognition etc.,
even in difference, certain [things] are fixed by their own essential nature, like the sense faculties etc.

body.text: tasmāttvayi kurvatsarveṇeha maṇḍalamakhaṇḍasaṃtata sadā yena paśyati na bhūmiṃ asantaśca.....parimāṇavarṇākṛtyakṣarā (4) eva pravṛtte..... maṇḍalakṛtamekaparāmarśamapyapaśyan varṇākṛtyā ataddharmmavyatiriktamavabudhyata iti tathā syāt viśeṣamapi na yat na hi rupyate ekenaiva vyavahāro ityeva vyaktitve rūpamiti yadi (5)tadā sāmānyamapi nīlādyākāravācī syāt | syādekavyavahṛteḥ yato 'nyasmādekatvenānye yadyekatvena vyavahartṛ syāttarhi buddhivaikalyasajātīyavyāvṛttivirodhaḥ | kiṃ cātha vyaktivena kiṃ bhāṣakatvena (16) vyavahārayati yat yat etat anayā pratītaṃ tadeva tayaikatvenavyavahāryamiti sabalā pravuttiḥ | bahuṣu sāmānyeṣu vācitvamihā............miti satyaspaṣṭa............anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ(7) pratyayavibhāgam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, with respect to you who act, in this assembly, the unbroken, continuous circle by which one always sees — and the non-existent... the measure, color, shape, and syllables alone prompt activity... even without seeing the circle-formed single reflective awareness, one understands by color and shape what is distinct from those properties that do not belong to it — thus it would be; yet one does not discern the particular, for it is not the case that conventional usage is by one [quality] alone — if the form in manifestness [is proposed], then even the universal would denote [forms] such as blue etc.; there would be single conventional usage; because from another, by oneness, if others were to engage in usage through oneness, there would be a contradiction with the exclusion of the homogeneous (<s>sajātīya-vyāvṛtti</s>) [arising from] deficiency of intellect. Moreover — does one engage in usage by means of the particular or by means of the property of speaking? Whatever is cognized by this, that alone is to be conventionally used as one — this is the empowered activity. The capacity of speech regarding many universals... through positive and negative concomitance, the division of cognition.

children.translated_text: The unfailing activity of the intellect is always [present] in both the primary and the superimposed;
in [the case of calling] a boy a 'lion,' likewise, there is even conventional proclamation.
Where a word is assigned by people to a non-real object through conventional fixation (<s>rūḍhi</s>),
that is primary there; elsewhere, due to similarity with that, [it is] secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>), with faltering progression.
Even in [the case of] non-existence, one may apply the designation of non-existence, or [one may do so] merely through conceptual construction;
or, being incapable, people may utter [words like] '<s>pradhāna</s>' etc. according to scripture (<s>śruti</s>).
And the cognition that follows [its object], being manifested by word-particulars,
is described as <s>gotva</s> (cowness), devoid of the form of color, shape, and syllables.
If [it were] a universal (<s>jāti</s>), even one [instance] in a house would be called a 'garland,' like a tree;
when there are many garlands, how [could] that word [apply] to the universal, due to the absence of that universal?

body.text:
mālādau ca mahattvādiriṣṭo yaścaupacārikaḥ
mukhyāviśiṣṭavijñānagrāhyatvānnaupacārikaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And in the case of garlands etc., the [usage] that is desired due to magnitude etc. and is figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>) — because of being grasped by a cognition indistinguishable from the primary, it is not figurative.

children.translated_text: The [property of] having no other cause is the same — that is [accepted as] primary in your accepted [instances];
which other cause does the word '<s>padārtha</s>' (category) consider beyond the group of six?
That which is established in a certain way through conventional fixation — [and] that which is said to be so due to similarity with that —
[the former is] primary, [the latter is] secondary; and even among positive entities, [the usage for] absence is through figurative extension (<s>upacāra</s>).

body.text:
saṃketānvayinī rūḍhirvakturicchanvayī ca saḥ
kriyate vyavahārārtha chandaḥ śabdāṃśanāmavat ||
body.translated_text: Conventional fixation follows convention (<s>saṃketa</s>), and that follows the speaker's intention; it is done for the purpose of conventional usage, like metrical forms and the names of word-parts.

body.text: vikalpasaṃskāra mātrāśrayasamudbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Arising from the mere substratum of the latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of conceptual construction,

body.text:
bāhya hetvāśrayāt sākṣātsaṃbhavāddheturodhakaḥ |
sambandha bodhiśabdo vā tadvodho vāpi bodhayet |

children.translated_text: even in the absence of that, in concealment (<s>tirobhāva</s>), like a proper name, without depending [on the object];
being dependent solely on that [word] alone — one wishes to utter, out of fear;
the mere-ness of which — consciousness abides there, from observation;
this convention, [based on] beginningless, naturally-arisen capacity (<s>śakti</s>), has been refuted.

body.translated_text: because of directly arising from the external cause-substratum, [it is] an obstructor of the cause; the word [expressing] the connection of awakening, or even the awakening of that, may illuminate;

body.text:
avyava
śabdaḥ prasthāpakatve syānnārthasyāpi tu saṃvidaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The word, being a dispatcher, would not [dispatch] the object, but rather cognition.

children.translated_text: But [cognition] being 'of that' — the connection [is] superior to [mere] capacity for making known;
designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>) is not a property of another — because of being the instrument of apprehension, by people.

children.text: karaṇatve 'pi kāryālpā kriyā na dvaya niṣṭhatā |
children.translated_text: Even in being an instrument, the action producing the result is slight — there is no resting in both;
apprehension not being of that duality — the cause of that is established in that.
Let [it] not proceed — whence [would there be] non-difference? By the cognition of the opposite of that;
in the cognition of the meaning of all [words], the cognition [itself] is the opposite.
Everything would be a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), due to dependence on the established [nature] of [its] own form etc.;
hiddenness would be a <s>pramāṇa</s> — [but] the distinction lies in the difference of causes.
Or: a <s>pramāṇa</s> with respect to realities, in uttering [the word] itself, likewise;
the cessation of apprehension of the object — in a speaker who possesses autonomy.
There is no lack of autonomy when the object is the single effect produced by expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) etc.;
cognition of a single object alone is knowledge — not dependent on the senses.
Not from another — caused by that, that entity has been made a revealer;
the approach is to a substratum of an entity inferred by the capacity of connection with the real entity.
There and not elsewhere — this has been obtained by others through confusion;
even in the absence of that, what has arisen, with reference to that sentence...

body.text:
[6]mā meti śūnyakāryeti kasya hetoḥ prakalpayet |
[bauddhanyāyācāryaśrīratnakīrtipādaviracitam |
udayanirakaraṇam]
body.translated_text: 'Let it not be, let it not be' — 'devoid of effect' — for what reason would one imagine? [Thus concludes] the <s>Udayanirakāraṇam</s> (Refutation of <s>Udayana</s>), composed by the feet of the revered <s>Ratnakīrti</s>, the Buddhist master of logic (<s>Bauddha-nyāyācārya</s>).
